News.title: ‘Syrian’ man, 36, charged with murder after body found in wheelie bin near UK beauty spot
News.content:
Next

A MAN has been charged with murder after a dead body was found inside a wheelie bin.

Mohamed Abotaka, 36, is due to appear in court accused of the murder of 52-year-old Ali Barzai in Plymouth.



Mr Barzai was found partially within a wheelie bin in a service lane off Grand Parade at around 6.40am on October 21.

He was pronounced dead at the scene. Mr Barzai is believed to be of North African heritage and enquiries are ongoing to locate his next-of-kin.



Abotaka, who is believed to be from Syria, remains in police custody and is due to appear before Plymouth Magistrates’ Court on October 26.

Detective Inspector Chris Lithgow said: “A suspect is due to appear in court charged with murder and we would urge people not to speculate on this case, especially on social media, and risk prejudicing these ongoing proceedings.

“A heightened police presence will remain in the area in the coming days.

“We understand this incident has caused concern within the local community, and I would encourage any members of the public with concerns to contact us.”

Any relevant information, images or footage can be reported via the Major Incident Public Portal or by telephone on 101 and the force’s website, quoting reference 50260282293.

Information can also be passed anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers via crimestoppers-uk.org or by calling 0800 555111.

News.title: Meghan Markle’s brother begs her for forgiveness for siding with dad in public spats before finding sick hoard of images
News.content:
Next

MEGHAN Markle’s half-brother begged for her forgiveness after siding with their dad in a series of public spats — then discovering an alleged hoard of child abuse images linked to their father.

Thomas Markle Jnr mocked the Duchess of Sussex on social media and his own YouTube channel, even donning a wig and dress to impersonate her in rows amid her marriage to Prince Harry in 2018.



Thomas Jnr, who had been caring for frail Thomas Markle Snr for four years at a house in the Philippines, spoke to The Sun on Sunday after handing over four boxes of vile images to child protection cops in Cebu City.

The 60-year-old window fitter said: “I’m so, so sorry Meghan.



“I now know I have been protecting the wrong person for the past nine years.

“Having seen what I have seen, I believe the man I’ve been defending and caring for is a monster.



“I now know exactly why you don’t talk to him any more and why you won’t let him meet Harry or his grandchildren.

“And I’m ashamed that I spent years taking his side when you fell out with him.

“I know we’re not close but I can still remember holding you when you were a baby and looking after you when you were small.

“So please accept my apology and know that I wish you and your family all the best for the future.”



Thomas Jnr found the haul while 82-year-old Markle Snr was receiving medical treatment in the US.

It emerged the alleged stash of sick material included an image of Markle Snr having sex with a girl who appears underage.

Following The Sun breaking the story in a world exclusive, Meghan, 45, disclosed she had been told “troubling and disturbing” claims about her father shortly after her marriage to Harry.



And a close friend of Meghan said she was “relieved” that her father is finally being properly investigated.

Thomas Jnr became the retired Hollywood lighting director’s carer after he suffered a life-threatening stroke in 2022. They moved from their homes in Mexico to start a new life a few doors apart in Cebu City in January 2025.

But Markle Snr’s health deteriorated in December and a blood clot forced doctors to amputate his left leg below the knee.

Thomas Jnr organised his repatriation back to the US in May and moved his possessions into storage.

The shock find came as he searched for a mobile phone among innocent family mementos.



Thomas Jnr has now told police further checks of computers, cameras, phone and DVDs unearthed “hundreds, if not thousands” of child abuse pictures and videos.

He said victims no older than ten or 11 appeared in sex acts.

And he added: “It was my dad’s phone with my number and my sister’s number in the contacts list — but it was contaminated with the worst images I had ever seen. It’s the kind of thing you just can’t unsee no matter how hard you try.



“I felt unsteady when I saw it, totally horrified. Then I looked at the piles of other phones, computers and cameras and thought, ‘My God! There will be more.’

“I was terrified of being caught with it but I also found myself consumed with anger.

“So I decided there and then that I had to report my dad to the authorities and at least try to do the right thing.

“Every ounce of love or loyalty I had ever felt towards him vanished the second I saw that phone. I decided he must face the full force of the law for the sake of those poor children.”

Thomas Jnr decided to call the FBI, assuming his father was subject to US jurisdiction as he was living in Pennsylvania at the time.



But he claims his initial call to a hotline was given a cursory response, and that contacting the National Centre for Exploited and Missing Children and police in Pennsylvania saw no reply.

He decided to steel himself to check the remaining contents and retrieved the four large cardboard boxes from storage. He got a local IT technician to help him access three computer hard drives.

Thomas Jnr recalled: “I thought the phone was bad but when the computer guy sparked up the hard drive it was like he’d opened the gates of hell.

He decided to steel himself to check the remaining contents and retrieved the four large cardboard boxes from storage. He got a local IT technician to help him access three computer hard drives.

Thomas Jnr recalled: “I thought the phone was bad but when the computer guy sparked up the hard drive it was like he’d opened the gates of hell.



One seemingly innocuous seemingly antique book called “Lewis Carroll Photographs Of Children: Four Nude Studies” hid more sordid secrets.

Thomas Jnr said: “The book had a plain cover and a few very old images of naked girls inside but as I opened the pages, strips of 35mm film negatives fell out.

“My dad was a lighting director and an expert photographer who could process his own film, but I can’t be sure who took the pictures.



“However I could see at least one image involving a bearded man raping a very young Asian girl. Another developed film negative showed two naked schoolgirls.”

Further analysis of one of the hard drives revealed a downloaded PDF file which opened to reveal Thomas Markle Snr’s professional CV.

It listed his old Hollywood address and phone numbers together with his “Executive Profile, Skill Highlights and Professional Experience.”

Another column of the CV listed his “Core Accomplishments” including three Emmy Awards won for lighting excellence.

Along with the child sex images and his resume was another download — of daughter Meghan addressing a women’s event at the United Nations.



The same hard drive also included a Facebook login page for a 619 San Diego coded phone number registered to Markle Snr.

Thomas Jnr said: “I can honestly say I have not been the same person since the day I found this stuff.

“But I have no worries whatsoever about handing it over to the police.”



He also recalled that, growing up in a variety of homes, every one had a locked room which was out of bounds to everyone except his father. He said: “They were no-go rooms and were usually secured with a padlock.

“He had homes in Chicago, Hollywood and Mexico and it was the same everywhere we lived. We thought having a dad room like that was normal.

“If he left the door unlocked while he was in there at his computer he would go absolutely crazy then not speak to us for three days.

“Now I know why he wanted to be alone — and it sickens me to my stomach.”

Thomas Jnr said he had “done all his crying” and has no intention of ever speaking to the father he once doted on ever again.



He told The Sun: “He’s not a well man, he’s 82, he lost a leg and he’s living in a medical facility so he may not live much longer.

“But as far as I’m concerned he’s already dead to me and I won’t be doing any mourning.

“I won’t be giving a eulogy like sons often do and I won’t even go to his funeral — but I’d be happy to turn on the cremation oven.”

Cebu City-based investigators from the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking yesterday launched a probe run by the specialist Women and Children’s Protection Centre.

And agents from America’s FBI have confirmed receipt of the contents of Thomas Jnr’s five-page affidavit of what was in the boxes. They look certain to conduct their own probe.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Thomas Snr is in a nursing and rehabilitation centre in Florida where he is being supported by his daughter Samantha, 60. He has denied the claims against him.

Officers from the specialist Women and Children’s Protection Centre Task Force declined to comment.

News.title: Dad, 33, attacked officer at ‘murdered’ teen’s funeral as cop reveals she was left ‘vulnerable & exposed’ by assault
News.content:
‘COWARDLY ACT' Dad, 33, attacked officer at ‘murdered’ teen’s funeral as cop reveals she was left ‘vulnerable & exposed’ by assault







Next

A DAD has pleaded guilty after attacking a female cop during the funeral of a teen boy who was allegedly murdered.

Jordan Rice, 33, threw a missile at Sergeant Sarah Breakspear which left her feeling like she had “been glassed”, a court has heard.



Sarah said the assault left her feeling “vulnerable and exposed”.

Rice was one of dozens of mourners to attend the wake of 16-year-old Ta-Shay Canoville.



But the remembrance event at Ringland Labour Club in Newport turned volatile towards police who were in attendance.

Prosecutor James Evans, said: “Events were emotionally charged and a large number of people present were hostile to the police.



“People had been drinking for a considerable amount of time and some were intoxicated.

“A noisy fireworks display added to the tension, although that’s not to say it was done deliberately.”



Cardiff Crown Court heard Sergeant Breakspear and colleagues from a support unit arrived at around 10.30pm in June to be met with “insults and threats”.

She was then struck in the face by a thrown object with such force that it knocked her sideways and caused her “immense pain”.

The officer described it feeling as if she had been “glassed” and she was taken away from the scene by colleagues after she experienced blurred vision.

In a victim impact statement, Sergeant Breakspear explained that she had been a police officer for 19 years and loved her job.

She said: “I have never felt as vulnerable and exposed as I did on the night of June 26.



“I felt my legs buckle and I honestly thought I had been glassed.”

She added: “I feel it was a deliberate act.

“He used the anonymity of the crowd to commit a violent and cowardly act.”

The officer suffered bruising and swelling to her face.

Rice was identified from footage of the incident and claimed he threw a plastic cup and not glass.



Rice, of Newport, pleaded guilty to affray and assault by beating of an emergency worker.

Harriet Ealdon, defending, said the father-of-one was a children’s football coach and in full-time work.

She said: “It was an emotionally charged day and this was an act of recklessness.

“The defendant has expressed his remorse and he wants to apologise to the officer for the injury he caused.”

Judge Vanessa Francis told Rice he “should have known better”.



He was jailed for 10 months with the sentence suspended for 12 months and ordered to carry out 80 hours of unpaid work as well as pay Sergeant Breakspear £500 compensation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ta-Shay and his friend Jaydon Bowyer, 19, died after a motorbike crash on Aberthaw Road in the Alway area of Newport on Thursday, May 7.

Two men have been charged with their murder.

News.title: I joined the Labour Party – NOT the Benefits Party… the Chancellor must make work pay in this Budget
News.content:
Next

IN August I wrote in The Sun on Sunday that Britain needed to stop relying on endless government bailouts and start getting people back to work.

Ahead of the Budget, I want to go further.



I joined the Labour Party, not the Benefits Party.

I said that in the House of Lords earlier this year and I stand by every word.



Because I believe work gives people dignity, independence and a stake in society.

And Labour should be the party that helps people get on in life, not leaves them dependent on the state.



But look at where Britain is today.

One in seven households has nobody in work and around 1.3 million children are growing up in long-term workless households.

A quarter of a million live in homes where nobody has ever worked.

Think about that. Children growing up without ever seeing a parent go out to earn a living.



That should shock us all.

My mum and dad were both children of coalminers. They came from nothing, worked incredibly hard and, after a few failed attempts, founded Iceland in 1970.

That business has created tens of thousands of jobs, paid billions in tax and supported communities across Britain.

I started on the shop floor and today I’m proud to lead a business employing more than 30,000 people.



When I visit our stores, often in towns other retailers have abandoned, I hear the same thing again and again: Britain should be doing better.

They’re right.

That’s why I’ve published a new paper for think tank, Progress, setting out what I believe the Chancellor needs to do in the Budget.

And my message is simple. Make work pay, make hiring easier and give businesses the confidence to invest.

Start with welfare.



Of course, we must protect people who genuinely cannot work. That’s what a decent society does.

But leaving people languishing on benefits when they could be working isn’t compassion. It’s letting them down.

We need more carrot and, yes, sometimes more stick.

I’d introduce a meaningful cash reward for people who move from long-term benefits into a job and stay there. And reward employers prepared to give them a chance.

At Iceland, we’ve seen the benefits of giving former prisoners a second chance through our recruitment programme. It’s good for our business and good for society.



We need more of that thinking.

But government says it wants more jobs while making them more expensive to create.

Employers now pay 15 per cent National Insurance on earnings above just £5,000.

If we want businesses to take a chance on young people, why not make it cheaper? I’d extend employer National Insurance relief to under-25s.

And why have we created a tax system where some working parents face an effective marginal rate of around 54 per cent when their earnings rise?



What sort of incentive is that to work harder and get ahead?

Meanwhile, Britain is spending around £110 billion a year just paying interest on government debt.

That’s roughly £3,190 for every person in work.

Just imagine what we could do with that money.

Better hospitals, schools, roads and opportunities for young people.



Instead, we’re paying for yesterday’s borrowing.

That’s why Labour needs to be brave about public spending, including reforming the pension triple lock from 2030.

We need to protect pensioners, but we also have to be fair to younger generations who will be left picking up the bill.

And we cannot keep taxing our way out of trouble.

Britain has extraordinary businesses, universities and talent. Yet our economy is barely growing, even with the IMF forecasting our growth up to 1.3 per cent.



So let’s reward companies that invest in new equipment, technology, training and jobs with aggressive tax breaks.

I’d go further and cut corporation tax for smaller businesses and entrepreneurs who are investing in growth, while asking bigger companies that aren’t reinvesting their profits to pay more.

Why should a growing business trying to create jobs face a tax system designed around the same principles as a multinational making billions?

Let’s simplify the tax system rather than make businesses spend more time dealing with accountants than customers.

And let’s give employers a proper five-year plan so they can invest without constantly second-guessing Westminster.



Artificial intelligence is already changing the world of work. At Iceland we’re training colleagues in AI because we know businesses cannot afford to wait for government to catch up.

We need to prepare people for tomorrow’s jobs, not just protect yesterday’s.

I support this government and want it to succeed.

The Prime Minister and Chancellor deserve credit for recognising that growth and youth employment matter.

But good intentions aren’t enough.



I’ve seen inside government how painfully slow decisions can be. In business, you simply cannot operate like that.

And ultimately, you cannot have better public services without businesses creating jobs, paying wages and generating the taxes that fund them.

Being pro-business and pro-worker aren’t opposing positions,Labour should be proud to champion both.

Because the best way to tackle poverty is to give people on benefits the chance to build a better life through work.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

For me, the test of this Budget should be simple. ‘Does it make Britain a better place to work, to hire and to invest’?



If it doesn’t, we’re missing the point. Over to you, Chancellor.

News.title: Two teens arrested after man attacked with knife inside busy shopping centre as cops ramp up patrols across city
News.content:
SLASH ATTACK Two teens arrested after man attacked with knife inside busy shopping centre as cops ramp up patrols across city







Next

TWO teens have been arrested after a man was attacked with a knife at a popular shopping mall.

A group of teens were allegedly seen lunging at one another before security guards were forced to intervene.



The fight broke out in Arndale Centre in Manchester earlier today.

In footage circulating online, security could be seen kicking away a knife from the group of yobs.

The weapon is then protected under a guard’s feet while waiting for police to arrive.



The injured man is believed to be suffering from “a wound on”minor” injuries to his arm.

Two teens, 18 and 19, have been arrested on suspicion of affray and possession of a bladed article.

In a statement, Greater Manchester Police said: “Officers were called to reports of an assault at the Arndale Centre at 12.50pm today (Saturday 24 October 2026).

“A man suffered minor injuries. Two men – aged 18 and 19 – were arrested on suspicion of affray and possession of a bladed article. They are in police custody.

“This is an isolated incident with no wider threat to the public. However people can expect to see extra patrols in place across the city centre this weekend.”

This comes a week after a 14-year-old boy was stabbed in the same mall.



The injured teen is believed to be in a stable condition in hospital, with the suspects currently on bail.

Police have stressed the two attacks are not related.

News.title: Robert Jenrick to announce £40 billion of spending cuts in Reform’s alternative Budget
News.content:
Robert Jenrick will unveil his alternative Budget setting out Reform's tax and spend plans

'BRITAIN IS BROKE' Robert Jenrick to announce £40 billion of spending cuts in Reform’s alternative Budget







Next

REFORM UK will tomorrow unveil plans for £40 billion worth of spending cuts in their alternative Budget.

Nigel Farage’s party wants to use the cash to pay for £1,300 in tax cuts to Brits clobbered by the cost of living crisis.



Reform’s Treasury chief Robert Jenrick will announce the plans in front of a giant banner warning – Britain Is Broke.

Mr Jenrick told The Sun on Sunday: “We can’t go on like this. Britain is broke.



“It’s time for emergency spending cuts to government waste so we can give working people tax cuts.

The party would cut £20bn from the welfare budget, £8bn from Net Zero subsidies and £6bn from foreign aid.



They will also cut £2bn from QUANGOs and the civil service, £3bn from student loans to dead-end degrees and foreigners, and raise £1bn from the immigration health surcharge.

The cash would be used to bankroll tax cuts.

This would include raising the tax-free personal allowance to £15,0000 – a move the party says will leave the average household £1,000 better off and lift 3 million out of paying income tax altogether.

Reform would also use the spare cash to take off £250 of people’s energy bills and save households £50 by scrapping the forecasted fuel duty rise.



The plan will be launched tomorrow – two days before Chancellor John Healey gets to his feet to announce his first Budget.

News.title: Woman, 31, charged with incest after sexually abusing child ‘younger than 12’ – as she is facing life in prison
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TWISTED ACT Woman, 31, charged with incest after sexually abusing child ‘younger than 12’ – as she is facing life in prison







Next

A WOMAN has been accused of incest and sodomy after allegedly sexually abusing a child younger than 12, according to court documents.

Lauren Winans, 31, was arrested this week on three charges and faces life in prison for the alleged abuse.

The Kentucky woman allegedly had sex with a person “whom she knew to be an ancestor who was less than 12 years of age” according to an indictment.

The alleged abuse took place between January and November 2022.





Winans, from Bardstown, allegedly abused and sodomized the child at some point between January 1, 2022 and November 20, 2022.

It is unclear what relation Winans had to the child.

The alleged victim is referred to as C.G.W in the court documents.

Winans was described as having “strawberry blonde hair” and “green eyes” in her arrest warrant.

It says her bond has been set at nearly £200,000.

Local reports say a man believed to be Winans’ husband worked as a police officer.

A statement from the Nelson County Sheriff’s Office said Andy Winans resigned from his role in early 2026.

Cops said: “The Kentucky State Police (KSP) is the primary investigating agency regarding the allegations involving Lauren Winans.



“The Nelson County Sheriff’s Office was not aware of these allegations, holds no details regarding the case, and is not involved in the investigation. Inquiries should be directed to KSP.

“Andy Winans is no longer employed by the Nelson County Sheriff’s Office.

“He resigned from our agency and joined the Bardstown Police Department in early 2026.

“Our office remains fully committed to accountability, transparency, and upholding the trust of the Nelson County community.”

There is no suggestion that anyone else, including Andy Winans, is involved in any of the alleged abuse.



Winans faces up to life behind bars if found guilty of her alleged crimes, the New York Post reported.

According to court records, she will be arraigned inside Nelson Circuit Court on November 5.

News.title: Urgent manhunt after prisoner escapes medical facility in London as public issued warning
News.content:
'DO NOT APPROACH' Urgent manhunt after prisoner escapes medical facility in London as public issued warning







Next

COPS have launched an urgent manhunt after a prisoner escaped from a medical facility, as the public have been warned not to approach him.

Anthony Lloyd, 38, was last seen forcing his way out of the unit in Lewisham, South London, at around 4.10pm on October 23.



He was spotted heading in the direction of Catford.

Lloyd is white, around 5ft 8, of medium build with short dark hair, and was wearing a grey/blue t-shirt, black tracksuit bottoms and white trainers.



Detective Superintendent Melanie Pressley, who is leading the manhunt, said: “We are conducting various significant enquiries to find Lloyd and return him to custody.

“We are concerned he poses a risk both to himself and the public and would urge anyone who sees him to call 999 immediately.

“Do not approach him.”

“If you have any information – however small – that could help us locate Lloyd, please get in touch with police as a matter of urgency.”

Police believe Lloyd could be anywhere in London, and he also has links to Surrey, Sussex, Thames Valley, Hampshire, Nottinghamshire, Derbyshire and Merseyside.

Anyone with information is asked to call 999 quoting CAD4739/23Oct.

News.title: France protests live: Demonstrator reportedly loses fingers in violent clashes
News.content:
The Louvre, the Orsay and Picasso museums are closed, with a partial night curfew also in place across different parts of Paris

A demonstrator has reportedly lost fingers in violent clashes with police as protests continue across France following a weekend of significant disorder that ravaged the country.

Around 70,000 officers have been deployed across France to prevent a repeat of last weekend's unrest. So far, today's protests appear less severe, with around 35,000 demonstrators compared with 60,000 at the same time last week.

More than 2,700 arrests were made following last week's looting, with curfews now imposed across Paris. The widespread disorder was sparked by anger over the cost of living crisis and poor school conditions.

Scenes of looting, burned-out cars and attacks on public buildings stunned the world as masked groups targeted businesses in Paris and other city centres. Helicopters, armoured vehicles and water cannons have also been deployed alongside the 70,000 officers.

A partial night curfew covering parts of Paris, including the historic Place de la République, remains in place until Monday. The Culture Ministry has also announced the closure of the Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums, as well as the Grand Palais.

News.title: Chancellor to unveil £1billion boost to build up to 10,000 new council homes in Budget
News.content:
Chancellor to unveil £1billion boost to build up to 10,000 new council homes in Budget

EXCLUSIVE: The Chancellor is set to announce more than £1billion of new funding for social and affordable housing, taking the total capital investment to more than £40 billion over the next 10 years

View 2 Images The Chancellor is set to announce more than £1billion of new funding for social and affordable housing (Image: David Hartley/Shutterstock)

Britain is set for a £1billion boost to council housing which can deliver up to 10,000 homes in the Budget.

‌



‌



The announcement next week by Chancellor John Healey will take the total capital ­investment in the Social and Affordable Homes Programme to more than £40bn over the next 10 years. The government also plans to help more councils borrow for ­housebuilding by extending ­preferential rates.

‌



A Treasury spokesman said: “For years families have been locked out of a secure and affordable home because we simply haven’t built enough. The Prime Minister promised to restore the public housing stock.

‌



To see more of the stories you value from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Northern England Olympics bid backed with £7million in Budget READ MORE :

View 2 Images The PM had promised a council house building 'revolution' (Image: Michael Bowles/Shutterstock)

“This Budget will go further on that ambition through significant ­investment in affordable housing and helping councils borrow to build so we can replace what has been sold and give people a place to live.”

‌



Since the 1980s, more than two million council homes have been sold through Right to Buy. But after ­successive governments failed to replace them, millions of people have been left struggling to find a first home.

More than 1.3 million households are on social housing waiting lists in England, and only 12,250 social rent homes were delivered in 2024/25. A record 177,500 children are living in ­temporary accommodation – up 5% in a year.

‌



And earlier this year, the boss of Britain’s largest housebuilder, Barratt Redrow, said it is the toughest time for first-time buyers since the 2008 financial crisis. The average monthly private rent rose by 3.8% in the 12 months to September. House prices rose by 0.9%, to £273,000, having gone up 1.2% the year before, figures out this week show.

PM Andy Burnham has ­promised the largest post-war council and social housebuilding programme, including the exemption of new builds from Right to Buy for 35 years. It forms part of a strategy to transform housing, with Housing Secretary Angela Rayner telling the Labour conference last month that the government would cap “outrageous” fees for leaseholders and regulate managing agents behaving like “cowboys, crooks and con artists”.

‌



It was also announced councils will be able to take back empty homes after six months. Mairi MacRae, acting chief executive at housing charity Shelter, said: “As we head into winter, record numbers of children are stuck in homelessness in grotty temporary accommodation, while countless more families struggle to cope with soaring housing costs.

"With rents tied to local incomes, social rent homes are the only genuinely ­affordable option for many families, but over the last few decades, supply has plummeted. This funding injection is another important step in the right direction, but to deliver the council house building revolution it promised, the government must go further.

Article continues below

"The autumn Budget is the Prime Minister’s chance to remove unsustainable housing debt from council balance sheets and truly ­turbocharge the delivery of social rent homes.”

News.title: French student's bleak warning as protesters march through Paris: 'We don't have a future'
News.content:
Holding a French flag, Matteo tells how young people in his country do not have a future. The student’s bleak verdict came as he was among thousands of demonstrators who marched through Paris.

After the country was rocked by its worst civil unrest in years, crowds took to the street on Saturday amid cost-of-living and school funding concerns. What started as a protest over staff shortages at a high school has sparked a national movement.

The Mirror joined a throng of protesters marching through the capital, with the crowd stretching as far as the eye could see.

To see more of the stories you value from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 9 Images Student Matteo told how young people in his country do not have a future (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

France protests live: Demonstrator reportedly loses fingers in violent clashes READ MORE :

France orders curfews amid violent riots across country as Emmanuel Macron begs for calm READ MORE :

“What we saw in the past two or three weeks is [Emmanuel] Macron, our President, is not understanding what we are protesting for,” Matteo said. “We can show all of the world through a strong movement that we are all together.”

France is not alone in its societal problems; many in Britain would no doubt share discontent over the cost of living. Indeed, Matteo points to other nations too. The political science student, in his 20s, explained: “I think we don’t have future and that’s clearly difficult.”

He added: “We don’t have future because of AI, we don’t have future because of ecology, we don’t have futures because our government doesn’t want to just let us have some good condition in our university.” On the lack of a future for French young people, he said: “That’s why there are a lot of people on the street. They are protesting.”

‌



9 View 9 Images Tech start-up worker Agathe, 33, with her sign in Paris on Saturday (Image: Humphrey Nemar) 9 View 9 Images Student Soline Malacarne said: 'Students are mobilised for bad studying conditions.' (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

Authorities confined the Paris march to the capital’s southeastern edge, away from the centre. Thousands of protesters marched from Porte d'Italie on Saturday afternoon. Trade unions led the procession, followed by protesters carrying flags and placards.

Agathe, 33, held a handmade sign saying “you’ve been served revolution”. The tech start-up worker told the Mirror: “We are protesting against government politics from years because it’s unfair. We are not listened [to]. And we when we try to manifest they try to forbid us to do it. So it’s a fundamental right and we are here for this to claim we have the right to not agree.”

‌



View 9 Images French authorities used water cannons and tear gas to disperse those protesting (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

She explained: “When you don’t listen [to] the people’s voice for years, you cannot ask people not to manifest and not to protest.” Agathe added: “I’m here for democracy, for liberty, I’m here for equality for everyone, for the less privileged and for equity.”

The Paris march began peacefully but near its endpoint at Porte de Vincennes, some protesters threw projectiles while police fired volleys of tear gas and used water cannons to disperse people. The Interior Ministry put nationwide turnout at 410,000, while the CGT union estimated nearly 800,000. The ministry's estimate included 110,000 in Paris.

View 9 Images Friends Mel and Leo in Paris on Saturday (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

‌



Earlier, we spoke to protesters gathered at Place d’Italie in Paris on Saturday afternoon. Art student Mel, 19, carried a banner reading “you are more shocked by ink on the wall than blood on the floor”. It is a reference to how she feels the protesting has been conveyed.

She told the Mirror: “I’m here because the state of France lately is so bad.” In reference to the government, police and far right, she explained: “I’m here today but I’m scared because they’re getting more violent every day.”

The teenager added: “It’s really terrifying to see my country like that. I’m proud to be French and the far right is trying to make it seem like people who are manifesting are not… But we don’t hate France, we do this because we love our country, we are proud of who we are.

“And, today, that’s why we’re here because I’m proud of who I am and I don’t want to leave my country in a way that I’ll be ashamed in the future.” She said the cost of living was “getting bad”, explaining: “Personally, I’m part of the lucky ones because I live with my family but I know friends who struggle every month to pay rent.”

‌



View 9 Images Students demanding better schools and workers seeking higher wages and pensions have brought anger over living standards into the final months of President Macron's presidency (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

Her friend, engineering student Leo, 18, said: “I think it’s really important to show that we are still going to protest, we are still going to go on the streets.” The teenager added: “I think it’s important that we can protest. It’s one of our rights.”

Meanwhile, Soline Malacarne said: “Students are mobilised for bad studying conditions.” The 23-year-old student, who also referenced the high cost of living, said direct democracy was “the best way to get heard”. She added: “I hope they will listen to the people.”

Elsewhere, police used tear gas in Lyon, where the rally had been banned, on Saturday morning. And in Clermont-Ferrand, officers reportedly used tear gas and stun grenades to push back demonstrators trying to reach the city centre. Authorities sought to prevent another weekend of looting, burned cars and attacks on public buildings. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said up to 70,000 officers would be deployed nationwide, backed by helicopters, armoured vehicles and water cannons.

‌



View 9 Images Students took over the streets with placards (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

Thousands also marched on Saturday in Orleans, south of Paris, in a separate peaceful protest against the far right as Marine Le Pen's National Rally held a two-day congress in the city. Students demanding better schools and workers seeking higher wages and pensions have brought anger over living standards into the final months of President Macron 's presidency.

Energy prices in France were 21.3% higher in September than a year earlier, helping drive overall inflation to 3.1%, according to the national statistics agency, INSEE. Mr Macron met high school representatives Friday. They said he had promised to overhaul university admissions, but called for protests to continue until concrete measures are announced.

Over half a million people took to the streets last Saturday. Some 3,000 shops across France were damaged or looted over the weekend. Gendarmes stood guard beneath the Arc de Triomphe as shops boarded up across Paris. Major museums, including the Louvre, Orsay Museum, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais were closed. Police changed the Paris route, replacing the planned Bastille-to-Nation march with a route between Porte d'Italie and Porte de Vincennes.

‌



View 9 Images Colleagues Lucile Toulgoat, left, and Rachel Basque (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

At Bastille, the original starting point, police used a megaphone to tell people to leave or face a 135-euro fine. We spoke to two protesters at Place de la Bastille who ended up being fined. Earlier, they had explained why they were there.

Rachel Basque normally sells fruit and veg but on Saturday she turned up for democracy. The 30-year-old, who was due at work later that day, said: “It’s our right and we shouldn’t have to be afraid to protest.” She added: “We are just fed up… we have to be here to support the kids and support ourselves.”

Her colleague Lucile Toulgoat, 25, added: “I’m tired of this police. I’m tired of the army coming.” Lucile said she felt “terrible” about the cost of living.

‌



For Matteo, the voice of young people is powerful. He said: “Gen Z is really strong at the moment to show the protest and to show that they want a better future.”

But whether they get it, sadly, remains to be seen.

News.title: UK weather live: 28 areas on flood alert as Storm Boelo set to bring 80mph winds
News.content:
The Met Office has issued 'danger to life' amber weather warnings for Storm Boelo, which arrives just after Storm Austen caused serious damage in the South West

Storm Boelo is set to bring 80mph winds and 'widespread travel disruption' to the UK this weekend, with forecasters warning of potential flooding, power cuts and problems on the roads.

One amber warning for wind, two yellow warnings for wind and a yellow warning for rain will cover different areas across the UK this weekend.

It comes after Storm Austen led to airports being closed, flights cancelled and even Brighton's iconic West Pier partially collapsing.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned on Friday that the UK could face “a winter of greater flooding” and said we are living in a world where “unexpected events” are “more and more common”.

An amber weather warning is in place across Scotland today, along with the north of England down to Carlisle and the north-east of Northern Ireland.

It comes just a day after Storm Austen battered the South West of England, with schools closed and 31,000 homes at one point left without power yesterday.

Tom Morgan, a Met Office meteorologist, said: “Yesterday’s Storm Austen affected the far south of the UK and northern France and the Channel Islands, whereas today’s Storm Boelo will be affecting the north of the UK."

News.title: Storm Boelo batters Brits with 80mph winds and rain causing travel chaos amid weather warnings
News.content:
Storm Boelo batters Brits with 80mph winds and rain causing travel chaos amid weather warnings

Amber warnings cover parts of Scotland, Northern England and Northern Ireland as Storm Boelo approaches its strongest phase with forecasters warning of damaging gusts, power cuts and travel disruption

View 4 Images The Met Office warned that further power cuts could affect mobile phone coverage (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Britain’s scorching summer feels a distant memory as Storm Boelo sweeps in, bringing the threat of 80mph winds.

‌



‌



Families face another weekend of travel disruption and possible power cuts as the second named storm of the season follows closely behind Storm Austen. The strongest winds are expected across northern parts of the UK, with forecasters warning of danger from flying debris and large waves.

‌



Amber wind warnings cover much of Scotland and parts of northern England from 9pm on Saturday until 9pm on Sunday. A separate amber warning covers parts of County Antrim and County Londonderry in Northern Ireland from 9pm on Saturday until 10am on Sunday.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Heavy rain brings the risk of flooding (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Manhunt launched for prisoner who escaped south London medical facility READ MORE :

Gusts of 60–70mph are expected widely within the amber warning areas, potentially reaching 80mph in exposed coastal locations. The Met Office warned that buildings could be damaged, trees brought down and roads and bridges closed. Power cuts could also affect mobile phone coverage.

‌



The warnings come as communities recover from Storm Austen, which battered southern areas on Friday. At one stage, 31,000 properties in the South West were without electricity, while strong winds and waves also caused part of Brighton’s historic West Pier to collapse.

Amy Webb, chief operating officer at National Grid Electricity Distribution, said: “We have teams on the ground assessing damage, making repairs and restoring supplies, and we’ll keep going until everyone is reconnected. We’ve had fantastic support from the communities where our teams are working. We’re very grateful for that patience and understanding while our engineers continue the job of getting everybody back on supply.”

‌



View 4 Images Brighter spells and mostly dry weather are forecast for Wednesday (Image: Getty Images)

In London, the weather has forced the cancellation of Sunday’s Diwali on the Square celebrations in Trafalgar Square. Organisers said conditions forecast for Saturday made it unsafe to carry out the preparations needed to stage the event.

‌



For those planning to travel, rail operators have urged passengers to reconsider some journeys. Avanti West Coast advised against travelling north of Preston on Sunday, while TransPennine Express said passengers should travel only if essential this weekend. LNER also advised against journeys between Edinburgh and Aberdeen on Sunday.

National Rail warned that fallen trees, damaged overhead wires and flooding could interrupt services, with speed restrictions adding to journey times while ScotRail asked people living near railway lines to secure outdoor belongings before the strongest winds arrive. The operator said in a post on X: “We’re asking anyone with garden items such as tents, trampolines or furniture, to secure them ahead of the arrival of #StormBoelo so that they don’t blow onto the tracks and interfere with lineside equipment or block the railway.”

‌



View 4 Images Parts of Brighton's historic West Pier collapse during Friday's Storm Austen (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Drivers were also warned to take extra care during the storm. RAC mobile mechanic of the year Jack Halstead said: “Very strong winds and heavy rain mean it’s vital to slow down and leave a far greater gap behind the vehicle in front. Where possible, drivers should avoid coastal and exposed upland routes when storms like these roll in.”

‌



Rain warnings add to the difficulties, covering Wales and parts of England until 11pm on Saturday. Another warning for parts of Scotland runs from 9pm on Saturday until 3pm on Sunday, with flooding and further travel disruption possible. But the impact varies across the country. Rain should clear much of England and Wales on Saturday evening, followed by clearer spells and scattered showers.

London and the South East face a wet and windy Saturday evening before clearer spells develop overnight. Sunday should bring sunshine for most, although conditions will remain windy. Further rain is expected on Monday and Tuesday before a more settled Wednesday. Sunday should be drier and brighter for most, although blustery showers remain possible in the north and west.

Article continues below

Scotland and Northern Ireland will continue to see showers or longer spells of rain, with winds easing only gradually. The unsettled spell is expected to continue into next week. A yellow wind warning is already in place for Tuesday across Scotland and parts of Northern Ireland and northern England, with uncertainty remaining over the strongest gusts. By Wednesday, the Met Office expects brighter spells and mostly dry weather, although some western areas could still see showers.

News.title: Terrifying moment Cheltenham staff member crawls across track as horses thunder towards him
News.content:
Terrifying moment Cheltenham staff member crawls across track as horses thunder towards him

The unusual incident was picked up on the TV footage in the opening race of seven at Cheltenham on Saturday, the William Hill Epic Boosts Novices' Limited Handicap Chase over 2m 4f

View Image The man could be seen on his hands and knees in the Racing TV footage (Image: Racing TV)

Eagle-eyed TV viewers spotted a man crawling across the course at Cheltenham as horses thundered towards him.

‌



‌



The individual was seen in the left-hand corner of the Racing TV footage while the runners were galloping towards the final fence in the William Hill Epic Boosts Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (1.10pm).

‌



Spectacularsunrise held a two-length lead at the time and came down, as another fancied runner Lisbane Park fell independently.

‌



Irish raider Rockonliam was left in the lead but began to idle and was reeled in by Sean Bowen's mount O'Moore Park (25-1), a transfer from Willie Mullins' yard to Martin Keighley's.

However, on a wet and windy afternoon at Prestbury Park, some fans of the sport were left wondering why the man was on the ground in the closing stages of the 2m 4f contest which started the card.

Dan Skelton reveals clue which led him to bargain Cheltenham winner Here Comes Georgie READ MORE :

"Why we got some fella at Cheltenham on his hands and knees scrambling to avoid horse 2 out. What on earth is going on!" one person wrote on social media site X.

‌



And another asked: "Was there somebody crawling along the floor as the horses turned in at Cheltenham?"

A stewards enquiry was held and it was found that they were a member of staff who had slipped while heading across the course.

‌



The report published on the British Horseracing Authority website read: "An enquiry was held to consider the circumstances surrounding why a member of the veterinary team appeared to be attempting to get up off the floor between the final two fences as the field passed.

"The clerk of the course was interviewed and reported that the staff member had lost their footing while crossing the track, as was their routine. He continued that as it was on the outside of the racing line and they did not have time to move, the individual made the decision to remain on the floor until the field had passed.

‌



"After hearing the evidence, a report was forwarded to the Head Office of the British Horseracing Authority for further consideration."

Cheltenham's two-day meeting marked the return of jumps racing there for seven months, after the final fixtures of the 2025-6 season were cancelled to allow a significant drainage project to be carried out.

Article continues below

It was undertaken on the back of the discovery of a hole in the racing surface on Festival Trials Day in late January.

News.title: CCTV caught moment two men shoot each other outside Birmingham nightclub
News.content:
CCTV caught moment two men shoot each other outside Birmingham nightclub

Aaron Nubie, 47, and Kimani Durrell-Smith, 28, pulled out guns and began shooting by FJ Lounge, in Aston, Birmigham, with an innocent food seller Garth Pantry also hit

Moment two men shoot each other at Birmingham nightclub

The moment two men opened fire on each other outside a nightclub after a row about 'disrespect' was caught on CCTV.

‌



‌



Aaron Nubie, 47, and Kimani Durrell-Smith, 28, pulled out guns and began shooting by FJ Lounge, in Aston, Birmingham, on March 23 last year.

‌



They were both struck as was Garth Pantry, an innocent food seller at the venue, who was caught up in the firing. He said in a victim impact statement how he had been left traumatised with difficulty sleeping as well as not being able to work.

‌



The chaos unfolded when Nubie returned to the venue with intent to "put right the disrespect" he believed he had been subjected to, Judge Andrew Smith KC said in court.

View 3 Images Kimani Durrell-Smith opened fire outside a food stall (Image: West Midlands Police)

Durrell-Smith, from Erdington, went to buy food outside the club and Nubie approached him with a gun before the violence erupted.

‌



Judge Smith said it was not "significantly premeditated" but neither was it spontaneous. Durrell-Smith pulled out his gun when he saw Nubie and both men opened fire within a fraction of a second of each other.

One of the bullets passed through Durrell-Smith's shoulder and hit in the shoulder Mr Pantry who was rushed to hospital where he underwent surgery for a partial collapse to his lungs.

‌



Nubie also required treatment having been shot in the neck and hand while Durrell-Smith did not attend the hospital despite the gunshot wound to his own shoulder.

View 3 Images Aaron Nubie has been jailed (Image: West Midlands Police)

‌



Representing himself in court, Nubie said: "It was a form of self-defence. I felt like I had a right to do it because my life was at stake at the situation." He said he had known Mr Pantry for many years and insisted he meant no harm to him.

Nubie, from Stockland Green, said he had experienced gang culture and organised crime in the past which had left him with post traumatic stress disorder and fearing he would lose his life to gun crime.

‌



The two defendants were both found guilty of two offences of wounding with intent while each admitted possessing a prohibited firearm, reported BirminghamLive.

View 3 Images (Image: West Midlands Police)

‌



They were handed extended sentences of 15 years in custody with extended three-year licence periods at Birmingham Crow Court on October 22.

Judge Andrew Smith KC said: "You didn't know one another but you had something in common. Each of you, as you accept, were in possession of a loaded 9mm handgun.

Article continues below

"Each of you carried your firearm in a readily accessible way and, as events were to unfold, did not hesitate to use your lethal, illegal weapons."

A West Midlands Police spokesperson added: "We responded immediately, launched a major investigation, caught them, and they’re now starting prison sentences. We’re working relentlessly every day to tackle violent crime and take guns off the streets of the West Midlands."

News.title: Greggs has major update for customers as new menu item 'biggest ever'
News.content:
Greggs has major update for customers as new menu item 'biggest ever'

It brought the launch forward by two weeks

View 3 Images It seems to have gone down a treat (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Greggs has given an update to customers today as it confirmed some record-breaking news.

‌



‌



It said that its much-loved Festive Bake had achieved its all-time single-day sales record, on the very first day it was available this year. Launched nationwide on Thursday, it returned on the earliest date in its 17-year history and fans wasted no time getting into the festive spirit, snapping up more Festive Bakes in a single day than on any other day since it first launched, Greggs said.

‌



Greggs brought the launch forward by two weeks, believing "Brits were ready to get their Christmas food fix earlier than ever" and, judging by the record-breaking opening, it seems it was right. Greggs said it now believed the strong start put it on course to sell more Festive Bakes than ever before.

‌



View 3 Images The Greggs Festive Bake

Zoe Harris, customer director at Greggs, said: “We know the Festive Bake has a huge following, but this launch has been something else. We brought it back two weeks earlier than ever before because we know people are ready to start feeling festive sooner and in just 24 hours, they proved us right.

‌



“To see the biggest day of Festive Bake sales ever is incredible. This record-breaking start means it could be our biggest Festive Bake season yet. Christmas has definitely come early for Greggs fans.”

Greggs Festive Bake ingredients

Fine-tuned for 2026, the Festive Bake brings together chicken, smoked ham hock, sweetcure bacon, creamy soft cheese and spiced pork stuffing in a rich sage and cranberry sauce. It’s wrapped in golden-glazed puff pastry and finished with a crisp crumb topping, which Greggs said "flakes all down your top".

‌



View 3 Images Greggs said it had broken a record (Image: Finnbarr Webster, Getty Images)

The festive line-up also features the Pigs Under Blankets Toastie, Pepperoni Pizza with Hot Honey, Festive Feast Baguette, Festive Flatbread and Sweet Mince Pie Roll, plus three new sweet treats and a range of seasonal drinks.

Article continues below

All items on the new festive menu are now available in shops nationwide, Greggs confirmed. Customers can secure their seasonal fix on the go via Click + Collect using the Greggs App, or have the entire feast delivered to their door through Just Eat and Uber Eats.

News.title: Met Police says letter with claims about Meghan's father not shared with other law enforcement
News.content:
Markle moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes.

He is reportedly now living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having a leg amputated in 2025.

News.title: UK braces for worst of Storm Boelo as amber warnings due to come into force
News.content:
Amber weather warnings are due to come into force in northern parts of the UK as the worst weather from Storm Boelo approaches.

Strong winds and heavy showers are expected to intensify through Saturday evening, with widespread gusts of 60 to 70mph expected to hit Scotland.

Amber wind warnings from the Met Office will come into force from 21:00 BST for parts of Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England, bringing an increased risk of travel disruption and potential risk to life.

The second named storm in as many days comes as National Grid continues to restore power to thousands of properties in south-west England after the area was hit hardest by Storm Austen.

The National Grid said on Saturday that more than 124,000 properties had been restored with power supplies since the beginning of the storm. However, hundreds were still without power on Saturday evening.

Storm Boelo is set to cause disruption throughout the rest of the weekend, with the amber warning in Scotland due to stay in place for 24 hours.

Forecasters have warned of strong winds with gusts to 80mph expected in exposed coastal areas.

These winds could cause power cuts, flying debris, damage to buildings and trees, travel disruption and danger to life from large waves, the Met Office said.

The strongest winds will affect western Scotland first on Saturday evening, before spreading eastwards overnight and through Sunday.

News.title: Between quick wins and big dreams lies Burnham's biggest test
News.content:
But the widespread suggestion that you'll be able to blink and miss the Budget has got some hackles up in the Treasury. A budget, by its very nature, can never be a small event - it sets billions upon billions of taxes and spending decisions.

And there are likely to be extra taxes on banks, vows to sweep away some business regulation, particularly for small business, more powers passing to local leaders under the guise of devolution and more action on energy bills which are heading back up again.

John Healey has made it clear publicly and to staff, that he wants to encourage people with the guts and drive to start a business. One source said: "If you are taking on John's mantra about talking up Britain then you can't say, 'Nothing to see here'."

Whatever else the chancellor brings to Parliament in his red box, do not expect him to arrive with all the solutions to the country's very well-documented problems, whether that's getting the economy growing more convincingly, sorting out gaps in defence cash, welfare, social care, or new ways to pay off the country's groaning debts more quickly.

One former minister suggests even if Healey and Burnham had stumbled upon all the answers in a few months, it's just not possible to fix everything at the same time because of the constraints on the economy.

They wondered: "Is he going to invest in growth? Is he going to put everything he has into the challenges people will face this winter? Is he going to throw it at defence? There is just not enough to tackle all these problems simultaneously - ministers are going to be exposed to the cold light of day."

Burnham and Healey have to find a way of maintaining the balance in an unusually happy Labour Party.

MPs talk of ministers and Burnham himself being more visible and approachable in Parliament, knocking around with colleagues in the evening, fewer "golden slips" doled out when ministers were excused from voting alongside colleagues so they could get on with their important jobs.

One minister told me they'd had to tell their private office not to arrange for them to be "slipped" , from going to the Commons in the evening to see backbenchers.

It's paying off in the mood among MPs. One told me: "You're not feeling like the only way you can ever have a chat with a minister is by arranging an appointment for three months down the line â the soft touches really matter."

News.title: Palestinian families displaced as Israeli forces demolish Hebron homes, local officials say
News.content:
The Israeli military has launched a sweeping crackdown in the occupied West Bank, demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron and displacing hundreds of families, according to local officials.

Footage shared online showed destruction caused by Israeli bulldozers, with at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened. The military has also cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents.

The operation was announced by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday, in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed.

Netanyahu said on Friday that buildings around the site of the attack and the neighbourhoods that the two gunmen were from would be "destroyed".

Hebron's Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari said more than 1,000 people had been displaced by the operation which had been centred on the Ein Deir Baha and Farsh al-Hawa neighbourhoods, and targeted homes, businesses, industrial sites and infrastructure.

He said dozens of families had been forced to spend the night outside, with some told to leave without taking their vehicles, while homes were marked for demolition with spray paint.

He added that he believed the military planned to displace a total of 2,500 people from about 0.35 sq km of urban land. The city's governor and deputy mayor meanwhile said at least 200 families had been displaced.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) did not respond immediately to the BBC's request for comment. It said in a statement on social media that it had dozens of targets across the West Bank and that its operations would last for several days.

News.title: Infantino tells BBC Sport he is backed by 'vast majority' of world football
News.content:
During the interview he reflected on having been "fully endorsed" by the Asian Football Confederation - following a U-turn by its president Sheikh Salman - and having the backing of "all African countries".

But only last week, he apologised to the Fifa Council over the "communication and consultation" regarding FFE.

He was told by Council members in that meeting that he was not "fit to be Fifa president" if he did not give them the documents they have asked for, including the rationale for FFE.

Yet, when pressed on when he would be providing the requested papers, he did not give a clear answer, saying they had to follow a "legal process" and that they were "working on it".

"We'll answer of course all the questions that are asked as far as the process allows, as far as we can," he said.

Speaking from the first Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, he said he and the Fifa administration were doing "as best we can" but admitted they have done "some things which are maybe less good".

He also said that they need to have dialogue "more often" with Uefa, in an effort to repair their strained relationship.

Asked by the BBC if he was fit to be Fifa president, and whether he had considered standing down, he laughed, before saying: "Well you know I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world.

"I think what is important is that in an organisation like Fifa, there can be different views, different points of view.

"But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need, to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority.

"I'm just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all [Confederation of] African [Football] countries have endorsed me. I'm speaking to all associations everywhere in the world."

He continued: "There are different points of view it's not always easy to bring them all under one roof but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views and then it will be up to the Fifa member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want Fifa to be run."

The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino for the election in March is 18 November - although none have yet filed and he could stand unopposed.

News.title: Before you crank up the thermostat, try these tips to keep you and your home warmer for longer
News.content:
With the clocks going back this weekend, the nights will be drawing in.

So if you have a thicker duvet, now is the time to bring it out. Some supermarkets sell winter duvets for under Â£20 - look for 10.5 tog or higher.

But there's something to be said for a craftily placed blanket, too. When it gets cold, Rebecca, 44, from Hertfordshire, sleeps with a blanket underneath her mattress, which she says stops draughts. "This was passed to me by my nan, she swore by it," she says. Others swear by placing a blanket above the mattress but under the bedsheet.

You can heat your bed before getting in with a hot water bottle, but make sure you check the expiry date. A guide by NHS Scotland, external says to let the water from the kettle cool for a few minutes before filling, only fill it two-thirds full, squeeze air out of the top before putting the stopper on, and don't hold it directly against your skin.

Using an electric blanket - to heat your bed before you get in or to wrap around yourself on the sofa - is "one of the cheapest ways" to stay warm, says Emily Seymour, energy editor at consumer organisation Which?. Testing by Which?, external shows it typically costs between 2p and 8p an hour to run an electric blanket at its highest setting. The London Fire Brigade, external says to unplug your blanket before you get into bed unless it has a thermostat control, not to use a hot water bottle at the same time, and replace it every 10 years.

News.title: Strictly's new presenters - after mixed reviews have they found their feet?
News.content:
Strictly Come Dancing's new hosting trio received a very mixed reception when the latest series began a month ago. Ratings have dipped and the jury's still out, but critics say they are slowly getting into the groove.

Changing the hosting team on the BBC's flagship Saturday night entertainment show was never likely to be a waltz in the park.

And going from two presenters to three, and giving them slightly different roles, upset the show's rhythm even more.

Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman were always going to be a hard act to follow.

Into their sparkly shoes have stepped the safe and smooth Emma Willis; the flamboyant former professional dancer Johannes Radebe; and cheeky comedian Josh Widdicombe, a wildcard who was not hitherto associated with either the dance world or prime-time TV.

Willis and Widdicombe have been paired on the live shows, where he is tasked with injecting humour into the moments before and after each dance - with mixed results, say critics.

Radebe, meanwhile, has taken over from Winkleman upstairs on the mezzanine, bringing his warmth and dance expertise to the celebrity interviews following each routine.

News.title: California considers imposing 'world's first' tax on billionaires
News.content:
While the ballot measure has many supporters - including some billionaires like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - it has faced fierce opposition from a variety of figures, from billionaires to the state's liberal governor.

Google co-founder Sergey Brin has given more than $100m to a political organisation funding ballot measures that could block the wealth tax, the Los Angeles Times reports, external.

California Governor Gavin Newsom, whose tenure is coming to an end, is perhaps the most notable political leader opposing it. He has voiced concerns that the measure could cause the wealthy to leave the state and drive out their crucial income tax revenue.

A September poll, external from the Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies and the Los Angeles Times found the proposition has not clearly won over a majority of voters, with 45% of likely voters in favour of the tax, 42% opposed and 13% undecided.

The statewide ballot measure would need to be approved by a majority of residents.

California is not the first place to toy with the idea of taxing the rich. Also on the West Coast, voters in US state of Washington are considering whether to accept or reject a "millionaires tax" - a 9.9% tax on income over $1m a year.

While wealth taxes were once a fairly common form of taxation in Europe, they have rapidly fallen out of favour and now only exist in three European countries â Spain, Norway and Switzerland, says Dr Kristian Niemietz, head of political economy at the Institute of Economic Affairs.

Niemietz believes wealth taxes are "more trouble than they are worth" because they cause administrative issues, suppress investment, lead to capital flight and, in the end, do not raise much revenue.

In the case of Norway, a local news organisation found that an increase in the wealth tax led to more super wealthy people leaving the country in 2022, external than in the preceding 13 years combined. A study on Switzerland, external found that a 0.1 percentage point increase in a wealth tax reduced taxable wealth by 3.5%.

News.title: Plan for Northern Olympics to get £7m in Healey's Budget
News.content:
The report will look in closer detail at how hosting the games could work.

It will consider the kinds of venues and transport links required, how different cities could share the games, how communities could benefit.

Crucially it will also examine how much it could cost as well as assess the chances of a bid succeeding. The Conservative-Lib Dem coalition government said in 2013 it estimated hosting in London had cost Â£8.9bn.

A report in 2013 by the UK Trade and Investment, which has since been replaced by the Department for International Trade, said it had sparked a Â£9.9bn boost to the economy through new contracts, sales and foreign investments.

But the estimated amount was queried by some, including the Federation of Small Businesses and the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (NIESR).

Conservative shadow sports minister Louie French said that while hosting an Olympic Games would "likely provide a positive boost for the country", the cost of proposals would require "careful scrutiny".

He said the chancellor should use the Budget to bring down everyday costs before looking to "spend millions in taxpayer cash on reheated announcements made by his predecessor".

French added: "The irony is that Labour's new tourism tax will create a cost barrier for sports fans wanting to visit the North of England for an Olympic Games."

The new feasibility study for the Northern Games will be done by government, UK Sport, the Northern Mayors and include the British Olympic and Paralympic associations.

Healey said: "Olympic legacy lasts way beyond the celebration of sport over the summer. The North hosting an event as big as this would be truly unforgettable.

"Britain's experience of London 2012 is proof we can host the world. I'm picking up the pace on our work to potentially bid for these prestigious games. It will lift communities, create opportunities and give the UK a huge boost."

News of the funding for the study was welcomed by the British Olympic Association, ParalympicsGB and UK Sport.

"We welcome the government's continued support for exploring the potential of a future bid for the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the UK in the 2040s," they said in a joint statement.

"Building on the success and legacy of London 2012, we look forward to working in partnership to explore this exciting opportunity and the benefits it could deliver for the nation, and for the global Olympic and Paralympic movements."

News.title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab
News.content:
The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.

As part of Wednesday's Budget, the government will commit Â£100m to establishing the new, "world first" institute with the support of leading AI firms.

The chancellor will also pledge millions of pounds in spending across a range of initiatives aimed at shoring up the UK's ability to respond to evolving cyber, biological and AI-enabled threats.

"AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school, and every aspect of our economy can benefit," John Healey said.

"I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI.

"One that doesn't leave workers behind and defends our national interest, while ensuring the benefits of AI-enabled growth are felt right across the country."

The full details about the role and remit of the new lab are yet to emerge.

But the AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said it would be a "major new global institution" that brings together "world-leading scientific expertise" to ensure the UK can safeguard its citizens and goals as AI develops.

"That means staying ahead of emerging threats, from cyber attacks to biological risks, while building more of the critical technology our security depends on," he said.

"By backing British science, advanced chips and our own AI companies, we can strengthen our national security, rebuild Britain's industrial strength and create good, skilled jobs across the country."

The AI Biosecurity Lab's creation will also be supported by leading AI developers, with OpenAI and Anthropic providing Â£200m worth of AI model credits that can be spent on the use of their models.

News.title: Tory activist in 'contract killing broker' claim had worked for party HQ
News.content:
A former Tory activist who appeared to offer to "broker" the hiring of contract killers in an undercover film report previously worked for Conservative headquarters.

Jack Ross was contracted to do social media work for the party until earlier this year, the BBC has been told.

It comes after Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch referred to them as "shocking allegations", adding that she did not "believe that person is a member anymore".

A Conservative spokesman said Ross's party membership had "been suspended with immediate effect pending an investigation". It has reported that Ross said his words were not meant to be taken seriously.

Ross was paid to provide social media advice to the party for a brief period, the BBC has been told. He was never an employee or Conservative Campaign Headquarters pass holder.

However, he met Badenoch on several occasions as part of his role as chief executive of Turning Point UK, an offshoot of a right-wing American organisation.

Ross has also met several other right-wing politicians including the former Prime Minister Boris Johnson and Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader.

In undercover filming broadcast this week by Al Jazeera, Ross appears to offer to "broker" the services of contract killers.

The Al Jazeera report said its undercover journalist approached Ross in 2022 with a fictitious situation of a family business at risk of being taken over by a criminal gang.

Ross is alleged to have asked the undercover reporter what was needed from him, and listed violent options that could be bought including stabbing, shooting and killing.

Al Jazeera said Ross denied the finding "completely" and claimed everything he said to the reporter was not meant seriously.

Turning Point UK has been approached for comment.

News.title: Sam Fender calls out ticket prices ahead of tour
News.content:
Sam Fender has called out the price of gig tickets ahead of his next tour, promising to lower the cost.

The 32-year-old announced his Proper Massive Stadium Tour earlier this week, which will visit Newcastle, Cardiff, London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Manchester in summer 2027.

While tickets are yet to go on sale, Fender responded to a post on social media which claimed to outline the expected ticket prices.

The Geordie musician also said standing would not be split into a front and back tier and he had "no idea how this was normalised at gigs".

Tickets are due to go on general sale at 09:30 GMT on Friday, with a pre-sale at the same time on Wednesday.

But Fender said he was "not happy" with the reported prices.

"They're getting changed," he said on Instagram.

"It got inflated well more than I'd had in mind, it should only be inflated in relation to the cost of putting the show on."

The North Shields singer also said he did not want there to be an option for fans to pay more money to be closer to the front.

"The standing will not be split as well, I had no idea about it," Fender said.

"I have no idea how this was normalised in gigs... it won't be happening on this tour."

He is not the first musician to raise concerns over ticket pricing.

Zara Larsson agreed with fans earlier this year that her tickets were too expensive.

The Swedish singer said while she did not have control over the prices, she hoped she would in the future.
