Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star opens up on Ruben Amorim ‘bomb squad’ with no reason given for ‘tough’ time
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star opens up on Ruben Amorim ‘bomb squad’ with no reason given for ‘tough’ time

Former Manchester United defender Tyrell Malacia has opened up on his tough time at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Former Man Utd boss Ruben Amorim has been criticised by Tyrell Malacia. (Image: (Photo by Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images))

Former Manchester United left-back Tyrell Malacia has revealed he had no conversations with Ruben Amorim regarding his inclusion in the club's notorious 'bomb squad'. The 27-year-old, who departed Old Trafford during the summer transfer window, has spoken out about his treatment under the former manager.

‌



‌



Malacia was among a group of outcasts that included Marcus Rashford, Alejandro Garnacho, Antony and Jadon Sancho, all of whom were banished from first-team training. Yet while his fellow exiles managed to secure moves elsewhere, the full-back found himself training in isolation.

‌



"I had a good first season and then I had my injury," Malacia told BBC Sport. "I don't want to talk too much about it, but certain things happened in my rehab.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Ruben came in when I just got back from my injury. He gave me a couple of games, but I had come back after a year and a half.

‌



"Imagine not playing for a year and a half and adapting to everything, especially in the best league in the world and playing for such a big club. It takes time.

"As a player you need to understand if you play for a big club like Manchester United, sometimes you don't get the time."

‌



View 2 Images Tyrell Malacia left Manchester United at the end of last season (Image: Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Dutchman made eight appearances following his comeback from injury before heading to PSV Eindhoven on loan for the remainder of the 2024/25 season, returning to United hopeful of a fresh start.

He said: "Even at that time I still wasn't 100%, but it was good for me to get game time and adapting to the game.

‌



"After that period of six months, I came back in summer I thought 'OK, now it's going happen, I'm going to get a fair chance'."

Antonio Conte's two demands to take Man Utd job emerge after giving green light READ MORE :

Man Utd chiefs SPLIT on Michael Carrick replacement as player row spills into boardroom READ MORE :

Yet Malacia found no place in Amorim's setup and was consigned to a so-called 'bomb squad' of players deemed surplus to requirements.

‌



Speaking candidly about that gruelling period, he said: "I don't know where that came from, I don't know if it was Ruben or higher up or anything, but I never said anything about it, I just kept working and doing my thing even though it was difficult sometimes training in a group of five.

"At some point Marcus, Garnacho and even Antony left. Then I stayed on my own, training with the second team, even with the under-18s and below. It's tough. It's tough mentally.

Article continues below

"I could have said 'OK, I'm not coming into training'. But I thought 'that's not going to help me'. It's a reason for them to say 'this is the reason you are with them or training on your own'. I just kept my head down and did the work.

"I always stayed fit since I came back from my injury, but people didn't know that. They were like 'why is he not playing?'".

Sports.title: Luke Littler backed to surpass David Beckham's wealth ahead of Netflix show
Sports.content:
Dennis Priestley believes Luke Littler has the chance to even outshine David Beckham’s wealth.

Priestley is a double world champion and had the distinction of lifting the first title of the PDC era when he beat Phil Taylor 6-1 in 1994.

The first prize then was £16,000 to the winner… now it is a million pounds, which Littler banked when he successfully defended his title last January.

Littler will take on 20 hopefuls in Netflix show 'Beat Luke Littler' next week. If any of the 20 challengers, including Fallon Sherrock, beat Littler over a single-leg format they will win £501,000.

‌



In ‘Champions: The Golden Age of Darts From Priestley to Littler’, “The Menace' says: ‘If I had the chance to do it all again, I would throw like Luke Littler, Luke Humphries or Adrian Lewis, who was maybe the first player to make it look so simple and fluid.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Luke Littler vows he will not go easy on amateurs attempting to beat him for £501,000 READ MORE :

“The game is so much quicker now – much faster than me standing there trying to concentrate while my arm stopped shaking. They used to put a stopwatch on my throw and timed it at 17 seconds for me to release three darts where Phil took 13 seconds.

“I got it rammed down my throat so many times and admittedly it’s not as quick as someone like Ricky Evans, who can hit 180 in about 2.2 seconds, but it wasn’t a question of mind games or deliberately putting off your opponent. And what’s four seconds between friends?

‌



"I just hope the game continues to grow and the players are allowed to express themselves.

“We don’t yet know what Littler is going to achieve, and how good he’s going to be, because he’s got another 20 or 30 years ahead of him if he wants it.

“If he’s still going when he’s 40, and he practises even half as much as Phil, the mind boggles. I once said that if he stays grounded, and he can be top of the tree for 10 years, he could be worth more than David Beckham.”

Meanwhile, Littler has been told by Taylor that living “like a monk” could see him become the greatest darts player of them all. In just over six weeks, ‘The Nuke’ will take to the stage of the Ally Pally to begin the defence of his world darts crown.

‌



Littler, who does not turn 20 until January, is chasing a third successive crown in a sport where the legend that is Taylor holds the record as the 16-times world champion.

View 4 Images David Beckham has a staggering net worth (Image: Getty Images)

But The Power believes Littler can eclipse his amazing success – if he follows the right path.

“Luke is leading darts into an era where the top players will soon have a lifestyle like tennis professionals – with their own trainers, nutritionists, masseuses and drivers. He will also find that the more he wins, the more it will do his head in when he loses,” says Taylor.

‌



"Will he overtake my record of 16 World Championship titles? He could do, he’s absolutely fantastic.

“Would it bother me? Not at all – records are there to be broken, and I’ve had more publicity since he came on the scene than I ever had when I was winning it. Luke has got age on his side, he’s got the ability and he’s got a lovely family behind him.

"He is so down to earth, such a nice kid, that if he remembers to live a boring life for the next 20 years – steer clear of nightclubs, booze, fast cars and all the normal vices for a young man – the sky’s the limit for him. If he is prepared to make those sacrifices and live like a monk, he could break all sorts of records.”

Taylor is speaking in a new book, ‘Champions: The Golden Age of Darts From Priestley to Littler’, where The Nuke says: “I’ve got plenty of years ahead of me, and obviously if I’m good at it, I want to keep going.

‌



“As Michael van Gerwen said, if there’s no fire in your belly, there’s no point in carrying on for the sake of it.

View 4 Images Darts legend Phil Taylor (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

“I don’t want to reach a head space where I’m just going up on stage and throwing darts because I can. If you’re good at your sport, you should carry on because you’re a long time retired.

“Look at Cristiano Ronaldo – he’s in a game which takes a real toll on your body, but if you go to a World Cup at 41 as a footballer you must love the game and be really good at it.”

‌



If Littler follows the leads set by Taylor and Ronaldo, it is impossible to calculate how many cups he will have in his trophy cabinet by the year 2048 when he will also be 41.

The double world champion has won 14 major individual PDC crowns and let’s not forget he was a world finalist at the age of just 16, losing to Luke Humphries in 2024, before taking the title over the next two years.

And that included banking the first prize of one million pounds, the richest in the sport’s history, when he beat Dutchman Gian Van Veen 7-1 in the final last January.

His impact on the sport has been amazing.

‌



As PDC President Barry Hearn says: “Luke Littler’s story gives me a reason to turn round to my wife and say, ‘You told me you didn’t like darts, but you don’t miss a dart when Luke is on the box’.

“He has brought in a new generation of fans and we have to be ready to harness their custom. There’s still a look-down-your-nose attitude towards darts in some quarters, but Littler earned over £2million at 17 years of age, and he bought his mum and dad a nice house. That brings it home what darts can do to change your life.”

View 4 Images

Champions: The Golden Age of Darts From Priestley to Littler by Mike Walters is released on Monday by Pitch Publishing, £25 hardback. www.pitchpublishing.co.uk/shop/champions-0

Sports.title: 'Roy Keane ripped into me in blazing row – but I had the perfect response'
Sports.content:
'Roy Keane ripped into me in blazing row – but I had the perfect response'

Roy Keane launched a furious rant at a player who responded in the best possible way

View 2 Images Roy Keane launched a verbal tirade at James McClean in 2017 (Image: Getty )

Roy Keane once ripped into James McClean during a foul-mouthed dressing room row while on Republic of Ireland duty. But the winger, now 37, responded perfectly to his then-assistant manager Keane’s criticism about his application levels by scoring in the following game.

‌



‌



McClean celebrated his 50th international cap for Ireland by captaining his nation in a friendly against Mexico back in June 2017. But the then-West Bromwich Albion star had a poor game as his side lost 3-1, having conceded a penalty himself in the first half.

‌



Manchester United legend Keane, who was Martin O’Neill’s assistant at the time, unleashed his wrath on McClean and his team-mates in the dressing room at half-time. The pundit appeared to be especially triggered by a meeting with Irish boxer Mick Conlan before the New Jersey match.

‌



Writing in his autobiography The Walls, as per the Irish Independent, McClean said: "Martin [O’Neill] had just finished his bit when Roy came over, got right in my face and started f***ing me out of it.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Roy Keane finally breaks golden rule as Gary Neville mocks 'fawning' Man Utd legend READ MORE :

Sir Alex Ferguson was one day from becoming Arsenal boss as contract offer revealed READ MORE :

"'Look at you, the f***ing captain, f***ing giving off, yeah? You were taking pictures before the game with f***ing Mick Conlan. Your head isn’t f***ing in it.'"

‌



McClean remained silent during Keane’s dressing room scolding. But the ex-United skipper doubled down by accusing him of "having a big ego" in another furious rant during a gym session.

McClean continued: "He said he’d never been critical of me in the press or around the group, and now, the first time he’d said anything, I’d pulled him up over it.

‌



View 2 Images McClean had a poor game against Mexico (Image: Getty )

"Then he started going off about the Lamborghini at Sunderland, which was f***ing six years earlier. I was thinking he must have been seething for the afternoon, gathering information."

‌



That was in relation to then-Sunderland manager O’Neill having allegedly dropped the Irishman for buying a supercar. But McClean responded to Keane's comments in the best possible way, scoring in Ireland’s 3-1 friendly win over Uruguay in the following game and performing a selfie celebration.

McClean went on to reach 103 caps for Ireland, scoring 11 goals for the Boys in Green. He returned to his hometown club Derry City in January 2026 but has not played for the side since August due to a bitter public dispute with the club hierarchy.

Article continues below

Keane, meanwhile, left his role as Ireland's assistant manager in November 2018, departing alongside O’Neill and the rest of the coaching staff after a poor run of form where they failed to win across the entire year. His last managerial role was his five-month tenure as O’Neill’s assistant at Nottingham Forest, after which he has focused solely on his successful media career.

Sports.title: Ramsay and Sule fire St Mirren to victory over Dundee
Sports.content:
St Mirren ended a run of five straight defeats as goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule secured a 2-1 win over Dundee.

Wing-back Ramsay fired Saints ahead in the 20th minute with his first goal since joining the club on loan in the summer.

Sule doubled the lead for the Buddies in the 57th minute to give his side a real grip of the game.

Dundee pulled a goal back in the 73rd minute through Bradley Fink after a decent spell of pressure but the visitors could not find an equaliser.

St Mirren were first to threaten as the wintry conditions played a role in the early stages. Ismeal Kabia unleashed a shot from the edge of the box, but it was held by Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

The home side made the breakthrough when Sule broke down the righ before playing the ball across goal into the path of Ramsay, whose shot trickled over the line with the block from Goodman unable to keep it out.

The Saints loanee almost doubled his tally when he rose to meet a free-kick from the left. His header fell straight into the arms of Goodman, who then spilled the ball before it was scrambled clear.

Sule turned scorer in the second-half to give St Mirren full command of the match. A cross from Killian Phillips was met by the head of the attacker on the edge of the six-yard box to double the home side's lead.

Dundee pushed to get a foothold back in the game with Ashley Hay bulleting a header narrowly wide from close range.

The visitors did eventually pull a goal back through Fink. St Mirren keeper Jacob Chapman saved the initial shot only for the Dundee striker to knock the ball home at the second attempt.

The away side pushed for an equaliser in the latter stages, but the Buddies held on to claim all three points, much to the delight of a delirious but sodden home crowd.

What the managers said...

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish:

"I'm delighted for the group. They probably needed something like that.

"It's easy for me to keep saying the same messages and keep talking to them about their confidence and belief and what we're trying to do, but when you go on a run like we've been on, it can be difficult for the players at times.

"We had one really good run, we've had a poor run, hopefully that's us coming out of it now as well."

Dundee boss Steven Pressley:

"In the first half we showed a lot of bravery in possession, in terms of our build-up and in controlling the game, but we didn't ask enough questions of them defensively.

"We spoke prior to the game about that particular fact: that we must ask questions of them defensively in a variety of ways. We didn't ask enough of them.

"Credit to St Mirren. They've gone through a difficult period, and they showed a lot of resilience today."

Sports.title: Giant Sequoia stakes Classic claims in Futurity
Sports.content:
Giant Sequoia produced an eyecatching performance to win the William Hill Futurity Trophy at Doncaster and in the process virtually guarantee Aidan O’Brien the trainers’ championship.

It was stablemate Sergei Diaghilev who set a brisk pace at the head of the Group One field, before the race began to take shape as they hit the two-furlong pole, with all the runners on the stands side.

Ryan Moore and favourite Noble Exhibit put down their challenge a furlong and a half out, but Giant Sequoia (11-1) was travelling strongly upsides and really picked up when asked by Dylan Browne McMonagle, stretching three lengths clear of Andrew Balding's staying-on Gran Dia.

It was a record-extending 13th success in the race for O'Brien, who had been happy to draw a line through the winner's disappointing effort in last month's National Stakes.

He said: "He disappointed the last day, but that was when our horses were off colour.

"I'm over the moon with him really, he travelled well, quickened very well and I'm delighted for everyone at home. It's a big team effort.

"He's very classy, he could be anything next year. He was just under the weather the last day. We gave him time, his work has been lovely.

"We weren't sure about that ground, but you never know until you try. He's very classy."

O'Brien has won the Town Moor feature with three subsequent Derby winners and added of the Frankel colt: "We always thought he was a Classic horse, a mile or a mile and a quarter would be no problem, but he could get a mile and a half. His dam (Pink Dogwood) was very good and she stayed.

"We always thought he was very good, a proper horse. I'd say he's a Guineas, Derby, French Derby horse, all those things.

"One of his owners is American (John Stewart), but we had four others for the Breeders' Cup so we tried to space them out a bit!"

On Noble Exhibit, who was edged for second by Gran Dia, O'Brien said: "He was a bit green, he was running around a lot.

"He won making the running twice and probably didn't learn a lot. Maybe in that ground he gave him the chance to run green and he got there and ran around a bit."

While Browne McMonagle has been winning countless big races for O'Brien's son, Joseph, this was his first Group One for the Ballydoyle handler.

"He's a great rider, that's all you can say," said O'Brien.

The jockey himself said: "He's a horse who has developed plenty throughout the year, he's a big boy to sit on.

"The race worked out perfect, it was a nice even tempo and he relaxed. I felt like halfway on it was just a matter of sitting into him and he reacted quick.

"He quickened well and when I got to the front he was having a nice look, but he's still a big baby and he's going to be a lovely horse next year.

"Everyone was very complimentary of him and they said he was a lovely horse and going up to a mile was always going to be a help to him. I think he'll get further in time and he's very solid. He's definitely a good horse."

He added: "That's a first Group One for Aidan, so a big thanks for the leg-up."

Bengal Tiger far too good for the rest in Prospect Stakes

Aidan O'Brien's Bengal Tiger looked a class apart as he left the field in his wake to land the William Hill Remembering Sue Wright Prospect Stakes at Doncaster.

Ryan Moore was happy to settle the 10-11 favourite on the outside as the keen-going Crystal Queen pulled them along in front in the six-furlongs Listed affair.

Moore shook his mount up with a quarter of a mile to race and as soon as he asked for an effort with a furlong to go Bengal Tiger put it to bed, streaking clear to score by three and a half lengths from Hi Corbett Court.

O'Brien thinks the winner will easily stay further and views him as a Classic contender.

Image: Bengal Tiger, ridden by Ryan Moore, on their way to winning the William Hill Remembering Sue Wright Prospect Stakes at Doncaster

"What he did the last day at Naas shouldn't usually happen, no matter how bad the race was the time was very good," said O'Brien.

"We were going to go to the Horris Hill at Newbury, but that got abandoned. We wanted to go there because we thought he'd love going seven furlongs, but we switched back here.

"The last half a furlong he started to take off, he's going to get seven easily and I'd say he's a Classic horse.

"It's unusual for one by No Nay Never to go through heavy ground like that, but he's out of a good Galileo mare (On Ice), so we shouldn't be surprised.

"It wasn't his speed that won him it today, it was staying, the last furlong he was getting going."

Sports.title: Lincoln thump four past sorry Burnley
Sports.content:
Mikkel Ladefoged marked his first league start with a second-half brace as Lincoln City blew struggling Burnley away to secure an emphatic 4-1 Championship victory at Sincil Bank.

The visitors led through substitute Andreas Hountndji's strike before Ben House levelled in first-half stoppage time.

And the damage was done within eight second-half minutes as Ladefoged and Dom Jefferies ensured the Imps secured victory in the first league meeting between the two sides this century on a miserable afternoon in Lincolnshire.

Danish striker Ladefoged put the game beyond doubt with his second with just over 20 minutes to go but the writing was already on the wall.

Burnley's afternoon got even worse when George Wickens saved Marcus Edwards' penalty late on.

Both managers rung the changes in a bid to get back to winning ways and it was Tom Shaw who ended his side's winless run of four games to go seven points safe of the danger zone as Burnley remained rooted inside the dreaded bottom three with the pressure continuing to mount on under-fire boss Nicky Hayen.

Burnley, who were relegated from the Premier League last term, have won just one game all season with calls for Hayen's head mounting among the club's disgruntled fans.

The hosts almost got off to the perfect start when Romanian international Andrei Coubis had the ball in the net inside the first five minutes, only for it rightfully to be ruled out for offside.

Lincoln's Reeco Hackett blocked Max Alleyne's effort on the line to keep the game goalless in the 25th minute.

The Clarets hit the front in the 39th minute when Hountndji, who came off the bench after 11 minutes to replace the injured Armando Broja, tapped home Lucas Pires' in-swinging corner at the back post.

But the lead didn't last long as House poked home at the back post himself after Coubis' long throw evaded everyone in the box deep in first-half stoppage time.

And Lincoln led minutes into the second half as 23-year-old Ladefoged curled an unstoppable strike from close range home with Gregoire Coudert well beaten.

Welshman Jefferies netted his first league goal since March with a strike from outside the box after Burnley failed to clear their lines from a corner.

Ladefoged made it four in the 67th minute when he headed home House's cross into the top right corner.

Ryley Towler felled Hountondji in the box, but Wickens guessed correctly to rub salt into the already gaping Clarets' wounds six minutes from time.

The managers

Lincoln's Tom Shaw:

"I'm delighted. I'm delighted for a few groups of people… the staff and the players for the work ethic and what goes on behind the scenes that you really don't see.

"Probably more importantly than anyone is the supporters. We felt we owed them one for the West Ham experience. It's a game we wish we could have back. We owed them something.

"We felt we were a little bit short points wise for our performances here. So we knew this was a big day and a big opportunity.

"We got our reward of Lincoln City beating Burnley 4-1 in a league game.

"You've got to remember the journey and all the people that helped us get here.

"Obviously we had the West Ham experience and then Millwall away with those last 20 minutes at The Den (drawing 2-2 from 2-0 up).

"That feeling at full-time, for everybody, was amazing. It was just an amazing day and one to build on for us.

"That's what we want this football team to look like and play like.

"We've got nothing to fear when you can see what our group is capable of."

Burnley head coach Nicky Hayen:

"We had one saved on the line and then scored a goal. And you think you can push on even more, but then we conceded another easy goal. A throw in went to the second post and no one takes responsibility to clear it and they react faster than us.

"It's the same story of the season for us that we keep conceding easy goals and you saw that in the second half.

"They want to work hard, but you have to show it. What we do in training is really good, but we can't execute that the same way in the games. Is that pressure? I don't know.

"It's frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn't matter because it's another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.

"We haven't got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops.

"I don't know (if I will still be in charge). I know it's a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Gudjohnsen double steers Blackburn past Wrexham
Sports.content:
Andri Gudjohnsen's second brace in a week earned Blackburn a clinical 2-0 win over Wrexham.

The Icelandic striker's return from injury has coincided with an upturn in Rovers' results as goals in each half delivered a third win in five games that moves Tony Mowbray's side to within two points of the play-offs.

His first, a minute before half-time, was a poacher's finish as he swept in when Sam Morsy's shot was parried, and he made the game safe in the 79th minute with an emphatic strike from 12 yards for his eighth of the campaign.

It could have been more comfortable as Dapo Afolayan and Augustus Kargbo went close, and although Sam Smith headed wide for Wrexham with the score at 1-0, Phil Parkinson's men were outclassed as their winless away run stretched to four.

Rovers were a whisker away from hitting the front in the third minute when Jayden Fevrier cut in from the right and curled agonisingly wide of the far post.

Wrexham settled into the game with both Kieffer Moore and Callum O'Hare's shots blocked in the 14th minute as Rovers desperately tried to clear their lines.

Mowbray's men weathered that pressure and nearly gave the visitors a taste of their own medicine when Hayden Carter's outstretched foot diverted Todd Cantwell's 42nd-minute corner goalwards, only for the ball to strike the post before Anthony Patterson gratefully gathered.

There was no reprieve two minutes later when Moussa Baradji, making his first start of the season, wriggled away from two players and set up Sam Morsy, whose long-range effort was parried by Patterson straight to Gudjohnsen, who clinically swept into the bottom right corner.

Afolayan missed a glorious chance to double the advantage four minutes after the restart when Cantwell's pass sent him through one-on-one but Patterson spread himself brilliantly to repel the effort.

Wrexham started to create chances of their own as Matty James volleyed wide before O'Hare's 57th-minute cross found Smith, who glanced a free header wide of the far post.

They went close again 10 minutes later when Jacques Ekomie raided down the left and crossed for Moore, whose left-foot shot was blocked and fell to Joe Worrall, who hammered just wide of the left post from inside the area.

Rovers introduced Kargbo from the bench and his express pace almost brought a counter-attacking second as he burst forward from a Wrexham corner on to Cantwell's pass and drove low from the right, forcing Patterson to parry behind.

However, Gudjohnsen made the game safe 11 minutes from time with another deadly finish, latching on to Cantwell's pass 12 yards out before turning away from Worrall and burying into the top corner.

The managers

Blackburn head coach Tony Mowbray:

"Andri has started his career pretty well, I think, and it goes where it goes, hopefully with us trying to fire the goals for a season or two.

"People tell me he was scoring a lot of goals at the start of the last season and then he picked up an injury. So he's obviously very, very talented.

"He's got good movement, he strikes a brilliant ball, he's very physical and competitive. He's got all the attributes.

"I've just talked about humility in the dressing room and as long as he carries that with him everywhere, he's got a great chance to have a wonderful career.

"He's a great kid, nice lad, doesn't get carried away with anything. I can feel the steadiness of him, he's just scored quite a lot of goals, even before today. And there's no overconfident guy. He just gets on with his job. He's very humble and I like him a lot."

Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson:

"Difficult conditions for both sides. We were against it a bit in terms of elements first half.

"Obviously conceding just before the break was a setback but we still felt at half-time the game was there for us. But we couldn't produce the quality we needed.

"We've had 23 attempts but to only have one of those on target, we have to look at that.

"I've got to give Blackburn defenders credit because they blocked things, made 9-10 blocks. They defended crosses, they defended set plays. It was a combination of their good defending, but we couldn't find that clinical moment to get us back in the game and the game was separated on two moments.

"When we analyse the positions we got into, we got in enough good positions to have got something from the game but we just didn't produce the quality."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Preston claim first point under Alexander
Sports.content:
Substitute Aune Heggebo struck late for West Brom to deny Preston a first win under Graham Alexander in a 1-1 draw at a wind-swept Deepdale in the Championship.

The Norwegian came off the bench on the hour and rifled home an 82nd-minute leveller just four minutes after Andrew Hughes hooked North End into the lead from a corner.

James Morrison's visitors had already come from behind to win against Wrexham and Blackburn in their last two matches but Preston deserved their point.

It was their first since Alexander took charge earlier this month and came at the end of a week where two of their first-team coaches left the club, in part as a result of their position at the bottom of the Championship.

Preston started well in the troublesome wet and windy conditions with Johnny Kenny forcing Max O'Leary into a low save with a speculative shot in the opening two minutes before Leo Leroy dragged an effort across goal shortly after.

West Brom were 2-0 inside 12 minutes against Blackburn last weekend and it was another slow start here, though Isaac Price did force Daniel Iversen into a smart save with a 28th-minute curling effort.

The Northern Ireland midfielder should have hit the target 12 minutes later, guiding Jayson Molumby's wind-assisted cross wide from close range.

Chances were in short supply for both teams but Alexander's side had a clear opening within 60 seconds of the second half as Kenny teed up Delano Burgzorg in the box and O'Leary did well to parry the Dutchman's powerful shot.

A few minutes later, Kenny went from provider to goal-chaser, trying to place an effort in at the near post from just inside the box, though it was a fairly routine save for Albion keeper O'Leary.

The wind was in the Lilywhites' sails and Burgzorg floundered an even better opportunity to bag the opener in the 54th minute, stabbing wide a gorgeous low delivery from Stanley Mills with the goal gaping.

Not long later, it was a chance-a-piece in quick succession as Kenny headed over Andrija Vukcevic's whipped in cross before Felix Myhre's point-blank prod was brilliantly blocked by Iversen as Brayann Pereira's header deflected perfectly into his path.

Perseverance and endeavour paid off for the hard-working home team and Hughes flicked Leroy's corner into the net with the visiting defence allowing the corner to bounce into his path.

Elation rang around three quarters of Deepdale but it was short lived as Heggebo slammed West Brom level in the 82nd minute as Preston failed to clear their lines after Iversen had brilliantly tipped Price's close-range strike on to the post.

Sports.title: Stoke and Bristol City battle to draw
Sports.content:
Stoke and Bristol City played out a hard-fought 0-0 draw at the bet365 Stadium.

The visitors came closest to pinching a winner through Gibson Yah's first-half effort.

Mark Robins' men have lost just once in their last nine matches, while Bristol City avoided a third straight defeat following back-to-back 1-0 losses.

The stalemate sees the Robins sit 14th in the Championship table, while Stoke drop out of the play-off places to fall to ninth.

Stoke's one enforced change saw Luca Bombino replace the in-form Eric Bocat at left wing-back after the latter suffered a knee injury in the Potters' 1-0 win over Derby last time out.

Image: Ethan Galbraith of Stoke City battles with Jason Knight of Bristol City

There was much more movement in the Robins line-up, with the most eyebrow-raising of Michael Skubala's four changes seeing Brad Collins, once signed by Robins at Coventry, make his competitive debut in goal in place of Sam Tickle.

Lisav Eissat, Joe Williams and Lorent Tolaj replaced Rob Atkinson, Yu Hirakawa and Scott Twine as City changed to a 3-5-2 formation to match their in-form hosts.

Only West Ham had picked up more points than the 19 Stoke had accumulated since losing their opening three games of the season, and the hosts made the brighter start at a wet and windy bet365 Stadium.

Lamine Cisse latched onto Ben Wilmot's defence-splitting pass before blazing his effort high and wide inside the opening two minutes.

Wilmot then took advantage of some indecisiveness in the Bristol City defence, nipping in and firing his effort past the far post.

Much of Stoke's early good play had come down the right between Wilmot and Cisse, but when the latter was forced off injured after 20 minutes, the hosts' threat dwindled.

The Robins took 35 minutes to notch their first attempt on goal when Dom Ballard was played in by Eissat and cut inside before firing his effort off Bosun Lawal for a corner.

The best opening of the half was to come shortly after when Bristol City wing-back Rio Cardines found space down the right and cut back for Yah, who scuffed his effort wide from 12 yards out.

Lawal then fired over following Jack McGlynn's corner.

The visitors started the second half where they left off in the first, with former Stoke loanee Luke McNally heading Cameron Pring's cross narrowly wide eight minutes after the restart.

Justin Devenny had scored two goals for the Potters since his move from Crystal Palace without getting back on the scoresheet since early September, but he came agonisingly close to putting Stoke ahead when he almost got on the end of George Hirst's knockdown following McGlynn's corner.

At the other end, Ballard glanced Pring's corner over the bar before whistling an effort narrowly over the crossbar as the visitors continued to threaten.

As the clash ticked over into stoppage time, McGlynn's curling effort left Collins stranded in the Robins' goal, but flashed past the left-hand post as both sides were left to settle for a point.

The managers

Stoke manager Mark Robins:

"It was really difficult. I can't be too critical and I don't want to be, because I don't think it's warranted. I think that we've tried to do everything that we could to get a goal, but I didn't think we were good enough.

"We move it in different areas and it becomes a bit samey and we don't learn from that. They've changed shape today, they've come for a difficult game and then the weather made it doubly so.

"We've tried everything but we've been in positions where we've taken a safe position to get on the ball rather than something a little bit more incisive.

"That's the only sort of slight disappointment, but when a team comes and sits like that, and it's the first time a team has come and done that, I think we've got to take some learning from it and where we've got to be positioned on the pitch.

"We had total control of the ball, total control of the game, but an easy option on it. Set plays we were dangerous, I thought it looked like we were going to score from one of them, I think we tried to negate their threat.

"To be fair to them, they've thrown bodies in front when they needed to and we didn't manage to get the winning goal, but if you can't win, don't lose."

Bristol City head coach Michael Skubala:

"A typical Championship, windy game of football. I thought it was a really good character performance from ourselves, I thought the game was difficult for both teams.

"We created some excellent moments in the game, some good box entries where we probably didn't have the last bit but I thought we came with a plan to set up and hit them on the counter-attack and I thought we did that well at times, so I'm really pleased with the performance and a good point on the road.

"We've been looking at it for a while to see if we can solidify, make ourselves stronger without the ball, but I thought the shape change was good, the lads were excellent in it and there was some really good performances.

"We knew how tough it would be because they've started the season very well here.

"They've got some really fast players on the top line, put some teams to the sword here, but I thought we defended very well and created some big chances.

"For us to defend and get our second clean sheet of the season is really important, to limit a Stoke team who have been on a really good run is also excellent, and I think we just needed to hit the target with some of our chances to turn it into a win."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Clinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and Gabriel
Sports.content:
The wait goes on for David Moyes. The 63-year-old Scot must have been hoping that on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as the Premier League champions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall.

While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal were never going to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester City after their defeat to Aston Villa earlier in the day.

Asked whether it was strange that his side are again going toe-to-toe with their great rivals but with the added uncertainty of what punishment City will receive after being found guilty of 115 charges by the Premier League, Mikel Arteta said: “[We are] just focusing on what we can do. We are very pleased with 90% of the results and performances that we have.”

This was hardly a vintage performance from the clinical home side after a testing week but it did not need to be against opponents who offered precious little in attack, even if they defended for their lives at times.

Having gone six matches without defeat to start the season, a second in succession will only add to Everton’s concerns after confirmation that the club’s American owners want out.

“It was always going to be hard after conceding the early goal,” said Moyes, whose solitary victory at the Emirates was as West Ham’s manager in 2023. “I want us to challenge the top teams but it’s difficult when you see the strength of their bench.”

Everton’s record at this stadium is almost as bad as their manager’s. They arrived in north London having won twice in 35 matches here and had to do without Jarrad Branthwaite and Jack Grealish, who was ruled out with illness. It did not bode well for them when Arsenal took the lead in the seventh minute with a third corner in succession.

View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa (No 15) squeezes the ball home for Arsenal’s early first goal against Everton. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Gabriel made the crucial first contact at the near post and Jordan Pickford tipped the ball on to the crossbar, only for Vitaliy Mykolenko’s failed clearance under pressure from Viktor Gyökeres to allow Konsa to ram home from close range. After a record-breaking 25 goals from set pieces last year, it was their first of the this campaign.

It was a measure of Arsenal’s exertions against Bayern Munich on Wednesday that Arteta rotated his side more than usual for a Premier League match, making five changes.

Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke spurned good opportunities to extend the lead in front of the watching England head coach, Thomas Tuchel. The latter was left out of the last squad, but could well benefit from Bukayo Saka’s expected long absence due to a thigh injury. He was inches away with an instinctive effort with his right foot from the edge of the area on the half-hour mark and was consistently Arsenal’s most dangerous threat.

Everton must have feared the worst as yet another Arsenal corner - 10 during the first half - was launched into the area. Yet the defence just about stood firm.

A moment’s lapse of concentration from Ben White just before half-time almost gave Everton an equaliser but Thierno Barry could not get enough on his attempt to flick the ball past David Raya in their clearest opening.

Gyökeres looked determined to make an impression on his first Premier League start of the season but the Sweden striker, who has yet to score for his club this season, looked laboured.

Quick Guide Arsenal 2-0 Everton key facts Show • With both Arsenal and Manchester City doing so this season, this is just the third top-flight campaign to have two teams win at least seven of their opening eight matches after 1892-93 (Preston and Sunderland) and 1913-14 (Blackburn and Manchester United). • This was David Moyes’s 400th defeat across all competitions in his managerial career with all clubs. 31 of these have come against Arsenal, more than against any other opponent. • The opener from Ezri Konsa (pictured celebrating) was Arsenal’s first set piece goal (excluding penalties) since May against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one. Opta Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

He could not believe it when Tony Harrington penalised him for a foul on James Tarkowski and a sheepish Arteta earned himself a booking for protesting. Unsurprisingly, Gyökeres’s number was up soon after as Arsenal turned to their bench.

It took less than 60 seconds for Gabriel to head in at the back post as White offered Tuchel a timely reminder of his qualities with a brilliant cross.

Moyes’s frustration meant he joined Arteta in the referee’s notebook. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall could have made things interesting but his header fizzed just wide of a post.

Arsenal are now breathing down City’s necks, although whether this title race lasts the course remains unknown.

Sports.title: Fulham climb out of drop zone after Oscar Bobb’s late show sinks Coventry
Sports.content:
Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a win against Coventry that lifted Álvaro Arbeloa’s side clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to score in the 80th minute, twisting his way into the area and bending a shot into the far corner. It was his second goal for the club since his £27m move from Manchester City in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by beating Hull 1-0.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s team second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon that bought the Coventry fans back down to earth after their 4-1 win against Newcastle in their previous home match.

Quality was in short supply between two teams who started the day in the bottom three. King should have broken the deadlock in the 18th minute when afforded too much space in the box, but his powerful shot rebounded off the top of the upright before Alex Iwobi sent a wild follow-up effort high and wide.

At the other end, Bobby Thomas met Jack Rudoni’s free-kick but got his angles all wrong as he headed well wide, before Brandon Thomas-Asante missed from Jay Dasilva’s cross after a good run forward from Rudoni.

A mis-hit back pass from Antonee Robinson offered Thomas-Asante another chance but his shot lacked power as Leno easily gathered.

View image in fullscreen Ephron Mason-Clark is denied by the Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

While Coventry were piling up half-chances Fulham were the ones bossing possession but, in keeping with their season so far, struggling to turn that dominance into goals. The Coventry defender Milan van Ewijk almost helped them out, deflecting Robinson’s low cross dangerously close to his own goal as it found the side-netting.

Just before the break Calvin Bassey went down in the box claiming a shirt-pull from Thomas-Asante, but the referee Adam Herczeg waved play on with replays suggesting they each had a hold of the other.

The video assistant referee had taken a look, and was involved again early in the second half when Rudoni’s free-kick from the right struck Iwobi on the arm before he cleared, but the Nigerian’s arms were by his side and play was waved on.

Coventry then suffered a major blow when the in-form Thomas, praised by Lampard in midweek, hobbled off just before the hour, replaced by the teenage Manchester City loanee Stephen Mfuni.

The hosts were starting to build some momentum after a series of substitutions but it swiftly ended as Bobb struck with 10 minutes to go.

Coventry tried to respond but a powerful strike from Matt Grimes was blocked and a late penalty appeal for handball against Shea Charles was waved away with the midfielder having had his arm tucked in.

Sports.title: Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSL
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo’s contentious second-half penalty delivered relief, a reprieve and a chance for a reset as Arsenal came from a goal down to earn their second win of the WSL season in the north London derby.

At a rain-lashed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Gunners were again their own worst enemy, forced to come from behind after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener. Georgia Stanway levelled and Russo powered in the penalty that gave them the lead they protected defiantly.

The Tottenham manager, Martin Ho, queried the penalty decision, with the ball hitting the raised arm of substitute Ella Morris from the clearance of one of her teammates. “My interpretation of the rule is if your teammate hits it and it hits your player, if you’re one yard away, the time and distance is taken into account, so there’s no penalty,” he said. “That’s my understanding of it, from when we were told to start the season. I want to understand what they’re saying, because then I can accept the decision.

“I don’t want the game to be about that, but when it decides a game it’s frustrating because it’s not within the law of the game.”

Arsenal’s manager, Renée Slegers, said she was glad to give the fans a win. “They sing us and fight us through the game,” she said. “At the end it’s scrappy, it’s game management and it’s scenarios, and they’re all with us.”

With the pressure building on her and her players after five games without a win, at times it felt like they were trying to disprove the phrase “you can’t dig yourself out of a hole”.

Arsenal had looked a little shaky in the opening few minutes but they settled, built possession and started to pose a threat. A failure to carve out clearcut chances and capitalise on any period of dominance has been the running theme of their season. They lacked fight and there was sloppiness too, with too many overhit passes putting the ball out of play or giving away possession.

That the opener came from a Tottenham corner was unsurprising. Victoria Pelova swung the ball in and Tandberg rose above her two markers, Stanway and Emily Fox, who failed to even to jump and challenge, and headed home.

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway equalises for Arsenal in the 17th minute. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

Spurs’ joy was short lived as Stanway made up for her marking error four minutes later by arriving to meet Russo’s cut back and powered the ball in off the crossbar.

After the break there was concern for Tottenham when Alice Sombath’s leg seemed to twist awkwardly as she stretched for the ball. The club’s record signing left on a stretcher to be replaced by Morris, who made her return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury towards the end of last season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

After the lengthy stoppage, Russo forced a huge save from Lize Kop as she attempted to turn in Caitlin Foord’s cross from close range, the forward putting her hands to her head and screaming in frustration at the missed opportunity.

It did not take long for that frustration to transform into elation. The resulting corner from Kyra Cooney-Cross was headed on by Leah Williamson at the near post and Lisa Baum’s effort came back off the post. Spurs’ clearance bounced off the raised arm of Morris and the referee pointed to the spot. Russo sent Kop the wrong way and drove the ball low into the corner.

Arsenal were clinging on as the final whistle loomed but they had “found their fight,” said Slegers. “We had a run of games where results haven’t been good enough. It was frustrating for everyone. I’m so happy we got to win on this occasion, in the north London derby, away from home in the rain and we showed that character in the team.

“This will definitely energise us. We need to back this up in the next couple of games.”

Sports.title: Nicolas Jackson double sees Aston Villa end Manchester City’s perfect start
Sports.content:
Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland.

City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca.

Zion Suzuki deserves almost as much credit as Jackson, making numerous saves to keep City at bay. On a day when there was little between the teams, those at either end of the pitch for Villa made the difference.

Aston Villa started at lightning pace while City cowered. City were so ponderous in the opening stages they even gave away a corner after being penalised for taking too long over a goal kick. After two mistakes gifted Ipswich goals last Saturday, Guéhi would have hoped for a more reassured performance but he was once again punished for the opener, miscontrolling a Rúben Dias pass to allow Jackson in, with the striker rifling home in the sixth minute.

City did not look like a side that had won every Premier League game thus far. The hosts, on the other hand, had forgotten their mid-table tag and were more reflective of the team sitting second in the Champions League standings with three wins out of three.

The inflatable fruit enthusiasts got to witness an improving situation on the pitch as City enjoyed plenty of possession in and around the Villa area, but Iliman Ndiaye, who had a penalty claim waved away, and Rayan Cherki, were thwarted by Suzuki’s reactions. Villa defended with commitment and discipline to limit the space available with great success, proving Unai Emery’s tactical acumen, doubling up on City’s wingers to keep them as subdued as possible.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland rises the highest to equalise for Manchester City. Photograph: Ed Sykes/Getty Images/Sportsphoto/Allstar

While City constantly threatened and Ndiaye struck a post, there was always a nagging doubt Villa could cause problems on the counterattack. Jackson against the unfortunate Guéhi was starting to look like a mismatch with the defender unable to cope with the speed and physicality of the striker. Guéhi was booked for pulling down Jackson on the edge of the area to leave him in a precarious position before he was replaced at the break.

Quick Guide Aston Villa 2-1 Manchester City key facts Show • Aston Villa are the first side to win three successive Premier League games against Manchester City since Liverpool in December 2016 (run of four). • Three of Manchester City’s last five Premier League defeats have come against Aston Villa, while they have lost four successive away league games to a side for the first time since February 2023 against Tottenham Hotspur. • Erling Haaland (pictured) has scored in each of his last seven Premier League appearances; it’s his joint-longest run in the competition along with between August and October 2022. • After conceding eight goals in their opening nine matches of the 2026-27 season in all competitions, Manchester City have since conceded nine times across their last four games. Opta Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The entertainment and exhilaration of the first half was always going to be difficult to sustain, but there was no backing down from either side. City’s endeavour was rewarded in the 53rd minute when Ndiaye got the better of Ian Maatsen and found Haaland who headed home from close range for his 13th of the season. It is hard to keep that man quiet.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There was a sense City could take control and went close through Josko Gvardiol and Jérémy Doku. Villa responded by moving the ball quickly from back to front, with Jackson sending a pass out to Ibrahim Mbaye before getting on the end of the cross for his second. Donnarumma should have done better, letting the ball slip under him.

Phil Foden, Rico Lewis and Ryan McAidoo were sent on to change things for the visitors and they provided energy but, despite dominating possession, passes and crosses were misdirected and needless bookings were collected. If City could point to perfection before this, the label was rapidly fading.

Jackson went off with eight minutes remaining to a standing ovation. Haaland had a very late chance to level, but Maatsen cleared off the line, to ensure Jackson and Villa claimed the glory, while City were left to ponder their flaws.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
Sports.content:
Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham. Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers.

Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham.

“We started not the way we wanted,” said Nuno. “We were looking at the situations with hesitation, bouncing balls, too many chances for Southampton to have a second phase, third phase and achieve a goal. But the reaction was good in the second half. The boys fought until the end.”

Richard Kone made an emphatic return to form by scoring a hat-trick inside 15 minutes as QPR thrashed high-flying Swansea 5-0 at Loftus Road. Jimmy Dunne struck twice for Rangers, who were four up at half-time, as the Swans – who were top of the Championship until Friday night – suffered their second defeat in a row. The Welsh side remain second in the table, while QPR’s resounding victory moved them back into the playoff positions in eighth.

View image in fullscreen Richard Kone reacts after putting QPR ahead against Swansea. Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PA

Adam Armstrong ended his goal drought with a milestone strike to give dominant Wolves a 1-0 win against Watford at Molineux. The 29-year-old striker, returning after a back injury, scored only his second league goal of the season, while it was his first Championship home goal for Wolves, all on his 450th league appearance.

Wolves, though, failed to turn their overwhelming superiority into goals, and the unease around Molineux was evident when the 78th-minute double substitution of Tommy Doyle and Tawanda Chirewa for Jordan James and Armstrong was met with chants of “you don’t know what you’re doing” aimed at the head coach, César Peixoto.

Quick Guide League One roundup: Huddersfield top; Foxes lose again Show Huddersfield went top of League One after their 2-1 win over bottom side Wigan in the early game was followed by Stockport dropping points. Ilias Bronkhorst and Derensili Sanches Fernandes scored for the Terriers in the first half, with Christian Saydee’s consolation coming in added time. Although Stockport secured a 1-1 draw at Notts County after Adama Sidibeh’s 81st-minute equaliser cancelled out Scott Robertson’s opener, it was not enough to return them to the top. Plymouth moved into fourth, just a point behind Stockport, with a 3-2 win seeing them leapfrog hosts Cambridge after Louis Appere’s own goal was followed by strikes from Xavier Amaechi and Aribim Pepple. Leicester dramatically fell to their fourth defeat of the season to increase pressure on manager Russell Martin. Luton’s Callum Marshall scored deep into added time after Liam Cullen had levelled in the 90th minute, just after Leicester’s John Lundstram was sent off for a second yellow card following Nahki Wells’ first-half opener. Martin said: “We did so well to get ourselves back in the game with 10 men, it’s so disappointing. Within a couple of minutes, the feeling can be so different. It can feel like a win almost, down to 10 men, a battling draw, brilliant goal and then we concede a goal and it’s frustration. It was the only time they entered our box really, and we gave a goal away. We gave away two poor goals today and that’s frustration.” Doncaster’s Owen Bailey scored twice in the first 14 minutes to win the South Yorkshire derby 2-0 against Sheffield Wednesday. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The substitute Aune Heggebo struck late for West Brom to deny Preston a first win under Graham Alexander in a 1-1 draw at a wind-swept Deepdale. The Norwegian came off the bench on the hour and rifled home an 82nd-minute leveller just four minutes after Andrew Hughes hooked North End into the lead from a corner.

Nicky Hayen’s future as Burnley manager is increasingly in doubt after his side slumped to a 4-1 defeat at Lincoln. Burnley went in front through Andreas Hountondji but Ben House equalised on the stroke of half-time. Hayen’s side then fell apart in the second half, with Mikkel Ladefoged scoring twice, either side of a goal from Dom Jefferies. With their team in the bottom three, Burnley fans targeted Hayen and the board with banners and chants.

Hayen said later: “It’s frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn’t matter because it’s another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops. I know it’s a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board.”

Cardiff halted Birmingham’s winning run as Yousef Salech secured a 1-0 victory to continue the Bluebirds’ climb up the table. Salech was named among the home substitutes initially, but the defender Krystian Bielik suffered an injury in the warm-up and had to drop out on an afternoon of relentless rain in the Welsh capital. Cardiff have now recorded three straight home wins as they continue to show real signs of adapting to life in the second tier following promotion from League One.

Andri Gudjohnsen’s second double in a week earned Blackburn a clinical 2-0 win over Wrexham. The Icelandic striker’s return from injury has coincided with an upturn in Rovers’ results as goals in each half delivered a third win in five games that moves Tony Mowbray’s side to within two points of the playoff spots.

View image in fullscreen Andri Gudjohnsen puts Blackburn ahead against Wrexham at Ewood Park. Photograph: Nigel French/PA

Chris Wilder was critical of his Sheffield United side’s “annoying” first-half performance after they had to settle for a point from a 1-1 draw with struggling Derby. Bobby Clark gave the Rams a first-half lead with Patrick Bamford equalising in the closing stages, while Derby had Dion Sanderson sent off in the 66th minute after he received a second booking. Wilder said: “We gave them the game that they wanted. Everybody’s brother was playing first half apart from Kalvin [Phillips] and Coops [Michael Cooper].”

John Mousinho admitted Portsmouth did not deserve to win after coming from behind to beat Millwall 2-1 in a game of freak goals at a blustery Fratton Park. Jenson Metcalfe put Millwall ahead on six minutes after a calamitous pass forward from the Pompey goalkeeper, Nicolas Schmid, and, 10 minutes later, Lyndon Dykes turned the ball into his own net for 1-1. Then, eight minutes from time, an attempted clearance from Millwall’s captain, Jake Cooper, ricocheted off the substitute Thomas Waddingham and into the net for the winner.

Quick Guide League Two roundup: Barnet held; Cheltenham go third Show Barnet missed the chance to cut the gap to League Two leaders Salford to a point after Oldham’s Mike Fondop’s header in the fourth minute of added time cancelled out Kabongo Tshimanga’s opener in a 1-1 draw. Cheltenham moved into third, a point behind the Bees, with Charlie McCann’s fifth-minute goal enough to end Newport’s nine-game unbeaten run. Rotherham moved out of the bottom two in an incident-packed 3-3 draw after playing over an hour with 10 men against a Shrewsbury side who also had Kian McMahon-Brown sent off late on. Paul Mullin scored twice before Kian Spence was shown a red card, allowing Josh Davison, Josh Ruffels and Will Boyle to put the visitors ahead with 23 minutes remaining. However, substitute Tom Bradshaw scored the Millers’ third before Brown was dismissed for an off-the-ball incident with Joe Rafferty. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“This is the first time this season we’ve got away with one,” said Mousinho. “We were lucky to nick the win off a poor start to the second half and the defending in the first half. But we stuck in it and did everything else really well.”

Philippe Clement saluted the never-say-die attitude of his Norwich players after a 3-1 comeback win at Charlton. The Canaries, on a run of six straight defeats in league and cup heading to the Valley, fell behind to a Charlie Kelman goal. But Paris Maghoma equalised and Mathias Kvistgaarden fired them ahead, before Ivan Mesik’s own goal completed the turnaround.

Stoke and Bristol City played out a 0-0 draw in wet and windy conditions, while on Friday, Will Lankshear scored twice as a Middlesbrough battered Bolton 5-1. Aidan Morris, in-form Lankshear and a Lewis Brunt own goal before half-time set the Teessiders on the way to a 10th successive win over their hosts in a run stretching back to 2014.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.

Saints started the second half brightly but goals from Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by referee Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on midfielder Nico Raskin, before substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.

McInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.

Celtic can restore their four-point advantage when they travel to Hibernian, the bottom side, at noon GMT on Sunday.

Dundee United won a rollercoaster game 3-2 against Aberdeen at Tannadice. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.

United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behind Hearts, who are at Motherwell on Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.

Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh with a 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header. St Mirren ended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory over Dundee with goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition.

Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined.

“Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We’re not starting to put together any timeframes. We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we’ll discuss calmly what recovery time is to be. We won’t be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that.”

Taking Saturday’s press conference in Kompany’s absence, Danks said he had spoken with the former centre-back briefly on Friday but only to wish him well. “I explained to him that we wouldn’t be having no football conversations. It was just checking in on his health and making sure he’s OK.”

Danks added: “All the football operations are in our hands and we’ll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward.”

Bayern’s second team’s game was postponed on Friday after Kompany’s collapse but Eberl said the club did not consider trying to postpone Sunday’s Bundesliga game. “I think the greatest joy for Vinnie would be for us to play well tomorrow and, ideally, get a positive result,” Eberl said. “That would probably be one of the best things we could do to help him recover.”

Danks confirmed the Germany captain, Joshua Kimmich, who has been on bereavement leave since Tuesday, would also miss Sunday’s game.

Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday’s home Champions League 2-2 draw with Arsenal despite missing the pre-match press conference due to the virus. Speaking after the Arsenal game, Kompany said his body reacted after he tried to push through the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body – and then at some point my body just said: ‘Enough is enough!’”

The defending champions are top of the Bundesliga table at the start of the weekend, level on 14 points with Borussia Dortmund and one ahead of Freiburg and Leverkusen. Bayern’s next Champions League match is on 3 November in Spain against Atlético Madrid.

Sports.title: Arsenal rediscover magic touch at corners as Ezri Konsa and Gabriel punish wasteful Everton and move Gunners level at top with Man City
Sports.content:
Arsenal rediscover magic touch at corners as Ezri Konsa and Gabriel punish wasteful Everton and move Gunners level at top with Man City

A well-worn Arsenal blueprint from previous seasons had finally resurfaced. It was only a matter time before Mikel Arteta’s team of 6ft-plus giants would, inevitably, turn to set-pieces; the rich supply method of goals which previously often decided or prised open matches.

Having not scored from a corner so far this season, the ploy was back, and emphatically so. Odegaard’s floated corner on seven minutes — Arsenal’s third in quick succession — reached Gabriel in the mix, who headed goalward.

The ball gently brushed Jordan Pickford’s fingertips onto the crossbar, falling to Ezri Konsa near the back post amid a sea of Everton bodies. He prodded home to register the Gunners first set-piece goal of the season.

By this stage last season, they were already on six and finished the campaign on a record-breaking 19. Rivals branded them ‘Set Piece FC’ but it’s not been heard around these parts since May.

To their credit, the Gunners were dominant. Whether a rain-sodden Arteta was trying to mount a defence against the recent ‘Unwatchables’ accusations after last weekend’s drab victory against Nottingham Forest, his team certainly made a mockery of that jibe.

The north London club typically found themselves camped outside the opposition’s box, trying to force their way through a low block and peppered their visitors goal with 18 shots.

Gabriel sealed victory for Arsenal with a second-half header

Gabriel rose highest to connect with a Ben White cross to score his first of the season

The Toffees hadn’t surrendered, keen to mount counter-attacks through the pacey Thierno Barry but were overwhelmed by a relentless red-and-white wave. Gabriel, making his 200th appearance, typified Arsenal’s resilience.

Having gone down in agony on 56 minutes after overstretching himself on a clearance, the medical team helped usher the Brazilian off the field. Cristhian Mosquera began to ready himself on the bench.

Gabriel saw this and did some stretches on the touchline, making it known he would not be subbed off. Ten minutes after re-entering the pitch, he latched onto Ben White’s cross to double Arsenal’s lead with a powerful header.

There’s a never-say-die spirit in this team, which makes them so hard to beat. Arteta had rung the changes, bringing in Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino for their first Premier League starts of the season.

The manager is also taking rotation seriously, too. In the previous campaign, certain positions were pretty much fixed, no matter the circumstances. Martin Zubimendi started 34 of the 38 league matches but was, tellingly, on the bench again here. This time around, Arteta has shown a willingness to give players a break where possible. It’s a sensible and needed evolution for the Spaniard; if Bukayo Saka’s recent thigh injury wasn’t a warning sign, then not much else would be.

Arsenal got off to a rampant start, taking no mercy against an Everton side who had only lost once in the league this season. Noni Madueke, a player whose end product had been under scrutiny, impressed with his dribbling skill and intent. He marched forward, only looking in one direction — forward.

He’s a handful to deal with when full of confidence and, after starting the 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich midweek, Madueke was in full flow.

Ezri Konsa had opened the scoring for the Gunners from a corner

The winger sat an Everton player down on the turf with a swift pivot, his neat cross to Gyokeres desperately cleared. On another occasion, he swivelled just outside the area, before shooting into the side netting.

Odegaard played the conductor role, looking for sharp passes through the opposition’s backline. Five minutes before the break, five Everton shirts circled him, the Norwegian using his dancing feet to get around and go close with his strike.

Eberechi Eze attracted applause for a neat touch from a sky-high ball, which was to be superseded by Max Dowman’s introduction on 80 minutes. The memories of his match-saving display last March against the Toffees, featuring a game-changing cross and a goal, has not been forgotten.

By the time Gabriel’s goal went in, the game was already meandering to a close. Merlin Rohl’s cross momentarily gave David Raya a scare, the ball just curling high and wide from the goalframe. That mattered not. Set-pieces are back on the Arsenal table. Future opponents ought to be wary.
