Sports.title: Tiger Woods poses with girlfriend Vanessa Trump in rare picture after announcing she is now cancer-free
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods has posed for a rare picture with his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, celebrating the news she is now cancer-free.

The legendary golfer and President Trump's former daughter-in-law went public with their romance in March 2025, sharing two loved up pictures.

She supported him as he appeared in court in March and accepted a plea deal in his DUI case after a car crash in Florida, while she also attended a TGL golf event with him last year.

But pictures of the pair together have been few and far between, with the couple declining to share any images since from their personal life.

However, they made an exception to pose celebrating Vanessa getting the all-clear from breast cancer.

In her latest YouTube vlog, Vanessa's daughter, Kai, who went to the same high school as Tiger's son Charlie, shared a picture of the family after her big news.

Kai Trump shared a photo of Tiger Woods with Vanessa celebrating her all-clear from cancer

Vanessa Trump has revealed that she is cancer free in a video alongside daughter Kai

Tiger and Vanessa Trump shared this photo in March 2025 as they confirmed their romance

Tiger and Vanessa stood with her two eldest children, Kai and Donald Trump III, with the bell she rang to mark getting the all clear beneath a 'congratulations' banner.

The 48-year-old Vanessa appeared alongside Kai in a lengthy video with Dr Nicole Saphier, for Breast Cancer Awareness month discussing her journey.

In a short teaser video shared to Instagram on Friday, Kai began: 'My mom was diagnosed with breast cancer in April.

'So we thought we would share her story and how she was diagnosed and how she overcame it.'

Vanessa appeared back on screen and shared: '[Tests] came back clear so I am finally cancer free,' as the mother-daughter duo exchanged a hug.

The mother-of-five had publicly announced in May that she was diagnosed with breast cancer.

Vanessa, the ex-wife of President Trump's eldest son, Don Jr, said at the time that she had undergone a 'procedure.'

'I want to share a personal health update. I've recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. While this isn't news anyone expects, I'm working closely with my medical team on a treatment plan,' she said.

Woods and Vanessa also shared a loved-up picture lying in a hammock in their first post

Vanessa Trump supported Woods in court in March as he took a plea deal in his DUI case

Vanessa also attended a TGL match in March supporting Woods in his new golf venture

'I am staying focused and hopeful while surrounded by the love and support of my family, my kids and those closest to me.

'Thank you for your kindness and support, it truly means more than I can express.'

In June, Vanessa issued a second statement that she was recovering from surgery and preparing to begin the next stage of treatment.

Kai has been candid about her mom's health journey after previously opening up about how the diagnosis gave them an opportunity to spend more time together over the summer.

Speaking to Fox News from the University of Miami back in August, she explained: 'I was very lucky to spend a lot of time with her over the summer, because of cancer and going to treatments with her.

'It was a blessing in disguise, because I was able to spend extra time with her that I would normally probably spend on the golf course.

'It was nice to spend those extra hours with her throughout the day before going to college.'

Sports.title: England bad boy Henry Pollock at centre of 30-MAN brawl and is grabbed around the neck by Ollie Chessum in feisty derby as Leicester beat Northampton
Sports.content:
England bad boy Henry Pollock at centre of 30-MAN brawl and is grabbed around the neck by Ollie Chessum in feisty derby as Leicester beat Northampton

Days after adorning the front cover of Tatler alongside fashion royalty in Valentina Pinault, Henry Pollock was the at the centre of a 30-man scrap in the driving rain at Welford Road.

By the end of this East Midlands derby clash between two bitter rivals, which was played both in a white-hot atmosphere and awful conditions, Pollock could have been forgiven for wishing he was back on the set of a glossy magazine photoshoot. He and Northampton endured more Welford Road misery.

At the same venue where he so noticeably imploded as his team were hammered 41-19 in this fixture last season, Pollock was substituted in just the 53rd minute after being at the centre of a mass brawl on the half-time whistle.

Pollock did nothing initially to provoke Leicester angst. But he then attempted to delay the teams entering the tunnel by looking to tie his laces. English rugby’s most talked about player always seems to find himself in the centre of the action, even if here, it was in defeat.

Leicester were deserved 28-7 victors, edging their bitter rivals through a significant raise in their physicality and basic skill level after the break and a dominant scrum. ‘Maybe we would have played even better in the second half if it (the half time fight) hadn't happened,’ said a delighted Leicester head coach Geoff Parling. ‘Can that fire you up? Yes, it can do.

Henry Pollock found himself at the centre of a 30-man brawl in Northampton's clash with Leicester

The England No 8 appeared to be grabbed around the neck by Red Rose captain Ollie Chessum

The argument continued down the tunnel at half-time, where Chessum repeatedly pushed Pollock

Meet Henry Pollock, rugby's golden boy with charm, ambition and invitations to spare, as he graces the cover of Tatler's latest issuehttps://t.co/FGDJVKQBPp pic.twitter.com/T8ACjZtSaq — Tatler (@Tatlermagazine) October 23, 2026

‘But it's not something to rely on and I didn’t think we would. I was already in the changing room (when it happened). It was honestly the calmest changing room you could think of.’

Pollock sheltered himself from the pre-match rain through the use of a snood. He warmed up with some keepy-uppies. Leicester were bang up for battle. Gabriel Hamer-Webb encouraged the home crowd. The brilliant Freddie Steward paced the field like a prized fighter.

The wet weather meant this was always going to be a dogfight and so it proved. Pollock was straight into the action with an early carry, as was his No 10 team-mate Fin Smith who was smashed back by a double Leicester tackle. Smith spent the rest of his game limping, but he was still able to chip for James Pater to open the scoring.

Playing with a penalty advantage, Smith’s kick was a shot to nothing. But it worked wonderfully as his opposite number Bily Searle couldn’t collect. Saints were playing into a strong wind, one proved when Steward put Leicester on the board with a monster penalty from just inside his opposition’s half.

Otherwise, constant errors and the whistle of referee Craig Maxwell-Keys dominated the encounter. The first half ended with a mass melee between both teams, sparked by Saints No 9 Alex Mitchell.

Pollock clashed with Leicester captain Ollie Chessum and Steward on the entrance to the tunnel. Chessum grabbed Pollock by the throat and pushed him. The fight put Leicester on the path to success and derailed Saints. ‘It’s part of the game. Emotions are high. It’s physical. Everything is in your face and there was a moment just before half time,’ said Steward.

The Tigers were dominant after the break. Pollock smashed Aaron Wainwright, but the Tigers mauled over through Jamie Blamire and their scrum – led by prop star man Joe Heyes – was dominant.

Leicester went onto claim a dominant victory against the reigning Prem champions

Heyes said: ‘It was a pretty hot changing room. We had to calm ourselves down a bit, but it added a bit of fuel to the fire. It means a lot to the locality. These fixtures are awesome. This is the best derby in the country.’

Pollock was removed from the fray with Saints rattled. Pater and Smith spilled balls in the backfield. Leicester’s scrum was outstanding, giving them the platform from which beanpole lock Cameron Henderson finished spectacularly before Finn Carnduff made it three. Searle couldn’t convert either but did kick a simple penalty and that was that.

Tom Lockett’s yellow card for a dangerous tackle, which earned Leicester wing Adam Radwan a yellow card reprieve, summed up Northampton’s day and there was still time for Steward to give Leicester a bonus-point through their fourth try. Steward jumped for joy. So too did the home crowd.

‘These games are going to be hostile,’ said beaten Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson. ‘In the current game you can’t throw anything (punches). It's just push and shove. I don't think that had any impact. Leicester were very good after half time.’

Sports.title: England defender Marc Guehi rejects the knee AGAIN: Man City star doubles down against anti-racism gesture after suggesting it had 'lost its meaning' - as Chelsea fans boo gesture before Spurs clash at Stamford Bridge
Sports.content:
England and Man City star Marc Guehi has refused to take the knee for the second week running.

Guehi, alongside Ipswich Town's Issa Diop, Everton's Ainsley Maitland-Niles, Leeds' Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Bournemouth's Rayan and Tyler Adams, remained standing when the Premier League rolled out its 'No Room for Racism' initiative last weekend.

Footballers in England's top flight have been given the opportunity to take the knee across two weekends this month in an effort to challenge discrimination.

The gesture was also met by a smattering of boos ahead of Tottenham's clash with Chelsea at Stamford Bridge later on Saturday.

Guehi, who this week suggested taking the knee had 'lost its meaning', refused to kneel before kick-off at Villa Park today as league leaders City took on Aston Villa, instead he remained standing and clapped.

When asked whether he had spoken to his players about taking the knee, City boss Enzo Maresca said: 'No, the players are already aware of the information.'

Marc Guehi refused to kneel for the second week running on Saturday

Issa Diop (right) can be seen standing while other players take the knee prior to Ipswich Town's clash with Nottingham Forest on Friday night

Every other player on the pitch at Portman Road took the knee while Diop remained standing

The England star's stance also followed Diop, who doubled down last night when Ipswich hosted Nottingham Forest at Portman Road.

Diop was the only player among the 22 on the pitch to remain standing as Forest's starters and his own team-mates all opted to take part.

Diop has not spoken publicly about his stance but the move has divided players, some of whom view it as a hollow gesture.

Maitland-Niles was named on the bench for Everton's trip to Arsenal, so was not on the field of play when the players observed the anti-racism gesture.

When asked about Calvert-Lewin's viewpoint last week, Leeds manager Daniel Farke explained his striker's thinking, saying: 'Dom is more or less like, "No, I don't go down. I show my respect by standing up."

'Every individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way. It's definitely a good campaign and a good topic that football and sports, in general, support situations like this because a dressing room is a perfect example of how we should all live together.

'Different passports, different languages, different religions, but they are all together as human beings and friends who work together toward one target. This is how the world should be.'

The campaign was previously enacted before every game until it stopped in August 2022 having been started in the UK in 2020 following the death of George Floyd in US police custody, which sparked the Black Lives Matter movement.

Subsequently, a decision was made to limit the gesture to match rounds falling during the No Room For Racism initiative.

It was agreed ahead of the season among Premier League captains that they would continue to perform the gesture twice over 38 rounds.

While the vast majority of players have taken part, some strong opposition has been voiced, notably by Wilfried Zaha in 2021, who said: 'I feel like taking the knee is degrading, because growing up my parents just let me know that I should be proud to be black no matter what and I feel like we should just stand tall.'

And last year, the Lionesses chose not to kneel before their Euro 2025 semi-final against Italy following racist abuse aimed at defender Jess Carter on social media.

Captain Lucy Bronze said the anti-racism message is not 'as strong as it used to be' following the abuse of her team-mate.

'It was driven by the group – obviously certain individuals more than others,' Bronze explained. 'I think it was just the fact that we feel as a collective, is the message as strong as it used to be? Is the message really hitting hard? Because to us it feels like it's not if these things are still happening to our players in the biggest tournaments of their lives.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles was one of six Premier League players who refused to take the knee last weekend, pictured standing ahead of Everton's 2-0 defeat against Chelsea on Saturday

'It's about putting another statement out there to say, it's something that still is a problem, it's something that still needs to be put right. More needs to be done in football, more needs to be done in society. What that is right now as an individual, I don't exactly know.'

But the head of football's international anti-discrimination body, Fare, questioned the Lionesses' decision to stop taking the knee.

Piara Powar told BBC Sport: 'The players have taken a decision to stop taking the knee, which is their right.

'Personally don't see the link between the two. The taking of the knee is a powerful anti-racist act and this England team have shown leadership across Europe in taking it for so long.

'Powerful actions are needed right now, to deal with the issues that are being played out as we speak.'

Sports.title: Max Verstappen fumes at 'unacceptable' Austin track for US Grand Prix: Red Bull star warns track is 'out of control' and insists drivers' concerns have been IGNORED
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen fumes at 'unacceptable' Austin track for US Grand Prix: Red Bull star warns track is 'out of control' and insists drivers' concerns have been IGNORED

Max Verstappen has said that the ‘unacceptable’ Austin track, home of this weekend’s US Grand Prix, is damaging his spine because it is too bumpy.

The four-time world champion revealed that he and his fellow drivers have complained to the governing FIA about the condition of the Circuit of the Americas layout and asked for solutions but reported that their requests had not been resolved.

He described the circuit, which is 15 miles southeast of Downtown, as ‘out of control’.

‘I love this track, I love this place,’ said the Dutchman. ‘It’s one of the best, one of the best venues, one of the best cities to be at.

‘But the bumps are unacceptable. Over time they’ve found a bit of a solution here and there, but it’s just putting a plaster on the bigger problem.

‘You need to open up the track fully (to sort it out). That costs a lot of money and time but that’s the only way to get rid of it because these bumps are not natural.’

Max Verstappen has complained about the Austin track ahead of the US Grand Prix

The circuit, which hosted its first race 14 years ago, is built on marshland, and was designed by German Hermann Tilke, then the go-to man for such projects.

Verstappen, 29, added: ‘You can say soil is the problem, but you need to make sure you reinforce it more.’

Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli, just 20, can win the title here in the US if he extends his lead from 102 points to 125 with what would then be five rounds remaining.

Sports.title: Man City's perfect record is over and now we'll see what Enzo Maresca's side are really made of, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - it's easy to ignore the storm when you're winning, but dark clouds loom after Aston Villa defeat
Sports.content:
Man City's perfect record is over and now we'll see what Enzo Maresca's side are really made of, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - it's easy to ignore the storm when you're winning, but dark clouds loom after Aston Villa defeat

Come on then, Enzo. Let’s see what you’ve got now.

Until lunchtime on Saturday, Manchester City had shown no signs of being affected by the chaos engulfing the club as Enzo Maresca’s men reeled off seven straight Premier League wins. We will know soon enough whether Aston Villa’s fourth straight home victory over City has broken the spell.

It easy enough to block out the noise when you win every league game. Easy to forget your club’s ongoing battle with the Premier League after they were found guilty of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 – a verdict City have appealed.

These players and coaches would not be human, though, if they had been able to avoid worrying about the future. What if our appeal fails? Will we be relegated? If so, how far? What happens to our contracts? Our careers? City’s next fixture, at home to the impressive Brighton, may tell us a great deal about what is to come.

Troubling times for City, and no less unsettling for the Premier League. Because if City escape on a technicality, what then? The damage to the competition’s image would be colossal. Please, just let the verdict be swift.

Nicolas Jackson scored twice to power Aston Villa to victory and inflict Manchester City's first Premier League defeat of the season

City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma was at fault for Jackson's winner after letting the ball slip up his body

City did not play badly here. They hit the frame of the goal twice through Iliman Ndiaye and Josko Gvardiol and were denied by some outstanding work by Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, who looks one of the buys of the season. So too does Nicolas Jackson, who scored in each half, either side of Erling Haaland’s equaliser. This must have tasted especially sweet for Jackson, who was shoved towards the exit by Maresca at Chelsea a little more than a year ago. Against the world’s best No9, Jackson won the battle of the centre-forward hands down.

Emery: Jackson was shooting like a rugby kicker! Unai Emery claimed that Nicolas Jackson’s shooting had resembled a rugby kicker earlier in the season before roaring into form as Aston Villa ended Manchester City’s perfect start. Jackson’s brace downed the Premier League leaders and the striker now has six goals in his last six games in all competitions following a £65million move from Chelsea in the summer. The 25-year-old has impressed Emery with his grasp of the tactical instructions at Villa and is now repaying the Spaniard’s faith in front of goal. ‘How he was working, how he was defending - wow,’ Emery said. ‘And then he has the power to attack the spaces and the duels. ‘His challenge has been when he can have chances to score [to] always [find] the corner because he was shooting so much in the beginning of the season like up in rugby. ‘He was shooting a lot of balls over the crossbar. He is progressing as well. We need him more running in behind because we need the runners on the field, and one of the runners normally is the striker, and he has quality and power. He’s coachable.’ Gianluigi Donnarumma should have done better with Jackson’s second and Enzo Maresca insisted that City should have left with something from the game. ‘I think we deserved more,’ Maresca said. ‘We haven't been clinical enough in the box. Sometimes when you concede the first goal was mistake, the second goal came from a transition. ‘We spent most of the game in their side, in their box. Sometimes you have to be more clinical but also more precise with the last pass, more accurate. We're going to learn from that.’ JACK GAUGHAN

‘We had many chances,’ said Maresca. ‘We played most of the game in their box but you have to be clinical and avoid mistakes like the two goals we conceded.’

All fair enough, though Maresca must have noticed a softness to City that simply was not there in their greatest days. Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku tormented Villa full-backs Matty Cash and Ian Maatsen throughout and on another occasion, their creativity would have produced more. When it comes to the other end of the pitch, the less said, the better.

Marc Guehi was dragged off at half-time after he was at fault for Jackson’s opener and then picked up a booking for a foul on the Villa forward. Ruben Dias seemed more interested in scrapping with John McGinn than stopping him playing. Enzo Fernandez looked slow and sluggish, a shadow of himself.

Maresca: I'm not worried about Guehi Enzo Maresca insists that he is unfazed by the form of Marc Guehi after another mistake led to Aston Villa's early opener. Guehi – taken off at the break - had also made two errors in victory over Ipswich Town last week. ‘I'm not worried about Marc at all,’ he added. ‘I know he is playing every minute since the season started with us and the national team. ‘It's not easy but the change was also because he was on a yellow card and the way we want to be aggressive sometimes to have one yellow card can be dangerous. But I'm not worried at all.’ JACK GAUGHAN

None of this should detract from Villa or their outstanding coach. Unai Emery has somehow managed to travel under the radar for much of his second spell in English football and has been overlooked by Manchester United twice since he arrived at Villa four years ago.

‘He’s just a tactical genius,’ said Cash. ‘Especially against City at our place, he’s always got a plan for something and he’s always coming up with new ideas.’

The Norwegian rose brilliantly in the box to head home past Zion Suzuki

Erling Haaland scored City's equaliser early in the second-half

MATCH FACTS Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 9; Cash 6, Lindelof 8, Torres 8, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Gomes 7 (Goretzka 82min); Alysson 7 (Mbaye 59, 7), McGinn 8 (Barkley 67, 6), Manzambi 6 (Buendia 67, 6); Jackson 8 (Madjo 82) Scorers: Jackson 6, 60 Booked: Cash, Manzambi, Madjo, Buendia Manager: Unai Emery 8 Manchester City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 6, Dias 5, Guehi 4 (Lewis 46, 6), Gvardiol 6; Anderson 7, Fernandez 5; Ndiaye 7 (McAidoo 69, 6), Cherki 6 (Foden 46, 6), Doku 8; Haaland 7. Scorers: Haaland 53 Booked: Guehi, Cherki, Anderson, McAidoo Manager: Enzo Maresca 6 Referee: Peter Bankes 6 Attendance: 36,743

Consider what Emery has had to handle since lifting the Europa League last May. Six of the starting XI from the Final against Freiburg have departed, leaving a squad needing a total rebuild. Daily Mail Sport has been critical before of Villa’s haphazard recruitment but this time they have nailed it.

Suzuki and Jackson have been two of the best in their positions this season. Though he did not have his best day against City, Johan Manzambi looks a £100million footballer in the making. Ibrahim Mbaye came on as a second-half substitute and promptly created the winner for his Senegal team-mate Jackson. At 25, Jackson is the oldest of the quartet. Exciting times.

‘This year started so poorly,’ admitted Emery. ‘We needed time to understand how we needed to improve. Today this was a very good test and the players have shown they can recover the level we achieved in recent years.’

City were caught cold by the speed of Villa’s start. The home side were awarded a corner when City delayed a goal-kick too long and in the sixth minute they seized the lead.

Guehi’s poor control allowed McGinn to find Jackson, who was allowed to cut in unchallenged from the left and fire into the roof of the net.

Now the Holte End was in full voice, telling City exactly what they thought of them but Maresca’s team did not wilt. They took control quickly and Ndiaye and Doku were a constant threat on the flanks. Ndiaye forced a fine save from Zion Suzuki and the Villa goalkeeper produced an even better one from Rayan Cherki. Ndiaye would later hit the post and Doku continued to torment Matty Cash.

Jackson capped off a brilliant start to the game for the hosts by putting them ahead

Jackson has now scored seven goals this season since moving from Chelsea in the summer

Haaland touched the ball only eight times in the first half but when it counted, he made his mark. Ndiaye glided past Manzambi and Haaland climbed to head home at the far post soon after the break.

Back came Villa. Less than a minute after coming on as substitute, Mbaye raced on to Jackson’s pass and picked out his team-mate 20 yards from goal. Jackson’s aim was true and Donnarumma allowed the shot to slip through his grasp and into the net. Moments earlier, Suzuki had done brilliantly again to tip Gvardiol’s effort on to the bar.

‘I’m very happy with the manager and my team-mates,’ said Jackson. ‘It’s been easier for me because of the coach and the players. Hopefully I can score many goals for them and it’s just the beginning. Thankfully we got our first win at home in the league.’

Sports.title: Naomi Osaka's ex-boyfriend addresses split from tennis star in new rap song about raising their daughter
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka's ex-boyfriend, rapper Cordae, has seemingly addressed their split in an emotional new song reflecting co-parenting their young daughter.

The 29-year-old artist opened up on the track 'Helpless' featured on his newly released collaborative album with Anderson .Paak titled 'Heavy is the Crown.'

On the track, Cordae reflected candidly on the difficulty of raising their daughter in separate households and seemingly revealed he's expecting a second child.

He said: 'I'm finna [going to] have my second child, although we still ain't said our vows / Was never my intention to raise a daughter in separate homes.

'Gave your mom my all, but the love she had for me dead and gone / Although you ain't a man if you can't admit it when you was wrong / Can't see it coming down my eyes, so do it through this song'.

The candid account marks the first time that Cordae has publicly reflected on his split with the four-time Grand Slam champion.

Naomi Osaka's ex-boyfriend, Cordae, has addressed their split in an emotional new song

Osaka and Cordae began dating in 2019 after crossing paths at a Los Angeles Clippers game

Cordae addresses his breakup with Naomi Osaka on ‘Helpless,’ a track from his new collaborative album with Anderson .Paak:



"I'm finna have my second child, although we still ain't said our vows



Was never my intention to raise my daughter in separate homes

Gavе your mom my all,… — The Tennis Letter (@TheTennisLetter) October 24, 2026

Osaka and Cordae began dating back in 2019 after crossing paths at a Los Angeles Clippers game.

The pair announced they were expecting their first child together in January 2023, welcoming their daughter, Shai, later that July.

However, the tennis superstar confirmed that their relationship had come to an end in January 2025 via a blunt message on her Instagram Story.

'Hi everyone, just wanted to say that Cordae and I are no longer in a relationship', Osaka wrote to her followers at the time.

The Japanese tennis star maintained that their split was entirely amicable, adding: 'No bad blood at all, he's a great person and an awesome dad'.

Osaka appears to remain on supportive terms with her former partner, having recently liked a social media post promoting the release of his new collaborative album.

The album also sees Anderson .Paak confront his own personal turmoil on 'Helpless,' rapping about the fallout of his divorce from Jaylyn Chang following 13 years of marriage.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta fumes at Premier League over 'terrible' fixture schedule after Arsenal win
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta fumes at Premier League over 'terrible' fixture schedule after Arsenal win

Arsenal were tasked with facing Everton less than three full days after taking on Bayern Munich in the Champions League away from home, having also been on the road last Sunday

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is unhappy with the Premier League (Image: Beanyman Sports)

Mikel Arteta took a swipe at the Premier League and bemoaned Arsenal's 'terrible' schedule following their comfortable 2-0 victory over Everton. The Gunners boss was unhappy with how his side were made to play at 3pm on Saturday after an away tie in the Champions League against Bayern Munich on Wednesday, as well as having gone to Nottingham Forest last Sunday.

‌



‌



Arsenal were back on home soil when they welcomed Everton, with goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes earning them all three points. Arteta made five changes from their 2-2 draw with Bayern, one enforced, and felt compelled to do so because of the Gunners' lack of recovery time.

‌



"We are very happy with the victory, the performance and the week," the Arsenal manager said at his post-match press conference. "We were given a terrible schedule. We have overcome every hurdle and I love the mentality of the team."

‌



Arteta also told Sky Sports: "In Munich, it was one of the most physical games we've played in four years, the shift that we put in was incredible and then we have to play on Saturday at 3pm so we needed those legs, that freshness as well. Players are in good moments and they need minutes. They all did really well."

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The other Premier League team to play an away match in Europe on Wednesday were Manchester United. Their fixture this weekend has been scheduled for 4:30pm on Sunday, a much kinder turnaround.

Unlike Arsenal, United don't have a Carabao Cup tie to play in midweek. The Gunners travel to Fleetwood in the fourth round and could without Riccardo Calafiori due to injury.

‌



"He had a slight issue," Arteta confirmed. "We don't know what it is. It seems very small."

Do you agree with Mikel Arteta? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta made five changes to his line-up (Image: Henry NICHOLLS/AFP via Getty Images)

Aside from fitness issues, Arteta had nothing to complain about. After going level with Manchester City at the top of the league, he added: "Really happy. We made five changes. We've had three games in less than six days so we knew how tough it was going to be.

‌



"But I thought the team performed really well. I thought it was really active from the beginning, put a lot of pressure on the opposition.

"We had some problems to finish the actions but we scored from a set piece - the first one this season - and that gave us the confidence and composure to go and dominate the game. But until we scored the second goal, we knew it was game on."

Sports.title: Kai Rooney stuns fans as they call for Man Utd promotion after win over Liverpool U18s
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney stuns fans as they call for Man Utd promotion after win over Liverpool U18s

Kai Rooney has set Manchester United fans' tongues wagging after his performance against Liverpool's Under-18s

View 3 Images Kai Rooney has wowed for Manchester United's Under-18s (Image: Getty)

Manchester United fans have called for Kai Rooney to be promoted to the senior squad after a sensational performance against Liverpool's Under-18s. United's youthful Under-18 squad, managed by Darren Fletcher, won 6-3 on Saturday morning.

‌



‌



Kai, the son of United hero Wayne, has been making waves throughout the club's academy. He joined the set-up aged 11 in 2020 and has progressed through the ranks, earning a two-year academy scholarship deal in July.

‌



Once he turns 17 on November 2, this deal will transition into a three-year professional contract. Last season, Kai featured primarily for the Under-16s and Under-18s, winning the Under-16 Premier League Shield and SuperCupNI. An injury slightly derailed his campaign.

‌



This term, Kai has made his Under-19 UEFA Youth League and Under-21 debuts. But he's mainly turning out for the Under-18s and started up front against Liverpool.

Michael Carrick makes Man Utd vow in emotional six-minute speech as pressure mounts READ MORE :

Wayne Rooney rips into 'selfish' Bruno Fernandes as Man Utd captain brutally exposed READ MORE :

Wearing the No. 9, Kai excelled. He led from the front with his pressing and set up Jaume Camacho, who scored four in the 6-3 drubbing. Fans online have made their true feelings clear on what the future should hold for the young Rooney.

View 3 Images Kai set up Camacho to make it 3-0 (Image: MUTV)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Kai Rooney is a pressing machine," one fan wrote on social media. A second commented: "Kai played a really good game, top notch. He ran like his dad - chased everything down and made plays."

‌



Other supporters pointed out that Kai should be much closer to Michael Carrick's first team. One comment read: "He is always getting closer to first-team potential."

Another claimed: "Our Under-18s are far more enjoyable to watch than the first team! Pace, hunting the ball collectively, calmness in midfield. It's a breath of fresh air watching them every week!"

‌



One final fan simply remarked: "Can they play tomorrow?" These comments come as first-team boss Carrick weathers a severe storm after some lacklustre results.

View 3 Images Fans were impressed with United's Under-18s (Image: MUTV)

‌



With seven Premier League games played, United have won just once. Their latest outing saw them demolished 4-1 by Como in the Champions League.

Carrick spoke ahead of his team's home game against Bournemouth on Sunday and delivered an emotional address, opening up about recent struggles. He said: "Recently we haven't had a good time, I think that's pretty obvious.

Article continues below

"Wednesday [vs Como] was a bad night and it hurt me to see us play like that. It was unacceptable. My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club and the supporters and they can be proud of in the identity we show.

"We have gone away from that recently. It's important we all recognise that. The foundation and values of this football club have been etched for many years. I totally understand and get every single one of them."

Sports.title: Dan Skelton reveals clue which led him to bargain Cheltenham winner Here Comes Georgie
Sports.content:
Dan Skelton reveals clue which led him to bargain Cheltenham winner Here Comes Georgie

Britain's champion trainer bought the chaser for £7,000 and he came away with a first prize of £52,030 in the feature race on the second day of the William Hill Showcase

View 2 Images The 3-1 winner striding to the line

Dan Skelton has revealed the clue which led him to impressive Cheltenham winner Here Comes Georgie.

‌



‌



The bargain buy had never run further than 2m 5f in his racing life but the champion trainer stepped him up to 3m 1f on his first outing for his leading stable at Saturday's meeting.

‌



Ridden by his brother Harry in the William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Chase , Here Comes Georgie was sent off a well-backed 3-1 favourite and was hunted around at the back of the pack with his stamina unproven.

‌



Sporting a new hood and tongue tie combination following wind surgery, the eight-year-old gelding crept into contention and joined the leaders at the final fence.

He gave his supporters a scare by slowing a touch on the run-in, but once galvanised again, galloped strongly to the line for a length-and-a-quarter success.

Storm Boelo could wipe out Sunday racing as Aintree braced for 50mph-plus winds READ MORE :

Dan Skelton picked up Here Comes Georgie for just £7,000, telling Racing TV viewers beforehand that his charge has caught his eye at Ascot.

‌



He was running off a 2lb lower mark than when he defeated the now 139-rated Ryan's Rocket in December 2024.

And Here Comes Georgie was the final finisher in a handicap chase at the course in the same month last year.

‌



Skelton chose him as owner Bill Hawkins, in attendance at Prestbury Park, was on the lookout for a winter horse.

And after banking £52,030 for first, he holds an entry for the £80,000 65th Badger Beers Handicap Chase at Wincanton on November 7.

‌



View 2 Images Dan Skelton broke new ground with Here Comes Georgie (Image: PA Wire)

"As trainers you have to knuckle down and trust your instincts and what you see," Dan Skelton said.

‌



"The whole team has done a brilliant job with this horse. He ran in a really good race at Ascot and wasn't beat too far. I just thought if he could get back to some form... and he was getting in the handicap in a £100,000 race."

Harry Skelton added: "He was a bit too cold down the hill, I would have liked him to have started to take me, to travel. When I jumped the last I thought he was going to go away and win three or four lengths but he did just pull up on the run-in. As soon as they got to me, he picked up again"

Article continues below

Trainer Martin Keighley went to £66,000 to add O'Moore Park to his string in Gloucestershire and the 25-1 outsider defied top weight in the opening William Hill Epic Boosts Novices' Limited Handicap Chase.

He found him in the GoffsGo June Sale while looking for a horse to compete on Saturdays - and was thrilled when Sean Bowen gave him a typically strong ride to get the job done and open his account over fences.

Sports.title: Son of F1 legend, aged 9, in terrifying crash as two vehicles drive over him
Sports.content:
Son of F1 legend, aged 9, in terrifying crash as two vehicles drive over him

The son of a Formula 1 icon was involved in a frightening crash on Friday which involved two karts driving over him after a collision

View 2 Images Toto Wolff's son escaped without injury after being involved in a nasty karting crash (Image: X/thomasmaheronf1)

Toto Wolff's nine-year-old son, Jack, was involved in a terrifying multi-kart crash on Friday. The incident occurred just one month after the Mercedes CEO's son won his first championship: the IAME Series Italy title in the X30 Under-10 category.

‌



‌



Jack competes mainly across Europe and has just completed his debut season. His first race win came in July. His father, Toto, has been at the helm of Formula 1's Mercedes since 2013, currently serving as team principal and holding a 33.3 per cent stake in the outfit.

‌



The Silver Arrows claimed a record eight successive Constructors' Championships between 2014 and 2021 under his leadership. Jack's mother, Susie, is also a former racing driver who now serves as managing director of F1 Academy.

‌



But both parents would have been left shaken on Friday, as they watched their son compete. The nine-year-old was taking part in Qualifying Heat 3 of the X30 Mini category at the Leopard Circuit in Viterbo, Italy. During the closing lap of the heat, Jack, driving No. 25, was locked in a battle for the lead with Nahyl Elgahoudi.

Michael Schumacher pal makes stance clear on public appearance amid health battle READ MORE :

As the two made contact, their wheels collided and Elgahoudi's kart launched violently up and over the front of Jack's machine, balancing precariously on two wheels before narrowly avoiding a full rollover. Jack was then sent into a spin.

View 2 Images Wolff's son was involved in a dramatic crash (Image: X/thomasmaheronf1)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

With no escape route, trailing driver Dimitar Uzunov smashed into the almost stationary kart, becoming airborne and flying directly over the cockpit while striking Jack's shoulder.

‌



Reports indicate Jack was treated following the incident but emerged unscathed. He exited the kart unaided and was keen to return to the paddock.

The commentator observed during the crash: "Look at that straight over the top there went... went Uzunov. How Elgahoudi did not flip there, I do not know... and Wolff as well, taking a big hit to the shoulder."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Speaking at a karting event this summer, Toto discussed his son's ambition: "This is where it all starts. Formula 1 is basically this on steroids. Same kind of racing and watching the kids is just a super experience.

‌



"It's important to find the right balance because obviously as a parent you're emotionally involved and it's completely normal. But he's nine years old.

"There are so many small kids and you need to strike the balance right and we try. Sometimes we get it wrong. You have difficult moments and he had some difficult moments.

Article continues below

"But in the end it comes all together, and every little failure is a learning for the future. Just give them time. They're so small, let them enjoy the karting and that's the most important."

Sports.title: Storm Boelo could wipe out Sunday racing as Aintree braced for 50mph-plus winds
Sports.content:
Storm Boelo could wipe out Sunday racing as Aintree braced for 50mph-plus winds

Horse racing at the home of the Grand National and Market Rasen is in doubt due to the weather, with inspections have been called as Storm Austen is followed by Storm Boelo

View Image Storm Boelo is expected to bring strong winds (Image: ©INPHO/Morgan Treacy)

Storm Boelo is threatening to wipe out Sunday race fixtures in Britain due to high winds. Inspections have been called at Aintree, which is due to stage the feature Grade Two William Hill Old Roan Limited Handicap Chase and Market Rasen.

‌



‌



The tracks are on either side of the country, 146 miles apart, but both are covered by a Met Office yellow weather warning for wind until 9pm on Sunday. Officials will take a look at 8am tomorrow morning to determine whether the meetings can be staged.

‌



A statement from Aintree Racecourse said: "We have been monitoring conditions and the weather forecast closely ahead of tomorrow's Halloween Family Fun Day and will hold a precautionary inspection at 8am tomorrow.

‌



"While the track is raceable, the forecast is for wind speeds to reach up to 50mph throughout the night and into the early morning, with the potential for these speeds to further increase throughout the day.

"The safety of our participants, racegoers and teams on site is our number one priority and we will update everyone as soon as possible."

Market Rasen's clerk of the course, Alice Cosgrove, told the Racing Post gusts of 53mph are in the forecast. Galway and Wexford are scheduled in Ireland, while Constitution Hill is running in the Group Two Gran Premio del Jockey Club at San Siro in Italy.

Sports.title: Sports star, 37, dies suddenly as 'devastated' wife shares heartbreaking tribute
Sports.content:
Sports star, 37, dies suddenly as 'devastated' wife shares heartbreaking tribute

Heartfelt tributes are pouring in following the sudden death of husband and father-of-two Daniel Stewart, who played as a key forward in the AFL for Port Adelaide

View 3 Images Daniel Stewart has passed away aged 37 (Image: Morne de Klerk/Getty Images)

Former Aussie Rules star Daniel Stewart has died suddenly aged 37. In a heartbreaking tribute, wife Laura said that she and her two children had been left 'devastated' by his loss.

‌



‌



Stewart represented Port Adelaide in the AFL between 2010 and 2013. Stewart played 36 matches and kicked 31 goals for the Power.

‌



The key forward was selected with pick No.35 in the 2009 rookie draft. Stewart was signed from North Adelaide, having come through at Eastern Ranges and Queensland club Labrador.

‌



On Instagram, Laura shared a photo of her, Daniel and their two children with a moving tribute. "Devastated to confirm the loss of our world," she wrote.

"A heart too big for this world. We love you so much daddy. Please respect our privacy as we navigate this incredible loss and prioritise our boys."

‌



3 View 3 Images Daniel Stewart played for Port Adelaide (Image: Morne de Klerk/Getty Images) 3 View 3 Images He kicked 31 goals for the Power (Image: Morne de Klerk/Getty Images)

‌



Port Adelaide have confirmed that their players will wear black armbands in their first home game at the Adelaide Oval in 2027 to pay tribute to Stewart.

A statement from Power chief executive Matthew Richardson read: "On behalf of everyone at the Port Adelaide Football Club, I extend our deepest condolences to Daniel's family including his mum Donna, dad Byron, wife Laura, his two sons Bernie and Lando and his brother Leigh.

‌



"We also extend our thoughts to his friends, including his close friend and former teammate Matt Thomas, and to all those at North Adelaide and Labrador who knew him.

‌



"Daniel was part of the Port Adelaide football family, and he always will be. A sudden passing like this is devastating and our thoughts are with everyone who loved him, and with the teammates, coaches and staff who shared the journey with him here at Alberton.

"The club will provide support to those affected by Daniel’s passing, including his former teammates and the people who worked alongside him. We will honour Daniel by wearing black armbands in our first home game at Adelaide Oval in 2027."

One of Stewart's former team-mates at Port Adelaide, Kane Cornes, also paid tribute. "A true tragedy. A brilliant and caring teammate who always had a smile on his face," Cornes posted.

"I loved watching him and his beautiful family from afar. He built a thriving business and shared a special friendship with Matty Thomas. Heart goes out to his family."

Sports.title: Former Man Utd chief who Sir Jim Ratcliffe axed lands new job with EFL club
Sports.content:
Former Man Utd chief who Sir Jim Ratcliffe axed lands new job with EFL club

Sir Jim Ratcliffe didn't waste time making changes when he purchased a minority stake in Manchester United in 2024 and took control of the club's football operations

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe quickly put his stamp on things (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Former Manchester United chief John Murtough has been appointed director of football at Birmingham City. Murtough left Old Trafford in 2024, having spent 11 years at with the Red Devils.

‌



‌



The 55-year-old's departure via mutual agreement came shortly after Sir Jim Ratcliffe acquired a 27.7% stake, which has since been increased, in United through his petrochemicals company, INEOS, and made several changes to their football department. Murtough went on to join Atalanta, working as that Italian club's director of global development.

‌



Now Murtough, whose CV also includes roles with Everton, Fulham, Coventry City and with the Premier League, is back in England. Birmingham confirmed his appointment on Friday and a statement from the club's board read: "We are delighted to welcome John to Birmingham City.

‌



"We have been clear from the outset about our ambition for this Club and for the city of Birmingham. We want Birmingham City competing at the highest level of English football and we are building for sustained success, both on and off the pitch.
