Ghana News.title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation: Asafo-Adjei says government’s figures do not add up
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Nana Asafo-Adjei Ayeh, has raised concerns over the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa, insisting that the figures presented by the government do not add up.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, the opposition lawmaker questioned the credibility of the expenditure, arguing that the inability to satisfactorily establish the number of beneficiaries raises serious concerns about the entire evacuation exercise.

"I am at this point confident in everything in me that the figures don't add up. If you cannot even establish the 1,964, then there is a problem with everything you did," he stated.

Mr Asafo-Adjei maintained that the documents presented to justify the expenditure must be subjected to thorough scrutiny, stressing that the details should support the government's public explanations.

According to him, the Minority's concerns are based on the contents of the available documentation rather than political disagreements or unrelated issues.

"The content of the document is what matters. The devil is always in the details, and that is what we are looking at, and it doesn't support your communication," he said.

The Deputy Ranking Member emphasised that his focus remains on establishing the facts surrounding the expenditure and ensuring that the government provides satisfactory explanations for the amount spent and the reported number of evacuees.

He rejected suggestions that the Minority was diverting attention from the substantive issues, insisting that his interventions have consistently centred on accountability and transparency.

"If you listen to the Minority, particularly me, I have never majored in any tangential. I am focused on this matter, and I want to get to the logical conclusion of this matter," he stressed.

His comments come amid scrutiny of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs over the reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa.

Ghana News.title: 2026 U17 WWC: Black Maidens book knockout spot with win over Canada
Ghana News.content:
Ghana produced a great second half performance to advance into the knockout stages of the ongoing U-17 Women’s World Cup.

The Black Maidens defeated Canada 2-0 in their final group game of the tournament to finish second in Group C after a troubling start to the tournament.

Nana Joe Adarkwa’s side came into the final group game knowing only a win was enough to get them into the next phase of the competition.

Despite a strong start to the game, the Maidens always rushed their final third decision making, leaving them with no goals after 45 minutes despite 13 attempts.

After the recess, Ghana continued to create chances in the game with Gloria Ameaa and Jessica Appiah posing dangers to the Canadian defence but both players were unable to find the back of the net.

Adarkwa called on his bench halfway through the second half, bringing on Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku.

Those changes yielded results as Achiaa scored with her first touch after the ball deflected off the crossbar, opening the scoring in the game.

In the closing stages of the encounter, Ashiaku doubled the lead for the Black Maidens with a brilliant strike, lobbing it over the goalkeeper to wrap up the victory.

The win sees Ghana finish their group campaign in second place with four points, behind Brazil who claimed seven points from three games.

Ghana also advance into the round of 16 on their return to the global stage at the U-17 level following their comeback from a two-edition ban.

Ghana News.title: NDC constituency election records impressive turnout at Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro.
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) constituency executive elections have recorded an impressive turnout at the Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro constituency in the Greater Accra Region.

The elections, which started in the early hours of today, are approaching their final stage, with delegates arriving in large numbers to cast their votes.

Voting is taking place at the Astroturf in Tuba, a suburb of Ngleshie Amanfro, where a large crowd of delegates, party supporters, and observers has gathered.

The exercise is being conducted by officials of the Electoral Commission (EC), while members of the party's election committee are coordinating and monitoring the process to ensure a smooth and transparent election.

A number of aspirants are contesting various constituency executive positions, including Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Treasurer, Organiser, Deputy Organiser, Communications Officer, Women's Organiser, Deputy Women's Organiser, Youth Organiser, Deputy Youth Organiser and Zongo Caucus Coordinator, in line with the party's structure.

The atmosphere at the venue has been generally calm and orderly, with security personnel present to maintain law and order.

Some delegates who spoke to reporters expressed satisfaction with the conduct of the polls so far, describing the process as peaceful and transparent.

They said the high turnout reflects the enthusiasm of members to elect competent leaders who will strengthen the party at the grassroots level ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Party officials in the constituency said they expect the elections to end peacefully and called on all aspirants and their supporters to accept the outcome in good faith and work together to advance the interest of the NDC in Bortianor-Ngleshie Amanfro.

Counting of ballots is expected to begin immediately after voting ends, with winners to be declared by the Electoral Commission officials.

Ghana News.title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation cost: Flight charter price comparisons alone can’t prove overpricing – IMANI Associate
Ghana News.content:
An Associate of IMANI Centre for Policy and Education (CPE), Kay Cudjoe, has cautioned against drawing conclusions of overpricing based solely on comparisons between the reported cost of chartering aircraft for the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa and alternative charter prices.

His comments follow public discussions surrounding the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa, including a reported aircraft charter cost of GH¢27,180,700.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, 2026, Mr Cudjoe stressed the need for a careful assessment of the circumstances surrounding the charter arrangements before determining whether the expenditure was excessive.

According to him, although comparisons with alternative charter prices may raise legitimate questions about the expenditure, they are insufficient on their own to establish overpricing.

“It is important to establish a very important part of the conversation…the area where we should be most careful is where the reported charter cost of 27,180,700.

"I think public comparisons with alternative charter prices cannot prove overpricing unless we look at the issues concerning aircraft charter,” he stated.

Ghana News.title: GH¢49.72m S.A. evacuation: Nobody slept in a bus; it cannot be true – Benjamin Quashie
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Benjamin Quashie, has rejected claims that some Ghanaians evacuated from the country slept in buses before boarding their chartered flights, insisting that accommodation was arranged for them in hotels.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, against the backdrop of the GH¢49.72 million spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa, Mr Quashie said the mission ensured that evacuees travelling from distant provinces were accommodated before their flights.

“Let me move to a few of the issues that have been raised because it bothers on the individual evacuees in South Africa. The first one is to state that not a single individual slept in a bus; it was impossible,” he said.

He explained that evacuees were brought from areas including the Western Cape and Eastern Cape, as well as East London, and that the buses used to transport them to Pretoria were paid for by the mission.

According to him, the evacuees were taken to hotels before their flights, with arrangements made to ensure they had time to rest and refresh themselves.

“When you look at the first three flights, the chartered flights, we brought them in from the provinces. Before they got here, we had gotten hotels,” he said.

Mr Quashie added that the arrangements were designed to reduce costs while ensuring that passengers arrived in Pretoria ahead of their scheduled departures.

“So because we wanted to save costs, if you are supposed to travel on Wednesday, we get you on a bus on Tuesday. So that when you get to Pretoria, all we want you to do is that you spend one day in the hotel, get yourself refreshed, we supply food and other things for you,” he explained.

He said the evacuees were subsequently transported from their hotels to the airport for their flights.

Mr Quashie challenged anyone claiming to have slept in a bus during the evacuation to come forward, while acknowledging that some journeys to Pretoria could take several hours.

“I am daring anyone who comes out and says that they slept in a bus,” he said.

He, however, clarified that passengers travelling from places such as the Northern Cape and Cape Town could have slept during the long bus journeys to Pretoria.

“The only way they would have slept in a bus is if you are coming from Northern Cape and Northern Cape is 12 hours or 13 hours or Cape Town, and you are coming and it is about 10 hours. Of course, you will sleep in the bus before you get to Pretoria. If that is what they mean by sleeping in the bus,” he said.

The evacuation of the 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa has come under scrutiny following reports on the GH¢49.72 million spent on the exercise.

Ghana News.title: Africa must take control of its resources and security future – Mahama
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has warned that foreign powers are seeking strategic influence and access to Africa’s natural resources, urging African leaders to unite to protect the continent’s sovereignty and security.

He cautioned that without a coordinated response, Africa risks surrendering control of its political and security future to external interests.

Speaking at the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, on Saturday, October 24, Mr Mahama said competition over natural resources, weak governance and foreign interference were contributing to conflicts across the continent.

He cited conflicts in Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where fighting is linked to competition over valuable resources, including gold, coltan and cobalt.

“External powers, from the East, the West, and the Gulf, are actively seeking leverage, access, and client states on our soil,” he said.

“Let me be clear: Africa is not an empty chessboard for foreign powers to play their games. We are not spectators. But unless we consciously decide to take up the pen and write our own script, someone else will write it for us, and we will not like how the story ends.”

Mr Mahama said the continent’s security challenges were also being worsened by governance failures in Somalia, the marginalisation of young people in Mozambique’s gas-rich Cabo Delgado region, and divisions between the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the Alliance of Sahel States.

He warned that such divisions weakened regional cooperation and undermined collective efforts to address threats to peace and stability.

The President also drew attention to the growing use of commercial drones by armed groups, warning that the relatively cheap and accessible technology was making conflicts increasingly deadly.

“Armed groups and non-state actors have mastered the commercial drone—cheap, accessible, and deadly. In Sudan alone, these low-cost flying weapons accounted for the vast majority of civilian casualties early this year,” he added.

Mr Mahama called on African leaders to strengthen cooperation, improve governance and take greater control of the continent’s natural resources and security priorities.

He warned that failure to pursue a united approach would leave African countries increasingly vulnerable to external influence and prevent them from determining their own future.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Trump says he may move White House press corps to new location
World.content:
Trump’s remarks come amid a fractious moment between the US president and the journalists who cover him.

Share Trump says he may move White House press corps to new location on social media

United States President Donald Trump has confirmed he could move the White House press corps to a different location, possibly away from the executive residence.

In a social media post on Friday, Trump described reports that he planned to remove the White House press briefing room in favour of restoring a historic swimming pool located underneath as “Fake News”.

“I NEVER even thought to do such a stupid thing!” he wrote in a Truth Social post.

Trump, however, indicated he may relocate dozens of reporters who cover the White House “to a less obnoxious location”.

The New York Times on Tuesday reported that Trump had pitched his former press secretary, Karoline Leavitt, on an idea to move journalists out of the White House’s storied James S. Brady Press Briefing Room. That proposal did not move forward during Leavitt’s tenure, which ended on August 27.

Trump’s remarks come amid a fractious moment between him and the journalists who cover him.

Last month, Trump banned journalists from three US-based media outlets – CNN, MS NOW and POLITICO – from the White House, a move that proponents of free speech said violated First Amendment protections.

A US federal judge ruled that the order was likely unconstitutional, forcing the White House to restore the journalists’ access. The Trump administration continues to fight the ruling.

Trump has also regularly chided and denigrated members of the media he claims cover him unfairly.

The latest incident was during an Oval Office event on Tuesday when Trump attacked The Independent’s White House Correspondent Andrew Feinberg.



“What’s wrong with you? Are you a sick person? I actually think there’s something wrong with you”, Trump said as Feinberg tried to ask a question. The moment was amplified by the White House on social media.

If Trump opts to proceed with changes to the White House press briefing room, it would be the latest in a long list of controversial projects he has ordered that would transform the property.

Since returning to power last year, the US president has demolished the White House East Wing to construct a new ballroom, installed concrete pavers over the lawn centred in the White House Rose Garden and built a helipad on the South Lawn.

The Times reported Trump told aides he wanted to bring back a West Wing indoor pool constructed in 1933 for use by President Franklin D Roosevelt, who suffered from polio and often swam, according to his presidential library, to ease soreness.

In the 1970s, former President Richard Nixon had a floor constructed above the pool to accommodate a briefing room for the growing White House press corps. The pool remains beneath the floor of the briefing room.

Leavitt confirmed during a Friday interview that Trump was “flirting” with the idea of restoring the pool.

“He just, maybe, wants to restore it to all of its glory”, Leavitt said during an appearance on HBO’s “Real Time with Bill Maher”. “I don’t know if he’ll do it.”

The White House did not immediately return Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

World.title: About 25,000 rally in Madrid in support of Spain’s state pension scheme
World.content:
Demonstrators want pensions to remain indexed to inflation and the gender pension gap to be eliminated.

Share About 25,000 rally in Madrid in support of Spain’s state pension scheme on social media

Approximately 25,000 people have gathered in the Spanish capital in support of the state pension scheme, as protests continue across Europe, prompted by a range of issues, including the cost of living, school conditions and alleged corruption.

Protesters from across the country marched through Madrid on Saturday before next month’s general election.

The pressure on Spain’s state pension scheme is being driven by several factors, including an ageing population, a low birth rate and wage stagnation, as well as a declining ratio of workers to pensioners.

Demonstrators are concerned that the state pension scheme could be significantly weakened depending on who wins next month’s election. The country’s monthly pension bill hit a record high this year of almost 14.5 billion euros ($16.2bn).

Protesters marched from Atocha train station to the Gran Via, Madrid’s busiest and most famous street.

Several of the demonstrators carried banners reading “protect and guarantee our pensions”.

Emilio Delgado serves as the deputy spokesperson of the left-wing party Mas Madrid in the Assembly of Madrid. Posting on X, he said that “no pension should be below the minimum wage. A lifetime of work deserves a dignified retirement.”

Protesters want pensions to remain indexed to inflation and are calling for the gender pension gap to be eliminated.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has accused the right-wing Popular Party (PP) of planning to weaken inflation-linked pension increases if it wins next month’s election.



However, leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo said on Monday that he would continue to raise pensions in line with inflation if his party wins the vote.

Sanchez has pledged to protect pensions if he remains in office and says the current pension system is affordable.

The system has gradually become more reliant on state funding because of a growing number of pensioners and increases in monthly payments.

World.title: Barcelona vs Real Madrid: La Liga – El Clasico preview, predictions, teams
World.content:
Bragging rights are up for grabs in Sunday’s El Clasico between La Liga leaders Barcelona and third-placed Real Madrid.

Share Mourinho looks to halt Barcelona’s run as El Clasico rivalry resumes on social media

Who: Barcelona vs Real Madrid

What: La Liga, El Clasico

Where: Camp Nou in Barcelona, Spain

When: Sunday at 9pm (20:00 GMT)

How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 17:00 GMT.

For weeks La Liga leaders Barcelona have been eagerly awaiting Sunday’s El Clasico as a chance to stretch the gap between themselves and rivals Real Madrid to a massive nine points.

Some turbulence in the final approach to the clash at Camp Nou has complicated the picture for Hansi Flick’s Spanish champions, who suffered their first defeat of the season at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Tuesday.

By contrast, Real Madrid have won four consecutive matches, thrashing RB Leipzig on Wednesday and starting to look, for the first time since Jose Mourinho’s arrival this summer, like a team.

Should Real come away with a win, it would not only halve the current six-point gap, but ⁠provide a much-needed confidence boost for a side that has lost six of the last seven Clasicos.

Mourinho’s return to the fixture will attract the most attention of all.

Mourinho set for 18th El Clasico

The ⁠63-year-old is a veteran of 27 matches against Barcelona and 17 El Clasicos on ⁠the Real bench.

Real Madrid President Florentino Perez first appointed Mourinho as manager in 2010 to compete with Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona, and he will hope the Portuguese can wrest the La Liga title back to the Bernabeu for a second time.

Mourinho’s first spell at Real coincided with arguably the most heated encounters in ‌the modern history of El Clasico, and there will be numerous cameras trained on his every move at Camp Nou on Sunday.



The Portuguese manager won just once in his first 10 El Clasicos but went unbeaten in his final five games ‌against ‌Barcelona, recording three victories.

Unfair to compare us with Barca, Mourinho says

Flick’s Barca have won back-to-back La Liga titles and lead the top flight, in which they are unbeaten, while Mourinho arrived this summer after Madrid went two seasons without a major trophy.

Mourinho highlighted that he has been at the helm only a few months in comparison with Flick, who arrived at Barca in 2024.

“People look at us like a finished product, but finished products in football are difficult because they are never finished, … but they look at us like we’re in an advanced phase of the process,” Mourinho continued.

“We’ve been working for three months. Out of that you can take preseason when the players were arriving [back from the World Cup] and the recent international break. Then we’ve been together a month-and-a-half, two months.

“This is the start of a product. We’re in an initial phase where the coach is learning, analysing, bit by bit defining paths. The players are learning about the coach. … Comparing a team in this state [to more established sides], I think is unfair.”

Flick praises Mourinho before clash

The German coach said he expected a Madrid side arriving with “a lot of confidence” and praised Mourinho.

“I have the highest respect. When you’re managing teams on this level for so many years and you always have success, it’s about quality. He showed this at every club,” Flick told reporters.

“Every player from the [German] national team who worked under him speaks with a great respect. I think the same. He’s a colleague, a very, very successful colleague and a great colleague.”

Flick said the 4-2 defeat in Paris by PSG on Tuesday gave his team some clues as to where they need to improve.

“We analysed this game. We did many things really good, but we saw some situations where we have to improve,” Flick said.

“We have to grow as a team. Tomorrow we play against one of the best teams in the world, so it’s a good opportunity to grow, to challenge ourselves, to improve ourselves and to grow as a team.”

Managers on ‘incredible’, ‘unique’ El Clasico

Flick: “El Clasico is different. It is the best match in our sport, and everyone will watch it. It is incredible. It is true that we are playing for just three points, but the importance of the match goes far beyond that.”



Mourinho: “We’ve been in a good dynamic, winning games, playing well, scoring goals, but in El Clasico, it doesn’t matter what you did before. It has no influence. El Clasico is unique. Normally, the football world stops to watch it. Hopefully, it’s a great game and we win.”

How have Barcelona played this season?

Barcelona have a perfect record in La Liga with nine wins from nine games. They are five points clear at the top of the standings.

Their only defeat in all competitions this season came in the last match, in which they fell 4-2 to title holders PSG in the Champions League league phase.

How have Real Madrid played this season?

Real are third in the La Liga points table, six points behind leaders and rivals Barca.

They have won seven league games but lost to Atletico Madrid and Real Betis.

However, Real have made a perfect start in the UCL, registering two wins in as many matches.

Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Predictions

Opta’s supercomputer has given Barcelona a 54.4 percent chance of winning this Clasico while Real have a 26.1 percent probability. There are 19.5 percent odds of a draw.

Overall, Barca are given a 77.93 percent chance of retaining the title this season with Real tipped to finish second and Atletico third.

Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Head-to-head

Matches: 264

Barcelona wins: 106

Real wins: 106

Draws: 52

Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Form guide

Barcelona: L-W-W-W-W

Real Madrid: W-W-W-W-L

Where can I watch Barcelona vs Real Madrid?

Spain: Movistar, DAZN

Middle East and North Africa: beIN SPORTS

South Africa: SportyTV, DAZN

India: FanCode

United Kingdom: Disney+, Premier Sports

United States: ESPN, ESPN+

Barcelona’s team news

Midfielder Dani Olmo will miss the Clasico after being ruled out for about a month with a thigh injury.

Other names already on the injury list are Jules Kounde (ankle), Eric Garcia (thigh), Andreas Christensen (thigh) and Roony Bardghji (knee).

Predicted starting XI:

Joan Garcia (goalkeeper); Xavi Espart, Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin, Joao Cancelo; Marc Bernal, Pedri; Lamine Yamal, Ferran Torres, Anthony Gordon; Raphinha

Real Madrid’s team news

Vincius Jr will miss the game due to a suspension while Raul Asencio (leg) and Rodrygo (knee) are both injured.

Predicted starting XI:

Thibaut Courtois (goalkeeper); Federico Valverde, Antonio Rudiger, Dean Huijsen, Alvaro Carreras; Bernardo Silva, Eduardo Camavinga; Arda Guler, Jude Bellingham, Yan Diomande, Kylian Mbappe

World.title: More than 2,000 forced from homes in Hebron amid Israel’s West Bank raids
World.content:
Palestinians in Hebron are ‘living in fear’ with the city closed, while Israeli forces arrest dozens across West Bank.

Share More than 2,000 forced from homes in Hebron amid Israel’s West Bank raids on social media

Israel has imposed a lockdown and displaced thousands of Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, as the military conducts raids in the occupied West Bank following the deaths of two Israeli soldiers.

This comes as the Palestinian Authority (PA) on Saturday called for international pressure on Israel to protect Hebron’s residents, who said soldiers announced evacuation orders over loudspeakers late at night, leaving them with no time to prepare and few places to move to.

Hebron’s mayor Yousef al-Ja’bari told Al Jazeera that 2,200 people had been forced from their homes as hundreds of Israeli raids took place since Friday’s attack by two Palestinian gunmen on an Israeli army reserve base. The two Palestinians were killed, as well as the two Israeli soldiers.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu then ordered a “full lockdown” of the West Bank following the attack.

Mayor al-Ja’bari said on Saturday that Hebron residents can neither enter nor leave the city.

Israeli soldiers also fired a stun grenade at Al Jazeera journalists near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint in Hebron, as they documented an Israeli operation to bulldoze homes and vehicles in the area.

The Israeli military carried out raids across at least 15 areas of the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Al Jazeera correspondents on the ground reported.

Those targeted include Jenin and Nablus in the north; Ramallah, Al-Bireh, Birzeit, and occupied East Jerusalem in the centre; and Bethlehem in the south.



Israeli forces have arrested about 70 Palestinians in raids across the West Bank, the Palestinian Prisoners’ Society said.

The PA, which governs the West Bank, called Israel’s actions “collective punishment”, citing the demolition of homes, forced displacement of entire neighbourhoods, and the “closure and siege of Palestinian cities”, and urged the international community to intervene, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Meanwhile, Hamas said in a statement that the “campaigns and escalations carried out by the occupation and its criminal settlers against our people will only fuel further outrage”.

Hundreds of thousands ‘under siege’

Around 200,000 Palestinians live in the city of Hebron itself, and a further 600,000 in Hebron governorate, making it the West Bank’s most populous governorate.

Those 800,000 Palestinians in Hebron governorate are “now under siege, with all entrances and exits closed since morning”, Issa Amro, a Palestinian activist and political analyst based in Hebron, told Al Jazeera.

“Inside the city, there is no safe place for anyone to hide … the city is really in fear,” Amro said.

Political positioning

Israeli politicians are trying to “capitalise” on the attack ahead of parliamentary elections on October 27 , Al Jazeera’s West Bank correspondent Nour Odeh said.

“Netanyahu, his Likud party, and his allies in this right-wing coalition are behind in the polls,” said Odeh, so in response they are “trying to put up a brave front, saying they’re combating Palestinians”.

Just days before Israelis are set to vote, Netanyahu avoided answering whether he planned to dismantle the PA, but said a “big surprise” awaits the organisation.

World.title: Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro about even ahead of election run-off: Poll
World.content:
The race between Brazil’s president and the right-wing senator has tightened in recent days.

Share Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro about even ahead of election run-off: Poll on social media

⁠Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula ⁠da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro remain about even on the eve of Sunday’s election run-off, shows a CNT/MDA poll.

The right-wing ‌senator, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, would receive 46.3 percent of the vote compared ⁠with 45 percent for the leftist ⁠Lula, according to the poll released on Saturday. Last week, ⁠the poll showed Bolsonaro leading ⁠Lula 46.8 percent to ⁠45.9 percent.

MDA surveyed 2,032 people from October 21 to ‌October 23, with a margin of error of 2.2 ‌percentage ‌points.

The poll comes the day after the final debate before the presidential run-off.

The candidates questioned each other on Friday about Brazil’s economy, infrastructure and regional development.

Bolsonaro accused the incumbent of allowing organised crime to expand, driving families into debt and not addressing the higher cost of living.

“He doesn’t know what hunger is,” Brazil’s first working-class president said of Bolsonaro. “He doesn’t know Brazil.”

Sunday’s vote comes after Bolsonaro finished first in the initial round of voting on October 4 with 47 percent to Lula’s 45 percent.

A Datafolha institute survey published on Thursday suggested the pair are now tied with 50 percent support each, compared with Bolsonaro’s four-point lead in polls published two weeks ago.

World.title: Hundreds of soldiers deploy as protesters rally in Italy’s Milan
World.content:
The Italian government has sent hundreds of soldiers to the country’s financial hub before anticipated unrest.

Share Hundreds of soldiers deploy as protesters rally in Italy’s Milan on social media

Milan, Italy – Protests have been called in eight Italian cities to demonstrate against Giorgia Meloni’s right-wing government and the rising cost of living, a week after demonstrations in Milan spiralled into clashes with police and looting.

Protesters marched in the Italian fashion and finance capital on Saturday, as soldiers spread out across the city and luxury boutiques were boarded up.

This followed an announcement online of a new round of protests by a newly formed group calling itself the ‘October 17 Movement’, which has been the main driver of demonstrations alongside student federations, grassroots trade unions, and antiwar coalitions.

“Those who deny our future are truly violent,” the group said on Instagram. “We distrust this government because we see it as authoritarian.”

In response to last weekend’s looting, the government announced a series of new security measures, including the deployment of 500 soldiers to Milan.

On Friday, police carried out raids and searches in several cities, against people suspected of taking part in looting and rioting in last weekend’s protests, the Italian news agency Adnkronos reported. Officers conducted another 150 raids on Saturday morning in the northern region of Lombardy.

But on its Telegram channel, the October 17 Movement said many of those planning to demonstrate wanted to voice their dissent peacefully.

“We must be peaceful. If we give [the police] an excuse, they will charge against us,” a participant identified as E said on Thursday.



Others have stressed that there is no distinction between those who engage in violence and peaceful protesters. “It’s just us,” said a member identified as Q.

Protesters had decided to keep the location of the demonstration secret until the last minute, with three meeting points expected to be announced on their social media accounts on Saturday afternoon.

In the meantime, police confirmed to Al Jazeera that they had located and were questioning the administrator of the group’s Instagram page. According to the Italian daily Corriere della Sera, he is a 30-year-old Italian-Moroccan freelance journalist and researcher. He is currently under investigation on suspicion of “inciting crimes”.

Most of the protesters arrested on Sunday were very young. Of the 271 people arrested, 220 were under the age of 18.

Some joined the protests after being unexpectedly added to a Telegram group, Corriere della Sera reported.

“They said that they would raise chaos and we could take a lot of goods,” one of them said.

Lawyer Michele D’Agostino is defending two demonstrators, aged 21 and 15.

“[The youngest one] didn’t even know the reasons behind the protest; he had just seen it on TikTok and decided to check it out with a friend,” D’Agostino told Al Jazeera.

“He was not among the looters, but he did not realise the seriousness of what was happening,” he said.

The public prosecutor has blamed social media for misleading young people into taking part in what he described as “insurrectional acts”.

Meanwhile, Justice Minister Carlo Nordio told Sky TG24 that there was a need to “expand the capacity of our youth detention facilities” in response to the mass arrests of people under the age of 18.

Earlier this week, truck drivers set up roadblocks in several regions of southern Italy to protest soaring fuel prices, leaving many markets without supplies for days. On Thursday, the government sought to offer them some relief by granting tax breaks and establishing a special fund for farmers and fishermen.

World.title: Why Israeli tourists and investors are unsettling Cypriots
World.content:
NewsFeed Why Israeli tourists and investors are unsettling Cypriots

Israeli tourism in Cyprus is surging, with nearly 600,000 trips by Israelis last year and growing investment across multiple industries. Israeli politics has even broken through. Cypriots say the influx is threatening local businesses and pushing communities out of their neighbourhoods. Al Jazeera’s Nils Adler @n.adler.media reports.

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
World.content:
Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network.

Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it.

This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back".

Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored.

"This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday.

Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield.

Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues.

Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.

The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.

World.title: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
World.content:
Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest.

Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames.

Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene where the blaze was still burning early on Saturday, as police said difficult terrain hindered efforts to bring the fire under control.

Police said they apprehended the suspect riding a motorcycle near the scene and possible motives were still being examined, German media reported. A criminal investigation has been launched.

There is currently nothing to suggest the involvement of further suspects, police official Gerhart Holzinger told a press conference on Saturday afternoon.

Public prosecutor Rainer Vietze said a psychiatric report had concluded the 33-year-old man showed signs of possible mental illness and diminished responsibility might therefore be assumed.

Vietze said a possible political motive was also being considered, but stressed the investigation was in its early stages.

The residence, above the town of Berchtesgaden, was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two.

Hitler and top Nazi officials used his nearby Berghof residence to plan the invasion of the USSR in 1941 and the whole complex was considered one of his headquarters.

He also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.

Local media reported that site had been "largely destroyed" and the public was urged to avoid the area.

Bavaria's Interior Minister Joachim Herrmann told reporters that the site would "under no circumstances remain a ruin", broadcaster BR24 reported. "It is important that we continue our work of remembrance," he added.

World.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
World.content:
A father who fatally shot a gunman at his daughters' school in the US state of Oregon has described his anguish over being unable to save more pupils after "hearing children pleading for their lives".

Three students and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student at Silver Rail Elementary School earlier this month. The attacker was then killed by Kaylub Giamanco.

"I want to apologise for not saving their babies," Giamanco, who has been hailed as a hero, said of his thoughts for the parents of the children killed, in an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB) that aired on Friday.

"The gratitude for saving people's children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn't save."

Giamanco, 36, said he wanted to meet the victims' families and "cry with them and hold them".

He credited a teacher who fought the attacker with giving him the chance to intervene without losing his own life.

"I would love to give her a hug because that's a real true hero," he said.

The students who were killed were all boys, aged five, eight and 11. They were among six people in total who were shot in a classroom at the school, police said. Alongside the teacher who was killed, another child and a teacher were wounded.

Giamanco told OPB that the day of the attack began with breakfast and making packed lunches. He and his wife had spent extra time getting their daughters ready because it was school picture day.

The carpenter had taken lunch to work but decided to go home to eat with his wife instead. That decision brought him past the school as the attack began.

He initially wondered whether someone carrying a long gun was playing a prank. Then he saw him fire at a pickup truck and head towards the school.

Giamanco retrieved a handgun from his vehicle and called emergency services.

"I said, 'I'm sorry, I have to go in. People are going to die'," he told the broadcaster.

He followed the attacker, who shot through the school's locked glass doors. Hearing children pleading for their lives and more gunfire, Giamanco crawled towards the building.

"I told myself this is probably the last thing that I'm ever going to do," he said.

World.title: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas
World.content:
"She was the purest, most amazing wife, mother and friend to have ever walked this Earth," her husband said in a Facebook post.

"I will never get over this, she was my soulmate, my childhood sweetheart, my one and only. The foundation of my entire family and the strength that held us all together.

"My boys had to witness something nobody should ever have to see of any age, but they know Mum died an absolute hero."

Gregory said he had also set up a fundraising page "for my sons and security after the tragic loss".

In the post on that page he described how his wife, who he had been with for 22 years, had held on to their son until he was rescued "but didn't have the energy to save herself".

He added: "I just have to be thankful for the hero she was in life and in death, and totally grateful for the fact my boys got out safely."

World.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
World.content:
Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.

Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free".

The video, posted on Friday, teases the release of a longer YouTube video to come on Saturday, in which Vanessa and Kai Trump will discuss breast cancer awareness and prevention, Kai wrote in the caption.

Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods.

"October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram.

"I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued.

Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben.

In Friday's video, Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team.

According to the American Cancer Society, the average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, according to the group.

Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some disease remains, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk.

Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy.

World.title: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
World.content:
Three people, who were arrested in connection with a suspected arson attack which killed four family members in the Republic of Ireland, have been released, gardaÃ­ (Irish police) have said.

Philip and Kim English and two of their children - nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum - died after their home in Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford was set on fire earlier this month.

A man aged in his 20s and a woman in her 30s were previously charged in connection with the attack.

On Saturday, gardaÃ­ said three people - two women in their 30s and a man in his 50s - who were arrested on Tuesday have been released without charge.

A fourth person, a man in his 20s who was arrested on Thursday, remains in custody.

World.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
World.content:
Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.

A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said.

Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added.

All the cases were within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry said.

More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.

Kenya's latest victim had been under quarantine when she developed symptoms on 13 October, the health ministry said.

The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later.

Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner.

World.title: Australian MP's condition improves after alleged car attack
World.content:
The condition of Helen Haines, the Australian MP hit by a car five days ago in north-east Victoria, has improved from critical to serious but stable.

The independent MP, 65, had both her legs amputated after what authorities say was a deliberate attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne, on Monday.

In the latest update on Saturday morning, the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne said Haines was in a serious but stable condition, the first improvement since she was airlifted there.

Her alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, was arrested shortly after the incident and has since appeared in court on three charges.

The politician's husband, Phil Haines, said on Wednesday that the "horrendous incident" had caused his wife significant injuries but "her heart and her mind" were "in good shape".

World.title: CBN grants JP Morgan approval-in-principle to set up merchant bank
World.content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has granted approval-in-principle to JP Morgan to set up a merchant in the country.

The move eases the path for the US largest bank to expand its services – payments, lending, trade finance and corporate banking – in Nigeria, where it has operated a representative office for years.

JP Morgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited plans to run wholesale banking, capital markets and advisory services, Michael Akuka, the CBN’s director of corporate communications and investor relations, said in a statement on Friday.

The approval-in-principle is the first phase of the licensing process, and does not translate into an ultimate banking permit.

JP Morgan needs to clear further regulatory hurdles such as incorporation with the Corporate Affairs Commission and operational approvals before it can commence operations, the regulator stated.

The push comes amidst hordes of banking sector reforms in Africa’s most populous country, aimed at bolstering the financial system, enhancing market confidence and boosting resilience.

According to the statement, the CBN also approved the nomination of Adedapo Olagunju as the managing director of the bank and Latter Kevin George, Nzelu Chinedum Izunwanne and Syed Gabriel Murtaza as non-executive directors.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our objective is to build a financial system that is stable, competitive and internationally connected, one that commands confidence and can effectively support investment and economic growth,” said CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso.

“We are encouraged by the growing interest of international financial institutions in Nigeria. Our focus remains on sustaining the reforms, strengthening the credibility of our markets and creating an environment in which both domestic and international institutions can participate and thrive,” he added.

On Tuesday, Bloomberg, citing sources with knowledge of the deal, reported that JP Morgan was on course to secure a banking licence in the country after depositing N50 billion ($38 million) with the CBN.

It noted that the bank hopes to receive the licence by year-end or in early 2027, provided it is able to obtain all the requisite approvals

P Morgan’s presence in Nigeria dates back to 1961, when Chase Manhattan Bank, which later evolved into JP Morgan Chase & Co., opened a branch in Lagos, providing a wide range of commercial banking services to local businesses and individuals.

A year earlier, Chase International Investment Corporation, a unit of Chase Manhattan Bank, served as the lead partner in organising Nigerian Textile Mills in Lagos, regarded as the first major private industrial project with an American interest in Nigeria.

World.title: APC Rally: Shettima, Yari urge Nigerians to re-elect Tinubu, cite APC’s record
World.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in Kaduna State to renew the mandate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying the party is seeking re-election based on projects and policies delivered under President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

Mr Shettima made the appeal on Saturday at the APC campaign rally in Kaduna, where he highlighted the administration’s investments in education and infrastructure as evidence that the party had kept its promises to the state.

The vice president said the administration had worked to restore Kaduna’s position as a centre of learning through the establishment and upgrade of educational institutions.

“We promise to bring back the glory of Kaduna State as the national centre of learning. Didn’t we deliver on that?” he asked supporters at the rally.

He cited the establishment of the Federal University of Applied Sciences and the transition of the Federal University of Education, Zaria, as part of the administration’s interventions in the state.

Mr Shettima also mentioned the establishment of vocational institutes in Rigachikun, Soba and Samaru, saying more than 4,000 people had graduated from the institutions.

He said the administration had also expanded education funding through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which he said had benefited hundreds of thousands of students in universities across the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The vice president further listed major infrastructure projects involving the North, including the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline, Kano-Maradi railway, Lagos-Kano rail corridor and the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano road.

He also cited ongoing work on the Sokoto-Badagry highway, describing it as a project that would create opportunities for agricultural production and economic activity.

Mr Shettima said the APC had demonstrated its commitment to continuity by completing or advancing projects initiated by previous administrations.

He also appealed to voters in the North to support Mr Tinubu’s bid for a second term, arguing that the President had demonstrated political support for northern leaders over the years.

He recalled Mr Tinubu’s support for Atiku Abubakar when the former vice president left the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), as well as his backing of Nuhu Ribadu in the 2011 presidential election and Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 and 2019 elections.

Mr Shettima said Mr Tinubu’s relationship with the North therefore predated his presidency.

The vice president also praised Kaduna Governor Uba Sani, saying his administration had helped promote unity across the state and spread the benefits of governance beyond metropolitan Kaduna.

He urged the people of Kaduna to maintain their support for the APC at the federal and state levels.

“We have the courage to come to Kaduna today because we have kept our promise to never relegate you,” he said.

Also speaking at the rally, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council and former Zamfara State governor, Abdul’aziz Yari, claimed that about two million farmers had committed to supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

Mr Yari said the administration’s policies on agriculture, the economy, education, healthcare and social intervention programmes would form part of the APC’s campaign message ahead of the 2027 election.

He said the party would campaign on its record rather than promises, citing what he described as improvements in the exchange rate, foreign reserves and other economic indicators.

Mr Yari, a serving senator, also pledged support for Mr Tinubu across Northern Nigeria, saying the region was committed to securing the president’s re-election in 2027.

“Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent, by God’s grace, for you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

The Kaduna rally is part of the APC’s nationwide mobilisation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

World.title: APC Rally: Tinubu speaks on second term ambition, promises prosperity, development
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday sought Nigerians’ support for his re-election in 2027, promising sustained economic recovery, prosperity and development.

Mr Tinubu made the appeal on Saturday at the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna.

He thanked Nigerians for electing him in 2023, saying a renewed mandate would enable his administration to sustain ongoing reforms and development projects.

The president blamed previous administrations for the hunger and poverty criticised by opposition parties, saying his government was working to address the challenges.

He cited regular salary payments, economic recovery and efforts to combat corruption and fuel smuggling as areas of his administration’s commitment.

Mr Tinubu urged eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the 2027 general election.

Earlier, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, said the federal government had completed more than 348 kilometres of roads in the North-west, while 1,800 kilometres had been partially completed.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Umahi said ongoing federal road projects in the zone covered 4,083 kilometres, out of about 17,000 kilometres nationwide.

He highlighted the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano road project, saying 81 kilometres of its 118-kilometre first section would be commissioned at the ceremony.

According to him, the first section was completed in 13 months, while more than 144 kilometres of the 164-kilometre second section had been completed.

Mr Umahi said the remaining 20 kilometres of the second section were expected to be completed by the end of November.

He added that Mr Tinubu had directed the installation of solar streetlights along the 375-kilometre Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano corridor.

The minister commended the president for funding the projects and Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, for his efforts towards their completion.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that highlights of the occasion was the presentation of campaign flags to the seven APC governorship candidates in the North-west.

(NAN)

World.title: APC Rally: Tinubu has delivered on key promises to Kaduna, North –  Gov Sani
World.content:
Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, stating that the president has delivered on key promises on infrastructure, security, education and human capital development.

Mr San stated this at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday, where he highlighted projects and interventions he said had changed the fortunes of the state and the North since the administration came into office.

The governor said the president’s performance should be the basis for voters’ decision in the 2027 election, rather than regional considerations.

He recalled Mr Tinubu’s campaign visit to Birnin Gwari in Kaduna State on 22 December 2022, when the area was a major security flashpoint in the North-west.

According to Mr Sani, the president had promised during that visit to reconstruct the Kaduna-Birnin Gwari road and tackle insecurity along the corridor.

He said the federal government had since released N178 billion for the 123-kilometre road project, which he said was ongoing.

Mr Sani also claimed that the security situation had significantly improved, making it possible to travel to Birnin Gwari without police escort.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“When someone came to us and said we should support him simply because he is a northerner, we asked him: can you show us your track record?” the governor said.

“But at this moment, the so-called northern candidate, what is his track record? No track record.”

He challenged the opposition to show comparable infrastructure projects delivered during its time in government, particularly in the North.

M Sani also credited the Tinubu administration with reopening schools and primary healthcare centres previously shut because of insecurity.

He said eight local government areas in Kaduna had been affected by insecurity when his administration assumed office in 2023, with more than 300 schools and 150 primary healthcare centres shut.

“Today, I’m happy to inform you that all the schools and primary healthcare centres have reopened,” he said.

The governor also cited the Zaria-Funtua and Kaduna-Abuja-Kano road projects among the federal interventions in Kaduna and the North.

He said the federal government had committed N740 billion to the reconstruction of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano road and that about 95 per cent of the project had been completed.

Mr Sani further said Kaduna was selected as the pilot state for a metropolitan rail project, with $865 million approved and $300 million reportedly released for the project.

Beyond infrastructure, the governor highlighted the federal government’s student loan and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) interventions.

He said the North-west had received N84 billion under the student loan programme, benefiting about 414,000 students, while 34,000 people in the region had benefited from the government’s TVET programme.

READ ALSO: Shettima banters with Fulani friends over refusal to enrol children in school

Mr Sani said these interventions were particularly significant in a region where agriculture remains a major part of the economy and where many young people require skills to improve their livelihoods.

He also cautioned APC supporters against what he described as opposition attempts to deploy Artificial Intelligence in the 2027 campaign.

“The opposition have now upgraded their campaign from Facebook and Twitter to AI,” he said, urging APC supporters to be vigilant.

The warning came as the APC Presidential Campaign Council separately accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of allegedly planning to use manipulated images, fake documents and AI-generated content to discredit the Kaduna rally. The council did not provide evidence for all the allegations.

The APC campaign opened in Kaduna on Saturday, with Mr Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima and other party leaders attending the rally as the ruling party begins its nationwide campaign for the 2027 presidential election.

World.title: Shettima banters with Fulani friends over refusal to enrol children in school
World.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima was seen on Friday exchanging banter with a group of Fulani men in Maiduguri, urging them to enrol their children in schools built by the Borno State Government.

​Mr Shettima was in the state to inaugurate key infrastructure projects, including a 400-bed teaching hospital at the state-owned Kashim Ibrahim University and the Yerwa Practice Mega School in Maiduguri.

​During the visit, the vice president exchanged greetings with some Fulani acquaintances who work as security guards at the facility.

Adorned in traditional turbans, the men warmly welcomed Mr Shettima, reminiscing as he inquired after familiar faces missing from the group.

​In a video seen by our reporter, Mr Shettima pointed out a face in the gathering and expressed pleasant surprise at how much a young boy he once knew had grown into adulthood.

He also asked after a woman he fondly referred to as his mother; the group explained that unforeseen circumstances had prevented her from attending.

​In a playful gesture, the vice president reached into the breast pocket of one of the men and pulled out a small pocket mirror. Laughing, he turned around to show it to Borno State Governor Babagana Zulum, who stood behind him.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

​Mr Shettima subsequently presented a cash gift to the group, instructing them to share it among themselves while reiterating his call for them to prioritise education.

​”The governor has built schools, but you are not enrolling your children. What is the problem?” Mr Shettima asked.
