​When they responded that they were still searching for a suitable school, the vice president pointed toward a nearby school where their children and younger siblings could be enrolled.

Governor Zulum then stepped in, assuring the group that the state government would help resolve any hurdles they faced, before Mr Shettima departed to catch his flight.

Mr Shettima later posted about the encounter on Facebook.

“I reunited with my Fullo cousins, who are entrusted with the safety and security of Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital, in Maiduguri today. How I’ve missed their warmth, wit and good-natured banter!”

READ ALSO: Vice President Shettima arrives Jigawa for flagship investment summit

The projects commissioning

The vice president also shared how he commissioned some projects in the state during the visit.

“I commissioned landmark projects in Maiduguri, Borno State, comprising the ultra-modern Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital (KIUTH) and two schools.

“In my remarks, I said President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s reform agenda places strong emphasis on building enduring institutions, developing human capital and improving the quality of life of Nigerians.

“I stressed why sustainable development must outlive the tenure of political officeholders, especially how the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu is designed to ensure that economic reforms deliver lasting social benefits, with investments in essential public services.

“Indeed, investments in healthcare and education are essential to economic productivity, national development and the recovery of communities affected by insecurity”, he stated.

World.title: PluggedIN 2026: Brands, creators explore IP ownership, sustainable partnerships
World.content:
Nigerian content creators and brand executives have called for stronger collaboration to build sustainable creative businesses, as the second edition of PluggedIN brought industry stakeholders together in Lagos.

Woof Studios Africa and Insight Redefini organised the event on Thursday at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, under the theme, “Beyond the Placement: Rethinking How Brands Work with Creators.”

Hosted by actress and media personality Bisola Aiyeola, the event explored how brands, advertising agencies, and digital creators could move beyond one-off sponsored posts to develop original content, digital series and intellectual property capable of generating long-term commercial value.

Building on its inaugural edition in 2025, PluggedIN expanded its engagement with brands through panel discussions, a creator showcase, small-group conversations and one-on-one meetings designed to turn creative ideas into funded productions, campaign briefs and lasting partnerships.

Bridging the creators-brands gap

Speaking at the event, Babatunde Olaifa, Group Chief Executive Officer of Insight Redefini, said meaningful collaboration was essential to the growth of Africa’s creator economy.

He argued that brands needed to recognise creators as intellectual property owners capable of developing original ideas, rather than treating them solely as influencers hired to promote products.

“The creator economy has flipped; it is no longer a secondary channel; it is the absolute frontline of consumer engagement in Africa today.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“If your brand is not collaborating with creators as intellectual property owners, not just influencers, you are already behind,” Mr Olaifa said.

According to him, Insight Redefini sought to bring its portfolio of major clients into conversations with creators, with clearly defined briefs, budgets and long-term partnership opportunities.

Founder and Creative Director of Woof Studios Africa, Adetutu Laditan, also added that the initiative was designed to bridge the gap between creative talent and the funding, production and distribution resources needed to develop commercially viable projects.

She noted that creators were increasingly thinking beyond individual viral videos, but needed support to turn their ideas into sustainable businesses.

“Nigerian creators are thinking bigger, and that is exactly what forward-thinking brands want to be part of.

“Our job at Woof Studios is to manage the business and production complexities, the funding, the producing, the distribution, so that a viral skit can become a sustainable series, a film, a franchise,” Ms Laditan said.

The Woof Studios founder added that revenue from YouTube’s advertising programme alone was insufficient to build a sustainable industry, stressing the need for stronger connections between creators, investors and brands.

She said bringing the two groups together was particularly timely, as many companies were planning their 2027 budgets and investments in the final quarter of the year.

According to her, creators who understood brands’ business objectives and could show how their ideas would deliver value would be better positioned to secure partnerships while developing their own projects.

Into brands, creators demand

A major highlight was a brand panel moderated by Esosa Osagiede, Group Creative Director at Insight Redefini, which examined what companies considered when selecting creators for partnerships.

The panel featured Adeyinka Jemi-Alade, Head of Integrated Marketing Communications at TGI Group; Bolaji Popoola, Media and Consumer Experience Manager at Mondelez International; Chisom Bikawei, Media Communications Manager at Nestlé Nigeria; Francis Obiajulu, Senior Brand Manager for Amstel Malta and Hi-Malt; and Sam Okolie, Head of Mainstream Spirit at Guinness Nigeria.

The panellists identified brand alignment, audience trust and genuine influence as key considerations, noting that follower counts and video views alone did not necessarily translate into meaningful audience engagement or consumer action.

They also emphasised the importance of establishing shared objectives, understanding target audiences and giving creators room to develop content that reflects their identities while meeting commercial goals.

The discussions highlighted a shift toward collaborations that let brands to help develop original stories and formats, rather than relying solely on isolated promotional posts.

Aproko, Taaoma, Layi share experiences

The creator showcase featured digital personalities including Aproko Doctor, Taaooma, Layi Wasabi, Osas Ighodaro, Bolaji Ogunmola, Ify’s Kitchen and Folagade Banks, popularly known as Mama Deola.

The creators presented their work and discussed how their platforms and creative ideas could translate into broader commercial opportunities.

A separate conversation, hosted by Aiyeola, featured Kiekie, Jay On-Air, Craze Clown and Winifred Nwania of Zeelicious Food. They shared perspectives on working with brands while maintaining creative independence, retaining audiences and building businesses around their content.

Other featured creators included Biodun Stephen, Afropolitan, Geena Foodies n Spice and Shank Comics.

Group Chief Operating Officer (GCOO) and General Manager of Insight Redefini, Babatunde Shobanjo, described the initiative as a positive development for the marketing communications industry, highlighting the importance of creating platforms where brands and creators could explore new ways of working together.

Looking Beyond Nigeria

Ms Laditan said Woof Studios Africa was also considering extending the initiative into other African markets, including Ghana, Kenya and South Africa.

She, however, stressed the importance of establishing a successful model in Nigeria before expanding elsewhere.

“Nigeria is probably the biggest creator market, even a creative market,” she said, adding that successful initiatives in the country could provide a model for other markets.

She said the immediate priority was to demonstrate that creators could build sustainable businesses through structured partnerships, creating a model that could subsequently be adapted across the continent.

The event comes amid growing interest in digital video and creator-led content as channels for reaching audiences.

YouTube previously reported that watch time in Nigeria increased by more than 50 per cent year-on-year in 2025, with the platform reaching more than 30 million adults monthly.

PluggedIN 2026 sought to build on this growing interest by creating a platform for creators and brands develop practical commercial relationships, with an emphasis on turning creative talent into sustainable businesses.

World.title: Jigawa sign $10 million deal with Indian firm to build modern hatchery
World.content:
As part of its agricultural transformation efforts, the Jigawa State Government has signed a $10 million Joint Venture Agreement with India’s Srinivasa Farms Private Limited for the establishment of a modern hatchery in the state.

The agreement provides for Srinivasa Farms to hold 60 percent equity in the venture, while the Jigawa State Government will own the remaining 40 percent, as the proposed facility is expected to be the first modern hatchery of its kind in Northern Nigeria.

Governor Malam Umar Namadi, who presided over the signing ceremony, described the partnership as an important stage in the state’s agricultural transformation efforts and expressed confidence that it would create new opportunities for poultry farmers.

“I am confident that this project will revolutionize the poultry industry, not only in Jigawa State and Northern Nigeria, but across the country. It is also part of our efforts to support the federal government’s agenda on food security,” the governor said.

He stated that the partnership followed engagements with Srinivasa Farms, including a visit to its facilities in India, where the state delegation observed its poultry operations and programmes for supporting smallholder farmers.

“The way the company empowers smallholder farmers, helping them to grow and establish sustainable businesses, greatly impressed us. We believe that Jigawa State has many poultry farmers who have struggled year after year, facing several challenges and making losses.

“With this joint venture, I believe the poultry industry will thrive in Jigawa State, Insha Allah.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The signed agreement contains provisions for training, technical guidance, and other forms of support to help smallholder poultry farmers improve their production and business operations.

The governor said the hatchery agreement was one of five partnerships being pursued following his visit to India as part of the state government’s effort to attract investment, strengthen agricultural value chains, and create opportunities for young people.

Making his remarks, the Srinivasa Farms’ Vice President, Mr. Senthil Kumar Krishnan, said the joint venture would focus on empowering rural communities and improving poultry production efficiency through technical services and quality products.

He said that farmers in Jigawa currently depend on supplies of day-old chicks from distant locations, including Kaduna, with long transportation periods sometimes affecting the quality of the birds upon arrival.

“By producing the chicks locally, we will be able to address these challenges. We will work with the government to provide the best possible support to farmers so that they can obtain quality chicks when they need them.

“Beyond supplying the chicks, we will also extend technical support to farmers, guiding them on how to raise the birds and achieve better results. Better production performance will translate into improved profitability for farmers. That is our main target.”

Furthermore, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Abdurrahman Lawal, said the investment would address some of the most persistent constraints facing poultry farmers, particularly the high cost and unreliable supply of day-old chicks.

He explained that many chicks supplied to farmers in the northern region are transported from production centers in southern Nigeria, covering distances estimated at between 1,200 and 1,500 kilometers.

“This long journey affects their condition and slows their response to feeding,” he said.

With the proposed hatchery in Jigawa, he said transportation distances within the state would be significantly reduced, with no location expected to be more than approximately 150 kilometers from the facility.

“We have also made plans to establish delivery facilities and involve young people in the distribution of these day-old chicks. The state government has further indicated its commitment to providing a support scheme that will offer relief to farmers in the course of production.”

The agreement was signed on behalf of the Jigawa State Government by the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Abdurrahman Lawal, while Mr. Senthil Kumar Krishnan signed for Srinivasa Farms Private Limited

World.title: Kaduna govt debunks alleged N2.3trn APC campaign funding letter
World.content:
The Kaduna State Government has dismissed as a deliberate fabrication a letter circulating on social media alleging that Governor Uba Sani approved and released N2.3 trillion for the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna, describing the document as fraudulent, misleading and a calculated attempt to undermine the Governor’s reputation for fiscal prudence and responsible governance.

In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Ahmed Maiyaki, the government described the purported letter, dated 18 October 2026, and titled “Notification for Preparations for the Grand Rally Flag Off,” as a figment of the imagination of its authors, riddled with inconsistencies that raise serious questions about its authenticity.

The letter, purportedly addressed by Governor Uba Sani to Senator Abdulazeez Yari, identified as Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, falsely claims that the Governor budgeted and released N2.3 trillion for the presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Saturday, 24 October 2026.

Maiyaki pointed out that the entire 2026 Kaduna State budget stands at N985.92 billion, making the alleged N2.3 trillion expenditure more than twice the state’s annual budget. He described the claim as financially implausible and unsupported by any authentic appropriation, approval or expenditure records.

He further identified glaring irregularities in the purported correspondence, including the misspelling of the Governor’s surname as “Uba Sai” and discrepancies in its presentation, which cast further doubt on the document’s credibility. The government also raised serious concerns over the apparent reproduction of the Governor’s signature without authorisation.

“The Kaduna State Government categorically disowns this document. Governor Uba Sani neither authored nor authorised the purported letter, and no N2.3 trillion was budgeted, approved or released for the presidential campaign flag-off. The allegation is entirely fictitious and represents a deliberate attempt to mislead the public,” Maiyaki stated.

The Commissioner emphasised that since assuming office on 29 May 2023, Governor Uba Sani has demonstrated a consistent commitment to fiscal discipline, transparency, accountability and the judicious management of public resources, prioritising investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He noted that the administration’s financial management philosophy is reflected in its extensive infrastructure programme, increased agricultural investment, rehabilitation of public institutions, settlement of inherited pension liabilities and expansion of social protection interventions aimed at improving the welfare of Kaduna citizens.

Maiyaki expressed concern over what he described as an emerging pattern of coordinated misinformation intended to discredit the Governor and his administration ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that the deliberate fabrication of official correspondence is criminal and punishable.

“Political competition must be conducted within the bounds of truth, decency and the law. The fabrication of government correspondence and circulation of false financial claims cannot be justified as legitimate political criticism. Those seeking to hold government accountable must do so through credible evidence, not manufactured documents,” he stressed.

The Commissioner disclosed that steps were being taken to establish the origin of the purported letter and called on relevant security and investigative agencies to examine the document, take steps to bring to justice for offences involving forgery or impersonation, and take appropriate action against anyone found culpable in accordance with the law.

He urged members of the public and media organisations to exercise caution in circulating unverified documents, emphasising that allegations concerning public expenditure should be subjected to proper scrutiny and verification before publication.

Maiyaki reaffirmed that Governor Uba Sani remains focused on consolidating peace, strengthening public institutions, accelerating infrastructure development and improving citizens’ welfare, stressing that the administration would not be distracted from its commitment to prudent financial management, transparent governance and sustainable development.

World.title: Obidient Movement to Umahi: Don’t associate Obi with IPOB; stop smear campaign
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

The Obidient Movement has condemned, in very strong terms, moves by the Minister of Works, Senator Dave Umahi, to associate the Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, ahead of the January 16, 2027 election, Peter Obi with the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB).

The Obidient Movement has asked the former Ebonyi State governor to put a stop to what it described as the smear campaign against Obi and answer the questions hanging over his alleged criminal records.

In a statement signed on Saturday by Obidient Movement Director, Media and Communications Directorate, Onyeka Dike, he said the group will not be distracted by attempts to demonise its supporters, stressing that their focus remains on a New Nigeria where public officials are accountable, citizens can exercise their rights freely, and every human life matters.

According to him, Nigerians support candidates for different reasons, including their records, policy positions, integrity and vision for the country, saying that attempting to reduce a broad democratic movement to a separatist organisation is an insult to the intelligence of millions of citizens exercising their political rights.

The statement read: “The Obidient Movement condemns David Umahi’s attempt to associate Peter Obi with the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), an allegation contradicted by IPOB’s own public statements and its history of hostility towards Obi’s political ambitions.

“In August 2022, IPOB explicitly declared that it had nothing in common with Peter Obi, accused him of playing what it called “dirty Nigerian politics,” and warned politicians against linking the organisation to his presidential campaign. In July 2022, it had similarly disowned his presidential bid and insisted that Obi was neither a member nor a supporter of its separatist cause.

“So, what exactly is Umahi trying to achieve by resurrecting an allegation that IPOB itself has repeatedly rejected?

If Umahi is suggesting that the millions of Nigerians who support Peter Obi are members of IPOB, he should provide evidence rather than throw reckless allegations into public discourse. If he means that a substantial proportion of South Easterners who support Obi belong to IPOB, he should state that claim clearly and produce verifiable evidence. He cannot casually smear an entire political movement and expect Nigerians to accept his assertions without scrutiny. Support for Peter Obi is not proof of membership in IPOB.

“Nigerians support candidates for different reasons, including their records, policy positions, integrity and vision for the country. Attempting to reduce a broad democratic movement to a separatist organisation is an insult to the intelligence of millions of citizens exercising their political rights.

“Indeed, Peter Obi has publicly condemned violence associated with enforced sit-at-home orders and has called for dialogue and lawful solutions to the insecurity affecting the South East. His political position cannot honestly be reduced to an association that IPOB itself has repeatedly denied.

“Umahi should stop pointing accusing fingers at others while questions about his criminal records remain unanswered.

“Over the years, serious allegations have been made against Umahi concerning violence and killings in Ebonyi State. Such allegations must be investigated on their evidence and merits, rather than dismissed or weaponised according to political convenience.

“The circumstances surrounding the five NELAN Consulting Engineers who disappeared in Ebonyi State in November 2021, after a disagreement with David Umahi during his tenure as governor of Ebonyi State remain unresolved. Umahi later publicly said they had been killed, but their families have continued to demand answers and challenge aspects of the official account. Umahi seems to know more than the security agencies are interested in investigating.

“Also, the death of Mary Habila, a 26-year-old member of the medical team attached to Umahi, also demand transparency. Habila died at Umahi’s residence in Ebonyi State on June 27, 2026. The police announced an investigation and said a post-mortem examination was necessary to establish the cause of death. Ever since then, the case appears to have been swept under the carpet and has suddenly disappeared from public scrutiny.

“The wider crisis of insecurity in the South-East also demands honest leadership.

“Communities have suffered killings, threats, disruption of businesses and fear, instigated by thugs affiliated with people like Umahi who believe in violence as a means of holding political power. Some of those thugs were recently killed by security forces in Ebonyi, Umahi’s home state, when they attacked the NDC House of Assembly Candidate for Ezza South Constituency, Mr. Rollins Offia Nwali.

“Umahi must understand that criticism of Peter Obi does not erase the questions Nigerians are entitled to ask about his own record. Umahi should produce evidence for his allegations, support a transparent investigation into Mary Habila’s death and the deaths of the NELAN 5, and answer legitimate questions about his record. Nigerians deserve facts, accountability and security, not political smears.

“The Obidient Movement will not be distracted by attempts to demonise its supporters. Our focus remains on a New Nigeria where public officials are accountable, citizens can exercise their rights freely, and every human life matters.”

World.title: 2027: Obi stingy, unfit for presidency, Wike declares
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has described the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Peter Obi, as a stingy man who is unfit to govern Nigeria.

Wike, who spoke at a town hall interactive meeting with stakeholders in Bonny Local Government, Rivers State, mocked the former Anambra State governor’s habit of carrying his own bags.

“As a former governor, you cannot be stingy not to have employed a personal assistant who will carry your bag. You want to show you carry your bag. We don’t want such a stingy person as a president,” he said.

He called Obi a social media presidential contender, arguing that popularity online was no substitute for the experience and capacity required to govern the country.

“Truly speaking, I gave him president of social media. If you were to vote who will be president of social media, I will vote for him. But if it is to govern Nigeria, it is capital no!” Wike said.

The minister questioned Obi’s record as Anambra governor, saying the performance of the incumbent, Chukwuma Soludo, should inform public assessment of the former governor’s administration.

He also took a swipe at politicians who switch parties in the face of internal crises, saying leadership required the ability to confront challenges rather than flee them.

“How will you solve the problem of the country? Did you see when there was a problem in PDP? Did I run? I defeated them,” he said.

Wike expressed doubts about the leadership of the African Democratic Congress ADC presidential ticket and the reliability of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, whom he said he had known from their days in the Peoples Democratic Party PDP.

He declared support for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress APC, saying the party offered the platform he would back in the 2027 presidential election.

On the previous Rivers State administration, Wike urged voters to scrutinise the records of politicians seeking higher office instead of relying on campaign declarations.

He alleged that $39 million was spent on a proposed 1,000-bed Justice Karibi-Whyte Specialist Hospital without the project reaching the foundation stage.

“Thirty-nine million US dollars, 53 billion naira, gone! As I speak to you, there is no foundation, no one block laid,” he said.

He claimed that about N60 billion was spent on the state’s monorail project, and questioned its functionality and the value it had delivered to residents.

On the sale of a gas turbine, Wike alleged that the transaction was worth $308 million, yet only $308,000 remained in the relevant state account when he assumed office in May 2015.

He also recalled a proposal to spend $10 million on fumigating Rivers State to address mosquito bites, questioning the logic of such an exercise in a state sharing boundaries with several others.

Wike announced that the Rainbow Coalition would unveil its candidates on Tuesday, October 27, and named Kingsley Chinda as its choice for the Rivers State governorship race.

He said some of the candidates would contest under the APC, even though the coalition’s membership cuts across party lines.

“Under the Rainbow Coalition in our state today, you see APC, PDP, all of us. No more Rivers of blood, no more shooting, not many people going to die,” Wike said.

The minister urged residents to back candidates he described as experienced and committed to public service, and promised that the concerns raised by Bonny residents would receive attention.

He praised the completion of the Bonny-Bodo Road, saying it had improved access to the island community and reduced the hardship residents previously faced travelling by boat. He said he had told Tinubu that the road was a major achievement for the people of Bonny.

World.title: Nigeria-Indonesia investment to boost GDP, create jobs, says NICCI president, Balogun
World.content:
By Favour Ulebor

The President of the Nigerian Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, NICCI, Ishmael Balogun, has said increased investment between Nigeria and Indonesia, particularly in oil and gas exploration, will boost Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product, GDP, create jobs and promote knowledge transfer.

Balogun spoke during the Nigerian Indonesian Investment and Trade Forum, NIITF, which held its fifth edition in Jakarta from October 20 to 21, 2026, with a focus on expanding bilateral trade and investment in oil and gas, renewable energy, agriculture, pharmaceuticals and infrastructure development.

He said stronger economic cooperation between the two countries would enable Nigerian businesses to access more opportunities in Indonesia while attracting foreign direct investment into Nigeria.

According to him, the chamber, established in 1997 to promote bilateral trade between Nigeria and Indonesia, currently has about 155 corporate members operating across several sectors, including oil and gas, agriculture, renewable energy, manufacturing, infrastructure and pharmaceuticals.

Balogun said the chamber also facilitated transactions among its members, with intra chamber transactions exceeding N1 billion annually.

He said trade between Nigeria and Indonesia had grown from $2 billion in 2020 to $2.7 billion in 2021, $2.9 billion in 2022 and $4.5 billion in 2023.

According to him, Indonesia purchases about $3 billion worth of crude oil from Nigeria annually, while Nigerian businesses import pharmaceutical products, palm oil, electronics and fast moving consumer goods from Indonesia.

He added that Indonesia also imports agricultural commodities from Nigeria, providing opportunities for businesses in both countries.

Balogun said the chamber established the Nigerian Indonesian Investment and Trade Forum in 2022 to create a platform for Nigerian investors to explore opportunities in Indonesia and encourage Indonesian businesses to invest in Nigeria.

He said previous editions had attracted government officials, diplomats and private sector representatives from both countries, leading to the signing of memoranda of understanding and further business engagements.

The NICCI president said the 2026 edition focused on oil and gas, renewable energy, agriculture, aquaculture, animal husbandry, pharmaceuticals and infrastructure development.

He said increased cooperation in oil exploration could have a more direct impact on Nigeria’s economy than trade alone, particularly through job creation, technology transfer and increased investment.

Balogun disclosed that an Indonesian government and business delegation had recently visited Nigeria for discussions with Nigerian officials and key players in the oil and gas sector.

Balogun said Nigeria had traditionally supplied crude oil to Indonesia through third party arrangements, but discussions were ongoing on establishing a more direct government to government relationship that could open up investment opportunities in exploration.

He said such investments could generate employment, improve technical knowledge and bring billions of dollars into Nigeria’s economy.

Balogun said the chamber was also working to make Indonesian products, companies and investment opportunities more accessible to Nigerian businesses that could not afford to travel to Indonesia.

He cited the chamber’s engagements during Food and Beverage West Africa in Lagos and the Kano Indonesian Expo, where Indonesian companies were invited to meet Nigerian businesses and explore commercial partnerships.

He said the chamber had also recorded increased participation by Nigerian businesses at the Indonesian Trade Expo, adding that 150 visitor visas were issued by the Indonesian Embassy in Nigeria for the Nigerian delegation to participate in this year’s activities.

Balogun maintained that the chamber was committed to strengthening business relations in both directions by helping Nigerian companies explore Indonesia and encouraging Indonesian companies to establish partnerships and investments in Nigeria.

Meanwhile, the Chief Executive Officer of Prime Next Logistics Ltd, Giorgio Enrico Del Celo, said international trade exhibitions provided opportunities for businesses to build relationships and identify potential partners across different markets.

Del Celo, an Italian who said he had lived in Nigeria for more than three decades, said his company’s participation in the trade expo was aimed at expanding its network and connecting with businesses from different countries.

“This Trade Expo and the next event next week is an opportunity, of course, for a freight forwarder to get connected with more and more people,” he said.

He explained that the company provided freight forwarding services, connecting people and cargo to and from Nigeria and other parts of West Africa.

According to him, the relationships established at international trade events might not immediately translate into business but could develop into commercial opportunities over time.

Del Celo said doing business in Nigeria required knowledge, patience, consistency and trust.

The logistics executive said businesses needed to build credibility and maintain reliable relationships with clients to achieve sustainable growth.

He said, “It’s not easy to do business in Nigeria. Let’s say the truth. Whoever says that it’s easy to do business, it’s not true.

“Trust is the main word. If you don’t have trust, no business. It’s very difficult to do business,” he said.

Del Celo, whose company recently marked 10 years of operation, said his experience in Nigeria had made him feel at home.

World.title: 2027: Enugu ADC alleges attacks, demands level playing field
World.content:
By Anayo Okoli

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Enugu State has called on the state government to ensure a level playing field for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, alleging attacks on opposition supporters and urging authorities to prevent political violence.

The party’s governorship candidate, Ocho Obodoeze, made the call after receiving an award from the Correspondents Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Enugu State Council.

Obodoeze accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of suppressing opposition parties and urged the state government to allow all political parties to campaign freely in accordance with the law.

He also called on the government to fulfil its responsibility of protecting lives and property amid concerns over reported political violence in the state.

“Enugu State Government should allow every political party to campaign in the state, in line with the Electoral Act and guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the 2027 general election.

“The government should desist from muzzling opposition parties. Instead, they should allow them to campaign freely like the ruling party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), is doing. Election is not a do-or-die affair. The will of the people must be allowed to prevail,” he said.

Obodoeze dedicated his award to Ifeanyi Christopher Nworie, who reportedly died from gunshot injuries allegedly sustained during an attack on supporters of the opposition New Democratic Congress (NDC).

Describing the gesture as emotional, the ADC candidate recalled that Nworie died from injuries he sustained during an attack by gunmen on an opposition party’s campaign office in Enugu on October 10, 2026.

He alleged that the incident reflected a pattern of attacks against opposition parties since political activities began ahead of the 2027 elections.

The Enugu State Government, however, has denied involvement in political attacks in the state, insisting that opposition parties are free to campaign and criticise Governor Peter Mbah’s administration.

Meanwhile, the Enugu State chapter of the ADC has congratulated Obodoeze on the award presented to him during the Correspondents Chapel’s 2026 Press Week celebration.

In a statement signed by the party’s state secretary, A. C. Udeh, the ADC described the award as well deserved and a morale booster for its members ahead of the 2027 elections.

“The prestigious award is a clear testament that NUJ has discovered and recognised the uncommon good qualities embedded in our governorship candidate,” the party said.

It described Obodoeze as humble, compassionate and committed to the welfare of ordinary citizens, expressing confidence in his capacity to lead the state if elected governor.

The party also pledged that an Obodoeze administration would reduce what it described as high and multiple taxation burdening residents of Enugu State.

It further promised to prioritise the welfare of workers and pensioners, describing its candidate as accessible and committed to the development and prosperity of the state.

World.title: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has blamed his political opponents for hunger and poverty in Nigeria, insisting that his administration is working to address the challenges.

Tinubu spoke on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign flag-off rally at Ranchers Bees Stadium, also known as Kaduna Township Stadium, in Kaduna State, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“I have an argument. I hear my opponent talking about hunger, poverty. Who created it? They did! They created the hunger, they created the poverty. We are trying to eradicate it,” the president said.

He also defended his administration’s record on salary payments and commended state governors for their performance, saying they were making progress in their respective states.

“We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing,” Tinubu said.

The president thanked Kaduna residents for supporting him in the previous presidential election, saying their votes contributed to his emergence as president.

“You gave me joy to remember the victory you gave me to become president. I come again to thank you,” he said.

Tinubu appealed to Nigerians to give him another term, saying he wanted to sustain his promises of prosperity, continuity, progress and development.

World.title: EPL: Arsenal see off Everton, go joint-top after Man City defeat
World.content:
Arsenal’s Brazilian defender #06 Gabriel Magalhaes (R) heads home their second goal during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Everton at the Emirates Stadium in London on October 24, 2026.
