Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Manchester City’s flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton.

Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons.

Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery’s men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side.

Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game.

“We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box,” said Maresca.

The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window.

But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong.

The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes.

Another of Villa’s new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves.

Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise.

Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson’s low shot on the hour mark.

“A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park,” said Emery.

“We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic.”

– Arsenal’s set-piece prowess –

Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton.

Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done.

Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes.

Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta’s men midway through the second period.

Fulham further eased the pressure on manager Alvaro Arbeloa with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb’s individual effort.

A second consecutive victory propels the Cottagers out of the relegation zone and up to 12th.

Tottenham are also seeking to escape the bottom three when they travel to Chelsea in the evening kick-off, aiming to improve on a terrible record at Stamford Bridge.

On Sunday the focus turns on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth.

A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick’s future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season.

AFP

World.title: Como follow Man Utd thumping with victory in Serie A
World.content:
Como’s Greek forward #09 Tasos Douvikas (C) celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the UEFA Champions League, league phase matchday 3, football match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia in Como, northen Italy on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP)

Como backed up their brilliant Champions League victory over Manchester United as Anastasios Douvikas scored twice in a 2-0 Serie A win against Sassuolo on Saturday.

Cesc Fabregas’s side climbed to fourth in the table, just two points adrift of early leaders Inter Milan who host Fiorentina on Sunday.

Como were frustrated for long periods by a stubborn Sassuolo team, but clinched an ultimately comfortable win courtesy of Douvikas’s two goals in the space of 11 second-half minutes.

The Greece striker has now scored five goals in his last four games, and eight in all competitions in total this season.

Como, who qualified for Europe for the first time in their history last term, thrashed Man United 4-1 in the Champions League in midweek.

Later Saturday, Roma bid to go top of the table when they visit Napoli, before second-placed Lazio also eye the summit in their home game against Parma.

AFP

World.title: Abia govt has abandoned us — Ubani Market traders cry out, seek Otti’s intervention
World.content:
By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Thirteen years after their relocation from the heart of Umuahia to Ubani Ultra-modern Market, thousands of traders are counting their losses, battling dwindling patronage and watching their businesses crumble as they accuse the Abia State Government of abandoning them.

From collapsing shops overtaken by weeds to deplorable internal roads, heaps of refuse, poor sanitation and the absence of electricity, water and banking facilities, the once-bustling market has become a symbol of dashed hopes for traders who say their compliance with the government’s relocation order has left them economically stranded.

They are now appealing to Governor Alex Otti to urgently intervene before the market, which was conceived as the commercial hub of Umuahia, collapses completely.

Their grievances go beyond decaying infrastructure. They include dwindling sales, the exodus of traders, alleged inconsistency in the enforcement of the market relocation policy, the burden of an annual ₦36,000 levy per shop and the absence of a promised alternative access road which traders say could reduce traffic congestion and road accidents.

The market, formerly known as Umuahia Daily Market, was relocated from the popular Isigate area of the city in 2013 during the administration of former Governor Theodore Orji. Its former site now houses the Umuahia Central Bus Terminal.

When the market was moved to its present location, about seven kilometres from the city centre, between Umuahia and Uzuakoli in Bende Local Government Area, it initially attracted traders and customers in large numbers.

The government had justified the relocation as part of efforts to decongest Umuahia and spread development beyond the city centre. It then provided luxury buses to convey traders and customers to the new market at heavily subsidised rates, while shop owners at the old location were allocated land to construct new shops.

With more than 10,000 lock-up shops, in addition to thousands of open stalls, the market initially enjoyed considerable patronage. It also had facilities including a fire station, conveniences and security posts.

But traders say the initial promise has gradually given way to neglect, with many businesses struggling to survive and some shops abandoned or collapsing.

They trace the deterioration partly to what they describe as the failure of successive administrations, particularly that of former Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, to sustain the original relocation policy.

According to them, the alleged lax enforcement of the relocation order allowed traders to return to available spaces around Isigate and other parts of the city centre, drawing customers away from Ubani and undermining businesses whose owners had complied with the government’s directive.

During a visit to the market by Vanguard, traders recounted painful experiences, describing a deteriorating commercial environment in which some struggle to cover their daily expenses.

‘This market does not look six months old’

A provisions dealer, Mr Ugochukwu Okeke, popularly known as Onwa, identified poor internal roads, lack of electricity, declining patronage and the absence of the promised alternative access road via Umueze as major challenges confronting traders. He said the failure to construct the proposed Ubani–Agbo–Umueze Road had continued to expose road users to the dangers of the busy Umuahia–Uzuakoli Road.

” In 2013 when we were asked to relocate to this place, Government promised to build a shorter route to the market passing through Umueze and Agbo to make it easily accessible from the city but up till today we have not seen it. The other day, a trader was returning to the City after the day’s sales and boarded a tricycle. On their way through the busy Uzuakoli road, a trailer had a break failure and rammed into the Keke. The head of the woman was cut off immediately as a result of the impact. That woman wouldn’t have lost her life if the road Ubani-Agbo -Umueze Road were fixed as promised earlier by Government 13 years ago.

” Another challenge we face here is poor sales due to continued decline in the number of people coming to shop here. This is because of the existence of markets around Isigate. Many traders have continued to pull out of the market back to town and government is doing nothing but just watching helplessly. This is affecting the few of us that are here.

” This is 13 years we were forced to come here but this market does not look as if it has lasted for six months because it is going down everyday.”

Beyond the physical deterioration, Okeke said the absence of banks in and around the market had created security risks for traders who handle cash from daily sales. He recalled an incident in which a neighbouring trader allegedly lost a carton containing money after hiding it among refuse to prevent thieves from stealing the proceeds of his business.

” My neighbour sometime ago lost his carton of money here. He was putting the proceeds of the day’s sales inside the cartoon and kept it in the midst of refuse to avoid being stolen because there is no Bank in the market. Afterwards he collected a carton of refuse thinking it was the one containing money. On getting home he discovered he had forgotten his money outside and tili today he has not found it back.”

The trader also faulted the collection of an annual consolidated levy of ₦36,000 per shop, saying the financial burden had become difficult to bear amid poor sales.He appealed to the government to make the levy payable per trader rather than per shop, as he said was currently the practice.

” Last year they came and said we will be paying N36,000 per annum promising to use the revenue to solve our problems. We paid. The worst thing is that they are collecting this revenue based on the number of shops a trader has in the market. Although we pay, we don’t yet see anything they are doing with it.

” I’m not sure the Governor is aware of this. That’s why I’m appealing to him to look into what is happening at Ubani Ultra-modern Market. We are suffering here. We are just merely surviving by God’s grace. There is no future for this market as long as the same Government continues to allow some traders return to Isigate. We heard that revenue collectors collect revenues from the traders there twice a day. That’s why they are not serious about forcing them out of that place. We are the ones suffering it here”.

‘Our business capital is depreciating’

A patent medicine dealer, Mr Michael Ubani, said the market’s fortunes would continue to decline unless the government enforced its relocation policy and addressed the infrastructure deficit. He said traders who obeyed the relocation directive had been left to bear the consequences while competing markets continued to operate within the city centre.

” We are hopelessly struggling to survive here. This is a stranded place for us because of its distance from the City metropolis. Government is not looking our way. Every effort to get Government’s attention to this market has been fruitless. You can see that traders are pulling from the market on daily basis due to lack of patronage.

” Amenities here are zero – no internal roads, no electricity. The Umueze – Agbo -Ubani road which would have provided a shorter route to the market is a total mess. We are regretting complying with Government’s order to relocate from town to this place 13 years ago. Our business capital is depreciating. You hardly cover your daily expenses here and that is why many traders are existing the market back to town.”

Ubani recalled that traders had protested at Government House last year in an attempt to draw the government’s attention to their plight.

According to him, although the then Commissioner for Trade and Investment promised to convey their complaints to the governor, the promised intervention had yet to materialise.

He said the traders were subsequently informed that the government was not generating revenue from the market, prompting the introduction of the annual ₦36,000 levy per shop.

” We took our matter to Government House last year. Unfortunately we did not meet the Governor but the Commissioner for Trade and Investment then promised to convey our grievances to the Governor. The Commissioner then told us that Government was not getting any revenue from the market. Since then we started paying N36,000 per shop every year. But we haven’t seen any Government intervention.

” We are pleading with the Governor to remember us. Some traders relocated to Imo State in protest when the former Government wanted to relocate to this place in 2013. Those of us who came here in obedience should not be made to think that we made a mistake. Ubani Ultra-modern Market traders need urgent Government intervention otherwise this market may soon shut down completely.

We are begging Gov Otti to hear our cries. This is the only main market in Umuahia capital City. Let the Government close down every other market in the town and ask everybody to be here so that this place can pick up”.

Another trader, Mr Chidiebere Uwakwe, who deals in nylon bags, said the continued operation of markets around Isigate was frustrating efforts to revive Ubani.

He said the deteriorating condition of the market was evident in the number of abandoned and collapsing shops, with traders watching their investments waste away.

” We are just wasting time here. Our business capital is evaporating in our hands. You can see that many shops have already collapsed here. Trees are growing in some of them. These were money of traders waisting due to government’s inconsistency. Why did they force us out of the former site of the Umuahia Daily Market inside town it they knew they were not serious about market relocation.”

Women traders count their losses

For women traders who depend on daily sales to feed their families and meet household expenses, the market’s decline has brought additional hardship.

Mrs Nkechinyere Odinkemere, a vegetable seller, and Mrs Comfort Ikwuagwu, a tomato dealer, corroborated the complaints, appealing to the government to address the traders’ concerns and restore commercial activity.

Ikwuagwu said the market had become unusually quiet despite its status as Umuahia’s main market.

” We are just idling away here. This place used to be busy but can’t you see it looks so dry like a school on vacation. We beg our amiable Governor not to allow this market shut down completely. We know our problem preceded his administration but he can do something for our sake”, Mrs Comfort pleaded.

Odinkemere said the average trader could hardly recover the cost of coming to the market, adding that some continued to open their shops simply because they had nowhere else to go.

She joined the call for the government to curb the proliferation of markets around the city centre and ensure that traders operated from Ubani.

” Since this is called main market, Government should not allow others markets inside the town. Everybody should be compelled to relocate to this place so that it will start to boom again and even attract development around here.”

Market chairman appeals to Otti

The Chairman of Ubani Ultra-Modern Market, Prince Chukwemeka Ebubedike, made a passionate appeal to Governor Alex Otti to rescue thousands of traders battling deteriorating infrastructure and declining business fortunes.

Ebubedike painted a grim picture of failed internal roads, collapsing shops, heaps of refuse, poor sanitation and the absence of basic amenities, including water.

“Our people are suffering,” he lamented. “The roads are bad, the infrastructure is collapsing, rain and wind have destroyed some shops, and refuse litters the market. We are pleading with our Governor to come to our rescue and give this market the attention it deserves.”

The market chairman recalled that the issue had been raised during the governor’s media chat, where Otti reportedly assured that his Chief of Staff would visit the market and that rehabilitation works would commence afterwards.

However, Ebubedike said months had passed without any intervention.

He stressed that traders had remained law-abiding and continued to pay the annual government levy of ₦36,000 per shop despite the difficult conditions.

According to him, the market leadership has also mobilised traders to register for their Permanent Voter Cards and participate actively in the democratic process, insisting that citizens who fulfil their civic and financial obligations deserve the attention and protection of the government.

Ebubedike urged Otti to prioritise the rehabilitation of internal roads, the renovation of dilapidated shops and the construction of the proposed access road linking Ubani Market to Abo Ibeku through Junior Gate.

He argued that the access road would provide an alternative route to the market, ease congestion on the busy Umuahia–Uzuakoli Road, reduce the risk of accidents and improve patronage.

Beyond demands for improved infrastructure in the market, Ubani market traders are appealing for protecting of their livelihoods, recovery of their lost investments and prevention of a once-promising commercial hub from becoming a graveyard of abandoned businesses.

Some residents hold the opinion that if Ubani market is revived, the current quest by money -conscious landlords to convert every available space in the City centre into a shopping plaza would stop.

Ubani market traders call for Government’s urgent intervention. For them, 13 years after complying with the relocation order is long enough for government to fulfil the promises that accompanied their move.

Their plea to Otti is urgent: rehabilitate the market, provide a shorter access road promised by past administrations, address the infrastructure deficit and ensure that traders can earn a living from the place they were directed to call their commercial home.

World.title: Sokoto Residents Challenge ADC Candidate Dan’iya to Present Development Blueprint
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

Concerned residents of Sokoto State have challenged the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, to move beyond criticism of Governor Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto’s administration and unveil a clear and achievable development agenda ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

In a statement jointly signed by Comrade Ibrahim Umar Kware, Comrade Aminu Hali Tambuwal and Comrade Bello Arzika Dandange, on behalf of the group, the residents said the people of the state deserve more than political attacks from those seeking their mandate.

According to the group, the 2027 election should be defined by competing ideas, credible alternatives and concrete solutions to the challenges facing the state, rather than a campaign built solely on fault-finding and condemnation of government policies.

The residents observed that since his emergence as the ADC governorship candidate, Dan’iya has consistently criticised the policies and programmes of the present administration without presenting a comprehensive policy document detailing what he would do differently.

“Enough of criticism. Sokoto people want to know what you intend to do for them. What is your development agenda and how do you intend to deliver on your promises? It is not enough to criticise the government without providing workable alternatives,” the statement said.

They argued that aspiring to govern a state of over five million people requires thorough preparation, clear vision and a sound understanding of public administration, including realistic funding strategies, implementation timelines and measurable performance indicators.

The group further urged Dan’iya to reflect on his tenure as Deputy Governor under former Governor Aminu Waziri Tambuwal and share the lessons learnt, cautioning him against what they described as the shortcomings of his political mentor whom they accused of assuming office without adequate preparation.

While emphasising the need for accountability on the part of the incumbent administration, the residents acknowledged Governor Ahmed Aliyu’s interventions in security logistics, road construction and rehabilitation, housing and primary healthcare revitalisation as efforts that merit objective assessment.

They noted that the provision of operational vehicles, motorcycles and other security equipment to security agencies has enhanced response capacity in parts of the state, even as they admitted that insecurity remains a challenge requiring sustained action.

According to the concerned residents, while the present government must be judged on its performance, the opposition has an equal responsibility to demonstrate superior capacity and offer better alternatives rather than expecting voters to be swayed by criticism alone.

They therefore challenged the ADC candidate to publicly present his specific plans for strengthening security in vulnerable communities, supporting farmers and small businesses, tackling youth unemployment, attracting private investment and improving service delivery across the 23 local government areas of the state, stressing that Sokoto needs a prepared leader with a clear plan.

World.title: NASENI Trains, Empowers 120 Electricians in Modern Electrical Installation in Kogi
World.content:
Ibrahim Oyewale in Lokoja





The National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI) has trained, empowered no fewer 120 electricians in modern electrical installation and maintenance in Kogi State as part of efforts to tackle youths’ unemployment in the country.



The Executive Director/CEO NASENI, Professor Khalid Halilu, disclosed this at the closing ceremony of NASENI Skills Acquisition and Empowerment programme and presentation of certificate to held in Lokoja yesterday.



Professor Halilu explained that NASENI was committed to taking skills acquisition to the door steps of Nigerians, noting that industrialisation goes beyond the machine and structures, but skills acquisition to ignite the industrial revolution in Nigeria.



The executive director however, commended the Kogi State government for their cooperation.



Professor Halilu who was represented by a Coordinating Director of Finance and Account, NASENI, Ibrahim Dauda explained that the agency has trained, empowered a total of 120 electricians in modern electrical installation.



He added that NASENI also gave them money to start their own business, admonished the trainees that their skills placed them in the fastest growing sector of Nigeria economy, the construction sector, so they must key into it immediately.



He warned the trainees not to sell the starter packs, stressing it is a sustainable livelihood tools for them and this will enable start new life.



The traditional ruler and the Chairman of Lokoja Traditional Council, the Maigari of Lokoja, His Royal Highness, Ibrahim Kabir, expressed gratitude to NASENI for the trading of 120 electricians in the modern electrical installation.



“My dear participants, the training you have received from NASENI places a responsibility on you to demonstrate the value of the investment made in your professional development…In this sense, you should regard yourselves as ambassadors of NASENI.



“Your conduct, professional competence; and quality of service will help to shape public perception of the agency and the effectiveness of its training programmes therefore encourage you to put the knowledge and skills acquired here into practical use and allow your work to speak positively about the institution that has invested in you. Be worthy ambassadors through your professionalism, integrity, discipline, diligence, and good conduct.



“Your success will not only benefit you and your families; it will also demonstrate the value of NASENI’s intervention and strengthen the case for similar programmes to be extended to other trades and communities,” the traditional ruler posited.

World.title: HYPREP Empowers 620 Ogoni Indigenes with Scholarships, Disability Skills Training
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Hydrocarbon Pollution Remediation Project (HYPREP) has empowered 620 indigenes of Ogoni in Rivers State through postgraduate scholarship grants and vocational training for persons living with disabilities, as part of efforts to promote inclusive development and sustainable livelihoods in the oil-producing communities.

The interventions saw 500 postgraduate students receive scholarship grants in Port Harcourt on Thursday, October 22, 2026, while 120 persons living with disabilities graduated from vocational training programmes in fashion designing and photography in Bori, Khana Local Government Area, yesterday.

Speaking at the two events, HYPREP Project Coordinator, Prof. Nenibarini Zabbey, said the initiatives reflected the federal government’s commitment to human capital development, inclusive empowerment and the recovery of Ogoni under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

At the scholarship award ceremony in Port Harcourt, Zabbey charged the beneficiaries to deploy their academic knowledge, research and professional expertise towards addressing the developmental challenges facing Ogoni communities.

He described the scholarship scheme as an investment in the region’s future, urging the students to see the grants as a call to service rather than merely financial assistance.

“Education gives you knowledge, but it also places a responsibility on you to use that knowledge to improve society. I encourage you to see this scholarship as a call to service,” he said.

Zabbey urged the postgraduate students to develop innovative solutions, establish professional networks and contribute to building a peaceful and economically sustainable Ogoni.

He explained that the scholarship programme aligned with the recommendations of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), which identified alternative livelihoods and human capacity development as important components of the response to Ogoni’s environmental challenges.

The coordinator acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over delays in disbursement but maintained that HYPREP remained committed to its obligations, noting that public projects required due process, accountability and careful planning.

One of the beneficiaries, Mrs. Bara Uloma Celestine, a PhD student of Mathematics Education at Ignatius Ajuru University of Education, said the grant would ease the financial burden associated with her studies and research.

“Despite all the expenses, I, on behalf of others, am very sure that the sum given to us will go a very long way. Not just to pay our school fees, but to carry out our various research works in our various fields and to publish some things at hand,” she said.

Similarly, Mr. Bienebari Solomon Oscar, a PhD student of Development Studies at the University of Port Harcourt, commended HYPREP for what he described as a transparent process.

“I can attest today, Professor Nenibarini Zabbey has shown that there are still leaders who have people at heart. The transparency of this whole programme and the way of handling everything, we are very satisfied,” he said.

At the graduation ceremony for persons living with disabilities in Bori yesterday, Zabbey said the training marked the fulfilment of an initiative that began in 2023 following appeals by the leadership of the Ogoni Persons Living with Disabilities.

He disclosed that HYPREP commenced vocational training for 300 persons living with disabilities, with the first batch of 120 graduating after completing courses in fashion designing and photography.

The graduates comprised 60 beneficiaries trained in fashion designing and another 60 in photography.

According to him, HYPREP had provided starter packs to enable the beneficiaries to establish businesses immediately after graduation. The project also distributed assistive devices, including wheelchairs, crutches, guide canes, hearing aids and prosthetic legs, to support their mobility and independence.

“What started as an appeal has today become a reality,” Zabbey said, describing the initiative as evidence of HYPREP’s commitment to inclusive development.

He commended the leadership and members of the disability community for their constructive engagement, patience and peaceful approach, which he said helped make the programme possible.

The coordinator urged the graduates to form cooperatives and business clusters to strengthen their enterprises, support one another and expand their economic opportunities.

He also warned them against selling their starter packs and assistive devices, stressing that HYPREP had introduced a post-training monitoring mechanism to track beneficiaries’ progress.

Zabbey said HYPREP’s interventions extended beyond environmental remediation to include potable water, healthcare, education, livelihood support, peacebuilding and community engagement, with the objective of ensuring that no segment of the Ogoni population was left behind.

He expressed optimism that the remaining 180 trainees would graduate in subsequent ceremonies, urging the beneficiaries to become ambassadors of the Project in their communities.

World.title: NEDC Distributes Starter Packs To 20 Beneficiaries for Eco-Friendly Stove, Briquette Production In Bauchi
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi

The North East Development Commission (NEDC) has distributed starter packs to 20 beneficiaries trained in the fabrication of energy-efficient stoves and the production of briquettes in Bauchi State.

The distribution, which took place on Thursday, is part of the commission’s efforts to promote youth empowerment, entrepreneurship, environmental sustainability and economic self-reliance in the North-east region.

Speaking during the handover ceremony, the NEDC Bauchi State Coordinator, Alhaji Aliyu Isyaku, said the equipment was provided to enable the beneficiaries to establish businesses, generate sustainable income and create employment opportunities.

He said the beneficiaries were trained in in 2023 and 2024. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the starter packs, describing the intervention as an opportunity to improve their livelihoods through productive economic activities.

Isyaku highlighted the business potential of energy-efficient stove fabrication and briquette production, noting that the ventures could provide alternative sources of income while helping to protect the environment.

According to him, promoting briquette production and energy-efficient stoves could reduce dependence on firewood, thereby helping to combat deforestation and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

He said the initiative aligned with the NEDC’s mandate to promote sustainable development across the North-east and expressed the commission’s readiness to support similar interventions based on beneficiaries’ commitment and measurable results.

The coordinator described the intervention as a practical investment in youth empowerment, green enterprise development and improved livelihoods.

He also stressed the importance of monitoring beneficiaries’ activities, providing technical guidance and assessing their businesses to ensure that the equipment was properly utilised and the intended objectives achieved.

Also speaking, Alhaji Modu Ali of the commission urged the beneficiaries to take the coordinator’s advice seriously, noting that entrepreneurship and self-reliance were important pathways to sustainable livelihoods and personal development.

Similarly, Sulaiman Ibrahim, another official of the commission, advised the beneficiaries to use the starter packs strictly for their intended purposes.

He assured them of continued monitoring and warned against selling or abandoning the equipment, saying such actions could undermine the objectives of the intervention and attract appropriate sanctions.

In his remarks, Lawal Saidu advised beneficiaries who might have other commitments to consider involving younger relatives or trusted business partners rather than abandoning the opportunity.

He emphasised the need for beneficiaries to diversify their income sources, develop business partnerships and ensure that the intervention translated into lasting economic benefits.

Some of the beneficiaries, including Ibrahim Abubakar and Naimatu Kabir, expressed appreciation to the commission for providing them with the opportunity to establish businesses and improve their economic circumstances.

They said the initiative would not only benefit them individually but also contribute to economic development, environmental protection and job creation in Bauchi State.

Kabir said the training in briquette production would help beneficiaries contribute to their communities by creating employment opportunities, particularly for young people and women.

She noted that indiscriminate tree felling was causing environmental damage and expressed optimism that promoting alternative fuel production could help address deforestation and global warming.

According to her, briquettes produced from waste materials could provide an alternative to conventional charcoal, reducing the need to cut down trees for fuel.

She added that the knowledge and skills acquired during the training had equipped her to train other young people and potentially employ workers as her business expanded.

The beneficiaries expressed hope that the intervention would enable them to establish sustainable businesses, support their families and contribute to the economic development of Bauchi State and the country at large.

World.title: Tinubu Flags off Reelection Campaign in Kaduna, Promises Prosperity, Devt
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday sought Nigerians’ support for his re-election in 2027, promising sustained economic recovery, prosperity and development.

Tinubu made the appeal on Saturday at the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna.

He thanked Nigerians for electing him in 2023, saying a renewed mandate would enable his administration to sustain ongoing reforms and development projects.

The President blamed previous administrations for the hunger and poverty criticised by opposition parties, saying his government was working to address the challenges.

He cited regular salary payments, economic recovery and efforts to combat corruption and fuel smuggling as areas of his administration’s commitment.

Tinubu urged eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the 2027 general election.

Earlier, Minister of Works David Umahi said the Federal Government had completed more than 348 kilometres of roads in the North West, while 1,800 kilometres had been partially completed.

Umahi said ongoing federal road projects in the zone covered 4,083 kilometres, out of about 17,000 kilometres nationwide.

He highlighted the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano road project, saying 81 kilometres of its 118-kilometre first section would be commissioned at the ceremony.

According to him, the first section was completed in 13 months, while more than 144 kilometres of the 164-kilometre second section had been completed.

Umahi said the remaining 20 kilometres of the second section were expected to be completed by the end of November.

He added that Tinubu had directed the installation of solar streetlights along the 375-kilometre Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano corridor.

The minister commended Tinubu for funding the projects and Kaduna Gov. Uba Sani for his efforts towards their completion.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that highlights of the occasion is the presentation of flags to the seven APC governorship candidates in North West.(NAN)

World.title: THE ALTAR OF FIRE, A HEART OF MEEKNESS
World.content:
JERRY EZE

Jerry Eze is minister of God with unblemished integrity, reckons DAN AIBANGBE

The Streams of Joy man, Pastor Jerry Eze is a dynamic prayer general, a fire-brand preacher and a versatile Evangelist. Known for the iconic slogan, What God cannot do, does not exist,

Pastor Jerry consistently demonstrates that God is still in the business of performing extraordinary wonders through men who remain upright, humble, and completely surrendered to Christ

​In an era where spiritual leadership is frequently audited by the metrics of the world, true authority remains a matter of consecration, alignment, and divine endorsement. Few ministers in contemporary Christendom embody this reality as profoundly as Pastor Jerry Eze. Emerging as one of the most remarkable spiritual forces of our time, his life stands as a living testament to what happens when a man lays down professional prestige, yields fully to the Holy Spirit, and chooses a path of absolute consecration. From the corporate corridors of international development to the global stage of intercessory fire, Jerry Eze has redefined modern ministry, proving that signs and wonders are not the products of charisma, but the natural residue of a life lived in unbroken fellowship with God.

​Before millions of believers across continents began tuning in every morning to the New Season Prophetic Prayers and Declarations (NSPPD), Pastor Jerry Eze was building a promising career in international development. Serving as a communications specialist with high-profile global bodies, including projects with the World Bank and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), he operated in environments that demanded high intellectual rigor, strategic diplomacy, and corporate finesse. Yet, the call of God was a burning fire that no career advancement could quench. Stepping away from the security and global prestige of world-class organizations, he made the ultimate pivot, trading corporate boardrooms for the place of prayer, corporate strategies for divine mandates, and professional accolades for the mandate to win souls. That decision marked the genesis of a spiritual awakening that now reverberates around the globe.

Mentored by the spiritual field marshal and legend of faith, Bishop David Oyedepo, Pastor Jerry is doubtless, one of a kind.

​What makes him such an exceptional minister of the Gospel is his rare blend of spiritual authority and deep Christlike humility. He is a paradox of holy intensity and gentle grace. On the altar, he manifests a lion-like spiritual prowess, a man of unyielding bold authority who confronts darkness, commands territorial shifts, and speaks into existence things that were not. His prayer style, widely recognized for its high-octane intensity, hits like a machine gun, releasing rapid, focused, and spirit-charged petitions that shatter strongholds. Yet, when the prayer climax subsides, that same spiritual lion transitions effortlessly into a shepherd of profound meekness and soft disposition. His gentle nature, accessible persona, and absolute truthfulness reflect a servant who has never allowed the weight of global recognition to inflate his spirit.

​This unique temperance is accompanied by an extraordinary prophetic gift characterized by surgical precision. Pastor Jerry does not trade in vague generalities or calculated guesses; his prophetic ministry cuts through spiritual cases with supernatural accuracy. He speaks into specific lives, situations, and medical diagnoses with details that leave audiences stunned and minds renewed. Yet, despite the staggering accuracy of his prophecies and the massive power evident in his ministrations, he guards his life with an uncompromising commitment to righteousness. In a generation where scandal often taints great gifts, Pastor Jerry stands as impeccable individual, a young, vibrant man of God without a trace of financial, moral, or doctrinal scandal, living openly as a husband, father, and minister whose integrity remains unblemished.

​At the core of this miraculous ministry is an unwavering passion for soul winning and a deep love for people.

He is a man with a larger – than-life vision, his heart softer than butter in compassion, always willing and ready to help the needy.

Each year, he provides succor to widows by building homes for them. He has also invested hundreds of millions of naira into empowering young entrepreneurs to launch their own businesses. Today, his ministry continues to receive widespread global recognition for its transformative impact.

​

In honor of his contributions to humanity during the Covid 19 crisis, the State of Dallas unanimously conferred state citizenship on Pastor Jerry

Whether ministering to thousands in packed arenas during global crusades or speaking through a screen to millions joining the early morning NSPPD, his heart beats distinctly for the lost and the hurting. He does not merely lead prayers; he carries the burdens of his global congregation on his heart, interceding daily for families, nations, and struggling believers. He harbors a zero-tolerance policy toward sin, repeatedly preaching that power without purity is a tragic deception. He refrains from playing with sin in any form, constantly reminding believers that the true measure of spiritual strength is not just the miracles one works, but the holy life one lives before an all-seeing God.

​

Perhaps the secret behind the explosive signs, instant healings, and groundbreaking financial breakthroughs recorded on his platform lies in his personal discipline. Pastor Jerry Eze leads a lifestyle anchored in deep sacrifice, relentless fasting, and rigorous personal holiness. He understands that spiritual authority is not gifted on the altar of compromise; it is forged in the secret place of consecration. His uprightness before God forms the bedrock upon which the supernatural rests. The abundant, undeniable testimonies that spill out of NSPPD daily – terminal diseases dissolved, hopeless medical cases reversed, are simply heaven’s response to a man who has refused to touch God’s glory or compromise His standards.

​As a young, vibrant leader, Pastor Jerry Eze represents a fresh wave of divine revival. He has mobilized millions of viewers every single morning into a disciplined army of intercessors, uniting believers across different time zones, languages, and denominations

Ultimately, Jerry Eze stands as a profound testament to the power of a life fully surrendered to God, proving that true spiritual dominion is born not of human strategy, but of relentless consecration and genuine love for humanity. As he continues to kindle the fires of revival across the globe through his ministrations and his expansive humanitarian works, he remains an enduring beacon of hope, a general of faith whose uncompromised devotion bridges the gap between heaven and men, leaving an indelible imprint on this generation.

Aibangbe is a Media & Public Relations Consultant

World.title: Akpabio Charges Door-to-Door Movement on National Renewal
World.content:
The President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, has charged the political support group, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, to carry the message of Renewed Hope to every nook and cranny of the country and build a consensus on nation building and national renewal.

Akpabio gave the charge at the formal inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement campaign headquarters in Abuja, yesterday.

He said the inauguration of the campaign headquarters should translate into affirming our faith in the Nigerian dream and a conviction that the greatness of Nigeria will not be determined by the difficulties the nation had endured but the courage of overcoming them.

Addressing members of the support group, Akpabio said, “You have recognised a fundamental truth of democracy: elections may be won at the ballot box, but enduring national progress is built in the hearts and homes of the people.

“That is the Nigeria we must build. That is the Nigeria President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has summoned us to believe in. His Renewed Hope Agenda is founded on the conviction that our present difficulties must not become the permanent destiny of our children.

“The road to national renewal may be demanding, but no nation rises to greatness by surrendering to its challenges. Great nations are built by people who refuse to surrender their future to their fears.

“And that is why this movement matters. When you go from door to door, do not merely seek political support. Carry a message of hope. Listen to the struggles of our people.

“Hear the concerns of the mother in the marketplace, the farmer in the field, the graduate seeking employment, and the young entrepreneur searching for opportunity.

“Let what you hear form the building blocks of tomorrow’s political architecture. Let every conversation remind us that leadership is not measured by the applause we receive, but by the lives we improve.

“Let this headquarters become more than a centre of political mobilisation. Let it become a centre of listening, engagement, national solidarity and service. Let its doors remain open to every Nigerian, regardless of ethnicity, religion, region or political persuasion.

“For the Nigeria we seek to build must be greater than the differences that sometimes divide us.”

According to Akpabio, the difficulties Nigerians are facing must never destroy their determination and politics must never become greater than patriotism.

Akpabio affirmed the commitment of the National Assembly to legislation that strengthens the economy of the nation and expands opportunity, protects democracy and advances the welfare of the people.

He charged the support group to build bridges across ethnic, religious and political lines. “Let us move from door to door, but above all, from heart to heart. Let us build bridges where others see barriers, inspire confidence where others spread despair, and plant the seeds of tomorrow’s prosperity in the soil of today’s sacrifice,” he said.

The campaign headquarters was inaugurated by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu and also attended by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, some state governors among others.

The PBAT Door-to-Door Movement is the brainchild of Government Ekpemupolo, also known as Tompolo.

World.title: Delta Approves N4bn Grant for 15,000 Indigent Deltans, Targets Small Businesses
World.content:
.Govt approves reconstruction of Illah-Ugbolu Road, others in Warri, Effurun, Emede

Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

The Delta State Government at its State Executive Council (EXCO) meeting yesterday approved the reconstruction of several major roads across the state, particularly in the state capital territory and environs, Warri-Uvwie and Isoko corridors.

The terrestrial communication arteries approved for reconstruction include Airport Road in Warri, Jakpa Road and Refinery Road in Effurun in Uvwie Local Government Area.

The council also approved the construction of Emede internal roads under Phases One and Two, as well as the reconstruction of Ugbolu–Illah Road.

Moreover, the state government approved a N4 billion empowerment programme targeting 15,000 indigent residents across the state’s 25 local government areas to support small businesses, promote entrepreneurship and cushion the effects of prevailing economic hardships across the state.

The initiative, approved by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, is expected to provide financial assistance to vulnerable residents, help existing small business owners overcome economic challenges and provide start-up capital for aspiring entrepreneurs.

The Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Charles Aniagwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by the governor at Government House, Asaba. He was accompanied by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Festus Ahon.

Aniagwu said the programme would be implemented through the Delta State Social Investment Programme in the coming weeks, adding that the governor had directed that beneficiaries be selected based on clearly defined eligibility criteria.

According to him, priority would be given to indigent residents who already operate small businesses, individuals seeking to establish micro-enterprises and vulnerable persons in need of financial support to improve their living conditions.

He explained that the intervention was designed to strengthen livelihoods, improve purchasing power and ensure that the benefits of ongoing economic reforms translate into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Deltans.

The State Executive Council approved compensation for land acquired in the central senatorial district for agricultural purposes.

According to Aniagwu, the decision was consequent upon discussions at the recent and previous economic summits in the state, where the need to make large plots of land available for large-scale farming as well as agricultural and agro-allied investment were highlighted.

The government was taking deliberate steps to attract commercial farmers from within and outside Nigeria while creating opportunities for local farmers to expand their operations.

The centre is projected to stimulate the local economy through the expansion of the state’s agricultural land bank in terms of increased accessibility to investors, which would positively affect agricultural output, generate employment and expand economic opportunities across the state.

Meanwhile, EXCO also approved the Economic and Fiscal Updates, Fiscal Strategy Paper and Budget Policy Paper to guide the preparation of Delta State’s 2027 appropriation estimates.

The fiscal documents are expected to provide the economic assumptions, revenue projections and policy framework needed to ensure realistic and effective budget planning.

World.title: Sunday tides: What beachgoers should know ahead of the full moon
World.content:
Sunday’s high and low tide times along South Africa’s coastline ahead of the approaching full moon. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Sunday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

Spring tide approaching along South Africa’s coast

Spring tides are approaching as the full moon draws closer on Monday, 26 October 2026.



According to the South African Weather Service, spring tides bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing along the coast. Higher tides may cover rocks and reefs, while lower tides expose more of the shoreline.

Beachgoers, anglers and other coastal visitors should check tide times and sea conditions before heading out.

Check the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Nahoon Beach closed after shark sighting
World.content:
Nahoon Beach in East London has been temporarily closed following a shark sighting on Saturday, just days after a 65-year-old swimmer died in a fatal shark attack at a nearby Eastern Cape beach. Image: Wikimedia Commons

Nahoon Beach in East London has been temporarily closed following a shark sighting on Saturday, just days after a 65-year-old swimmer died in a fatal shark attack at a nearby Eastern Cape beach.

The Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality (BCMM) confirmed the latest closure as a precautionary measure, warning bathers and beachgoers not to enter the water until further notice.

READ | After a fatal shark attack in KuGompo, do shark-repellent bracelets actually work?



The warning comes after Janine Lochrenberg was killed in a shark attack at Orient Beach in KuGompo City, formerly East London, on Tuesday, 20 October.

Lochrenberg was swimming with a group of open-water swimmers when the attack occurred. Fellow swimmers rushed to help and brought her towards shore, where attempts to save her life were unsuccessful. An inquest has been opened into her death.

Beachgoers warned to stay out of the water

In its notice, BCMM urged the public to respect the temporary closure of Nahoon Beach and follow all instructions issued by beach officials.

“As a precautionary measure, all bathers and beachgoers are strongly warned not to enter the water until further notice,” the municipality said.

The city added that it would provide further updates on the reopening of the beach once conditions were considered safe.

Fatal shark attack raises concern along the coast

Lochrenberg’s death has shocked the Eastern Cape’s open-water swimming community and renewed attention on beach safety following shark activity along the coastline.



Orient Beach and nearby Eastern Beach were closed after the fatal attack. The municipality subsequently reopened those beaches following safety considerations, while the latest shark sighting has prompted a separate temporary closure at Nahoon Beach.

Beachgoers are urged to take warnings seriously, avoid entering the water at Nahoon Beach while the closure remains in place and comply with any further safety instructions from municipal officials.

No reopening time has been announced as at the time of publishing.

World.title: World Rugby indecision over tackle height laws in elite rugby
World.content:
Following the trial of a lower legal tackle height at the 2026 U20 Junior World Championship, World Rugby’s executive board has concluded that more data is needed before a definitive conclusion can be reached on any roll out into the wider elite game.



The findings from the 2026 U20 World Championship trial will be discussed in detail at World Rugby’s Medical Commission Conference taking place on 27-28 October in Frankfurt, Germany.

Speaking following the meeting, World Rugby Chairman Brett Robinson said: “The trials from earlier this year were really interesting, but the reality is we’re not yet able to come to a definitive conclusion on such an important issue in our game. The data from 40 games at this year’s Junior World Championship just isn’t enough to say how such a change would impact the men’s and women’s elite game.

“This is an area that our unions want to see trialed, and World Rugby will continue the trial at our own under 20 competitions, but the only way we’re ever really going to get the level of data we need is for an elite domestic level competition to adopt the trial.



“Player welfare is at the heart of everything we do and that goes for unintended consequences just as much as it does for those changes to the game we consciously make.”

World Rugby take note of pros and cons

Interestingly, what World Rugby did note is that tackling lower has seen an increase in “knee drop” tackles where players drop to their knees in a dangerous manner.

The World Rugby executive board issued a law clarification, reenforcing existing law, from the beginning of October in order to address this welfare issue with officials acting in clear and obvious circumstances only.



Changes to be made

The “hip drop” tackle, where a tackler uses their bodyweight to pull a player to ground and drops onto the legs of a ball carrier from behind, will be explicitly added to foul play law and will be sanctioned with at least a penalty kick.

Meanwhile, the “knee drop” tackle, where a player drops to one or both knees before making a tackle, will be highlighted to players, coaches and match officials as an action already covered in law and can also be sanctioned with a penalty.

World.title: Two arrested for illegally feeding, exploiting Cape fur seals
World.content:
Two suspects are in custody after allegedly feeding and harassing Cape fur seals at Hout Bay Harbour. Image: Cape of Good Hope SPCA

Two suspects have been arrested for the alleged unlawful feeding and harassment of Cape fur seals in Hout Bay, Cape Town.

The arrests took place on Friday, 23 October 2026, at Hout Bay Harbour.

SPCA SWOOPS IN

According to the Cape of Good Hope SPCA, the arrests were precipitated by “ongoing complaints about activities that bring visitors, including children, into dangerously close contact with wild seals in exchange for paid photographs.”



Additionally, the suspects allegedly displayed “aggression or hostility” when visitors declined to pay a fee after the photographs were taken.

The SPCA worked alongside the City of Cape Town Law Enforcement Animal Control Unit and the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment to take the two suspects into custody.

SEALS: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

Cape fur seals reside on South Africa’s western coastline. They live in tight-knit colonies that span hundreds, and they tend to be calm and non-aggressive when encountering humans.



Nevertheless, members of the public are strongly discouraged from feeding or interacting with seals. This is especially if the seals feel threatened or are injured or infected by rabies.

Seals are also protected under the National Environmental Management: Biodiversity Act and the Threatened or Protected Marine Species Regulations. As such, you are prohibited from feeding, physically interacting with or harassing seals. Failure to adhere to these laws constitutes criminal offences.

“Visitors are urged to watch seals from a safe distance, give them space to move freely, and decline encounters that involve food, touching or close posing,” the SPCA says. “Please report concerns to the SPCA or Law Enforcement rather than confronting those involved.



“The SPCA and its enforcement partners will continue spot checks and undercover operations at the harbour to gather evidence and take action where offences are detected. Hout Bay’s seals deserve to remain wild, and everyone visiting the harbour deserves to be safe.”

SEAL FEEDERS CONVICTED

In related news, two men were convicted and sentenced back in May for the unlawful feeding and exploitation of Cape fur seals. They would do so also at Hout Bay Harbour.

They each received a sentence of an R80 000 fine or 24 months’ imprisonment, wholly suspended for five years, provided that they are not convicted of a similar offence during that period.



What are your thoughts about this latest arrest and the ongoing exploitation of Cape fur seals? Let us know in the comments below!

World.title: MK Party condemns IEC over rejection of candidate list corrections
World.content:
The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has condemned the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) for rejecting its request to correct and rectify its candidate lists.

The party said it had submitted a formal request seeking corrections to its candidate nominations, including the placement of ward candidates, omitted candidates and candidates who have since died.

The MK Party said on Tuesday, 20 October, the IEC rejected its requested amendments, maintaining that the ANC versus IEC court case did not reopen the nomination process beyond the limited restoration of nominations that had already been captured on the online system before nominations closed.



The party, led by former president Jacob Zuma, has since demanded that the IEC provide a substantive written report explaining why its requested corrections were rejected, with reasons for each rejection.

It has also called for a clear explanation of the distinction between the relief granted in the ANC proceedings and the corrections sought by the MK Party.

CONCERNS OVER IEC’S TRANSPARENCY

The party has also raised concerns about the IEC’s administration of electoral processes, including the dashboard interruption during the 2024 elections, according to Mahlangu.

“With regard to the party’s candidate list leak in 2024, the IEC confirmed the unauthorised disclosure of candidate lists belonging to the MK Party and ANC, raising serious concerns about the protection of sensitive electoral information,” Mahlangu said.

He also referred to allegations made by Congolese opposition figures against Janet Love, whom they accused of helping to legitimise an allegedly fabricated voter register in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Mahlangu further cited the charges of theft, fraud and money laundering involving R1.2 million faced by the IEC’s former deputy chairperson Nomsa Masuku, relating to her former employment at Standard Bank.



“The importance of transparency and accountability has not diminished. The current dispute over candidate lists reinforces our distrust in the Commission,” he said.
