World.title: Hopeful pensioner caught between joblessness and SASSA rejection
World.content:
A Western Cape woman says she is still trying to understand why SASSA turned down her application as she works through the process of applying for the Older Person’s Grant.

The woman is unemployed and looking for work. She rents privately and supports one to two people at home.

She told The South African that she regularly struggles to make ends meet. Unemployment is now her biggest financial worry.



Her comment to The South African summed up where she stands:

“I don’t have a SASSA grant now.”

The question SASSA has not answered for this applicant

Asked about her biggest challenge with SASSA, she pointed to one issue: understanding why her application was rejected.

Even so, she rates SASSA’s communication with recipients as very good. She has not qualified for any other form of government support. If she could change one thing about SASSA, she would increase the grant amount.

The Older Person’s Grant pays R2 400 a month from April 2026. To qualify, applicants must be South African citizens, permanent residents, or refugees living in South Africa, be aged 60 or older, and pass SASSA’s income and assets means test.

What rejected applicants can do

A declined application does not have to be the end of the road. SASSA must notify applicants in writing and explain the reasons for a refusal. Applicants who disagree can ask the agency to reconsider its decision or lodge an appeal with the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals, generally within 90 days of receiving the decision.



Applicants should keep their rejection letter and gather supporting documents, such as bank statements, before visiting their nearest office.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: The best beaches in Cape Town for a sunset swim
World.content:
Sunset swims are taking over this summer.

If you want to catch a wave, enjoy the warmer weather and watch a gorgeous Cape Town sunset, visit these beaches.

Six Beaches for a Relaxing Sunset Swim

If you want the sunset aesthetic without the crowds, and the option to launch your paddle board and relax in the water, these are your best options.



Atlantic Seaboard and Table Bay

If you’re willing to take a dunk along the Atlantic Seaboard, expect frigid temperatures.

This isn’t the kind of dunk you take to wind down. In summer, the water temperatures along the Atlantic Seaboard peak at 19°C.

But when Cape Town’s temperatures exceed 30°C, these dunks can be refreshing.

Three Anchor Bay Beach

The water in Three Anchor Bay is calm.

It’s easy to access with ample parking beside the beach or opposite Beach Road near Shell.

In the warmer months, the beach gets busy. But not as busy as Saunders Rock or other beaches in and around Sea Point.



From the beach, you can catch the last rays of the sunset, but you won’t get a clear view since the sun sets closer to Camps Bay in summer.

However, in the winter months like July, the sun sets opposite the bay.

Glen Beach

Glen Beach is next to Camps Bay. Yet it doesn’t get the crowds of Camps Bay or Clifton.

The water’s cool, but the crowds and sunset atmosphere are great.

From the water, you get spectacular sunset views in late spring and early summer.

Big Bay Beach

The sunset from Big Bay is magnificent. You can get the mountain and the warm hues from the beach.

There’s also ample parking and space.

But your swim will be impacted by the tides and wind. Check both before heading to Big Bay for a swim.

False Bay

Along False Bay, the water’s warmer, influenced by the Agulhas Current.

Since it’s on the eastern side of the city, the sunset view isn’t as vibrant and is essentially sunless.

But you do get diffuse, cascading colours.

Fish Hoek Beach

Fish Hoek isn’t as crowded as Muizenberg because it’s further down on False Bay.

But the beach can get busy.

Typically it quiets down in the evening, perfect for a sunset swim.

But be aware of your surroundings. Sharks swim closer to shore in spring and summer, and when the sun begins to set, they rely on their other senses to find prey.

If you see the Shark Spotters removing the shark exclusion net, consider getting out of the water.

Water’s Edge Beach

Water’s Edge Beach is between Seaforth and Boulders.

A sunset swim at Water’s Edge comes with calm waters, views, and the occasional penguin.

The nearest parking is the Seaforth parking. From the parking lot, walk toward Boulders Beach; there’s a tiny passage just after Water’s Edge Pre-Primary leading to the beach.

When Boulders is open, the Seaforth parking fills up. If you want a relaxing sunset swim at Water’s Edge, wait for closing.

In October and November, Boulders closes at 18:30; in December and January, it closes at 19:30.

Fisherman’s Beach

Fisherman’s Beach is the secret beach of secret beaches in Simon’s Town. It’s about a 3-minute drive from Seaforth.

But there’s no parking along the beach.

Instead, it’s either a 30-minute walk from Boulders Beach, or you can pay R50 for parking at Simon’s Town Country Club and walk down.

But because it’s secluded, expect to be sunset swimming without the masses.

Some honourable mentions include Llandudno and Bakoven Beach. But if you’re in Cape Town at sunset, you can turn any beach into a sunset swim beach.

World.title: Four arrested in suspect drug lab raid near Sun City
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police have bust another suspected drug lab, this time in Ramokokastad near Sun City in the the North West.

Police arrested four people after a raid on a property in Thabeng Section.

They seized 800 kilograms of drugs and chemicals and equipment used to make Mandrax and crystal meth.

A manhunt has been launched for a fifth suspect who escaped arrest.

The suspects are expected to appear in the Mogwase Magistrate's Court soon.

World.title: Mbalula tells voters what ANC plans to deliver
World.content:
MPOLWENI - ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula has been campaigning in Mpolweni, KZN.

It comes after he collapsed following a Constitutional Court ruling in the ANC's favour about disputed candidate lists.

Mbalula thanked the community for their continued support.

"Above all, the issues here are matters that relate to housing, which is being attended to. And then the school has been down. We're going to visit the school. And there's going to be mobile classes that are going to come next week to the school. We'll visit. We're going to talk to the community as well.

"The issues with regard to road situation on the ground, that too has been attended to. We are with the mayor here, who briefed us about some of the things that are outstanding. There are issues of the transformer in terms of Eskom. The other transformer has been brought in. And then we're going to be talking to Eskom to extend the transformer to the rest of the community so that they can all of them be covered. So these are things that are doable, that we can do. So we thank our people for keeping the faith and the belief in the people's movement."

World.title: Youth voter apathy under the spotlight
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - There’s a growing disconnect between South Africa’s youth and political parties.

That’s according to Rivonia Circle, a non-profit think tank focused on democratic reform, policy development and leadership.

With the 4 November municipal elections just days away, the concern is whether young people are losing faith in the ballot box or simply disengaging from the political process.

Rivonia Circle's Naledi Ngqambela said young people are disengaged.

"I think young people are aware of what’s happening in the country. I just think that they’re so disengaged because political leaders are not doing what they said they will do. So, that’s why young people are sort of seemingly looking like they’re not engaged on what’s going on around the country. But also, political parties or political leaders are not engaging young people the way that they want to be engaged.

"So, as you mentioned that young people are always online and I think that’s where also political leaders need to be. Be online. Go to schools and engage in the way they want to be engaged. So that it’s fun and it’s also fulfilling for them to be part of the electoral system. I’ve seen an advert by the IEC actually, where they’re working with one of social media influencers, Alfie, and I think that was such a great initiative to work with social media influencers so that young people are always engaged and that young people know what is happening in the country.

"Because it’s much easier as people they gravitate towards. So they always need to be online, need to do fun things. If young people are out at a party place, politicians have to be there and they need to engage and they should say ‘clock it’ they should, you know, engage them at a level that they want to be engaged. So, I like that initiative by the IEC and I think we need more of that.”

World.title: Brazil's Andrade returns to take vault gold at worlds
World.content:
ROTTERDAM - Brazilian gymnastics star Rebeca Andrade capped her return after a two-year break with gold in the women's vault at the world championships in Rotterdam on Saturday.

The 27-year-old, a two-time Olympic champion in the vault and floor exercise, finished ahead of Americans Claire Pease and Skye Blakely.

The victory unfolded in front of the greatest gymnast in history Simone Biles, who was in the stands at the Ahoy arena.

American Biles, who won three gold medals at the Paris Olympics two years ago, has not competed since. She has yet to decide whether she will make a comeback for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

As Brazil's most decorated Olympian, with six medals, two gold, three silver and one bronze, Andrade took a 22-month break following the 2024 Paris Games to focus on her physical and mental well-being.

She returned to official competition in June, winning gold on the vault at the Pan American Championships in Rio.

Andrade secured the victory with a score of 14.466 points, claiming her third world title on her signature apparatus.

Reigning European champion Angelina Melnikova of Russia did not compete after being denied a visa by Dutch authorities.

World.title: ATM ramps up campaign ahead of local polls
World.content:
SOWETO - With just over a week to go before the local government elections, political parties are intensifying their campaigns.

The African Transformation Movement held a rally at Orlando Community Hall in Soweto today.

The party is backing its parliamentary leader, Vuyo Zungula, as its mayoral candidate for Johannesburg.

Zungula has pledged to tackle lawlessness and inequality.

The party has also left the door open to coalition talks, saying community interests must come first.

Zungula faces a competitive mayoral race, with the DA’s Helen Zille, ActionSA's Herman Mashaba and the MK Party’s Bongani Bhaloyi among those also vying for the city of gold's top job.

World.title: 'Hotter than normal temperatures from October to December' - Weather Service
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Weather Service has warned that the El Niño weather pattern will bring less rainfall and hotter than normal temperatures from October to December.

South African Weather Service's Tokelo Chiloane said Gauteng is currently in the grip of a heatwave.

"Currently we are out of heatwave conditions however the heat is still going to be there, it's going to last long. We'll have days where we have cloud cover but most days we'll experience through the remaining months of spring into summer season will be warm to hot to very hot conditions," Chiloane said.

World.title: Cape Town Kite Festival tackles mental health
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Cape Town International Kite Festival has been bringing colour to the skies for 32 years.

But organisers said the event is about more than just kites.

Cape Mental Health CEO Ingrid Daniels said it's also an opportunity to start important conversations about mental health and the need for support.

" So the Cape Town International Kite Festival is an amazing event that we've been hosting for 32 years. There's such amazing symbolism with kites, and so it's synonymous with our work and what we do. When you look up into this beautiful sky that you see behind us, um, it reminds us that kites soar against adverse winds despite the fragility of the string.

"And for every kite up there, there's someone down here who's in need of mental health support. And the work that we've been doing for these 113 years, the Cape Town International Kite Festival, is an amazing platform for us to change the conversations around mental health. We don't only want to talk about mental health during the Cape Town International Kite Festival or Mental Health Awareness Month, which is in October, but we want people to talk about mental health every day, 'cause our mental health should be prioritized.

"We live in a country where we are exposed to so many high-risk mental health conditions such as poverty, gang violence, violence, gender-based violence, and just the difficulties that people face)

World.title: Thousands protest in Turkey over journalists' arrests, media shutdowns
World.content:
ISTANBUL - Thousands rallied in Istanbul and Ankara on Saturday against what they described as growing pressure on journalists in Turkey, including arrests, media shutdowns and the appointment of state administrators.

"Enough. We can no longer breathe," shouted marchers in the crowds, which were composed mainly of journalists, rights groups and opposition party representatives.

Press freedom has been increasingly constrained in Turkey since a failed coup attempt in 2016, with sweeping prosecutions and digital censorship.

But recent weeks have seen what rights advocates say is mounting pressure on independent journalism.

Eleven journalists have been jailed in the past two months and several media outlets shut down, according to the Turkish Journalists' Union.

At least 3,000 people gathered on the Asian side of Istanbul, according to police.

They held up photos of jailed journalists, chanting: "We will not be silenced. Enough is enough!" and "We will not bow to pressure".

Earlier this month, police raided Turkey's most-watched news channel, Halk TV, halting broadcasts and installing a government-appointed administrator.

The move was the latest against media outlets seen as critical of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his government.

It followed the closure of the website and social media accounts belonging to leading digital news outlet T24 over what authorities described as "LGBT propaganda".

"This gathering is not simply about standing up for journalists," veteran journalist Zafer Arapkirli told AFP after the Istanbul protest.

"It is also about defending respect for society's right to access information and news through journalists and independent media," said the columnist for the BirGun daily.

- Intimidation -

For Arapkirli, who himself faces lawsuits, the more intense the pressure becomes, the stronger the response and the determination to stand against it must be.

"What the regime wants is to intimidate, silence and frighten society through such pressure, by arresting individual journalists, seizing media outlets, banning news coverage and blocking access to social media," he said.

"We must show that we will not allow this to happen.

"We have done so up to now. I believe we are now moving towards demonstrating this determination on a much larger scale".

In Ankara, at least 3,000 protesters gathered, according to a police count.

They shouted: "No to censorship" and "Freedom for jailed journalists".

World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Washington Post journalist says attack by Israeli West Bank settlers has only ‘strengthened’ her resolve
World.content:
Heidi Levine, the Washington Post journalist brutally attacked by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank last week, said the terrifying ordeal has only strengthened her resolve to continue covering the plight of Palestinians.

“What hurts me the most is I can now really understand what others have gone through, what Palestinian women, children, men have gone through,” she told CNN’s Jake Tapper on Thursday from Israel, where she’s recovering after being released from hospital the day before.

“I’m an American, I work for the Washington Post, my story is getting a lot of attention around the world, everyone wants to talk to me – but I can’t imagine what it’s like for all the victims that have gone through the same ordeal and are living with the threat of this violence on a daily basis,” she added.

“It actually has strengthened my commitment to continue working to try to make a difference.”

Levine, a veteran photojournalist known for her work in the Middle East, was covering the annual olive harvest in the West Bank when she, a group of Palestinians, and other journalists came under attack. Violence in the West Bank has surged in recent years as settlements have expanded, often backed by Israeli forces; attacks on farmers and communities who rely on the olive harvest for their livelihoods now come on a daily basis.

Initially, Levine said, the harvest began as planned. But then, peering through her telephoto camera lens, she noticed people gathering at a nearby hilltop. They seemed young, some wearing black masks; she could see religious garments and headwear like kippah and tzitzit that she said clearly identified them as Israeli settlers.

Their numbers slowly grew to reach several dozen. They began lighting the olive trees on fire and moving closer. “Then all of a sudden, chaos broke out,” she said.

“There was tear gas, there was gunfire. From what I understand, a man was shot; a Palestinian man was shot in the leg, and the settlers charged forward,” she said.

“I was thrown to the ground … They just kept kicking me and hitting me with sticks, and it just kept going on and on. And then I actually thought, okay, maybe I’ll just play dead and pretend I’m dead, and they’ll stop and they’ll leave me alone.”

Instead, her attackers started ripping her gear off her body – her camera bag, her lenses, her pouch containing her American passport, credit cards, documents and other items.

Then they hauled her to her feet, in a moment that has sparked controversy and debate in the week since videos of her attack emerged. In a statement after the attack, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said footage “appears to show Levine knocked down and immediately helped to her feet by the same unidentified individual.”

This, Levine says, was false.

“No, they only stood me up because they couldn’t manage to get everything off my shoulders to rob me, including ripping off my gold necklace that my daughter gave me for my birthday,” she said.

The attack finally halted when journalist Jasper Nathaniel and several others came to Levine’s aid – but the danger wasn’t over. Video footage from that moment shows her rescuers holding her up and trying to escape from the attackers, who continue to throw rocks as they give chase.

“Run, run!” Levine’s rescuers can be heard shouting in a panic.

“I can’t,” she responds weakly. They urge her again: “You have to, come on!”

Speaking to Tapper on Thursday, she described it as “this biblical battle where the Palestinian men, a group of men went in front of me to protect us, me and my rescuers from being attacked again.” Without the Palestinians’ intervention, the whole group “would have been in the same situation as me.”

Even with a flak jacket and helmet on, Levine sustained serious injuries, with a broken rib, a broken vertebra, and a severe finger injury that required surgery, said Nathaniel last week after visiting her in the hospital. When she spoke to CNN, her hand was still heavily bandaged.

Her attack was widely condemned by foreign press, the White House, and some Israeli leaders including President Isaac Herzog. Netanyahu, however, tried to cast doubt on Levine’s attack and said that “serious questions remain.”

Just one day after Levine’s assault, settlers attacked a group of European diplomats visiting the Palestinian Christian town of Taybeh, prompting further outcry from the international community.

On Monday, Israeli police arrested at least 10 suspects for both attacks.

But many Palestinian victims of similar attacks never see justice. Since the olive harvest began on September 27, Israeli human rights group Yesh Din has documented more than 530 incidents of “settler and soldier violence” – which, beyond outright attacks, also includes the looting of crops and livestock, and destruction of olive trees.

More than a quarter of the violence “occurs in solders’ presence and under their protection,” said Yesh Din.

There has been a dramatic expansion of illegal settler outposts across the West Bank since Netanyahu’s government formed in December 2022 – with more than a third approved by the government. With that expansion, settler violence has also spread into parts of the West Bank that had previously seen little or none.

When asked if she blames Netanyahu and other far-right Israeli leaders like national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir for her attack, Levine laughed humorlessly.

“Well, you hear their rhetoric, right? You hear their speeches. I’ve documented their visits in the West Bank, so I think the answer is pretty obvious,” she said, warning that things will only worsen, and that authorities “don’t even know how to handle it.”

“This has been going on for over four decades that I have been covering this region, but I’ve never seen this situation in the West Bank or the situation in Israel at the level that it is today.”

World.title: At least 8 people killed in unprecedented shooting at church in Jordan
World.content:
At least eight people were killed and another 40 injured after gunmen opened fire on a church in Jordan’s southern Karak province, in an unprecedented attack that has left the nation stunned.

The “unidentified” gunmen have not yet been captured, the public security agency said in a news conference Friday afternoon, adding that the shooting was a terrorist attack against Christians attending a funeral in the town of Hmoud.

Jordan’s King Abdullah said Jordan will “harshly” respond against those responsible for the “terrorist act.”

“The blood of Jordanians is precious, and we will strike those who transgress against this country with an iron fist,” the king said on X.

The Prime Minister of Jordan Jafar Hassan said all state agencies are working to bring the perpetrators to justice, according to the kingdom’s official news agency Petra.

“What happened in Karak was the result of extremist terrorist ideology rooted in takfir (declaring others to be infidels), and we will not allow society to go down this path,” Petra quoted Hassan as saying.

Jordan’s King Abdullah arrives at Prince Ali Bin Al Hussein Hospital to visit the injured following a deadly attack at a church funeral in Hmoud, Jordan, on October 23. Salah Malkawi/Getty Images

The casualty toll was revised several times throughout the day as more information surfaced.

Jordan’s Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said two of those wounded are in critical condition.

A witness told state-run Al-Mamlaka television that one attacker was carrying an AK-47 assault rifle, and the shooting continued for several minutes.

Another witness speaking to CNN confirmed that the attack lasted a long time with gunmen shouting “Allahu Akbar” while targeting the courtyard of the church, where most people were standing.

“It was a massacre … I did not imagine I would get out alive,” she told CNN, saying she had to hide behind the altar, along with other mourners, to survive the attack.

“They struck people who were gathered to grieve and mourn,” she said. “I never ever imagined anything like this would ever happen anywhere in Jordan”

Security camera footage circulating on social media showed three gunmen opening fire on the street before heading toward the church.

The town has been home to a predominantly Christian community for centuries. On Friday, people had gathered at St. George’s Greek Orthodox Church to mourn the death of a community member.

“Some guys were standing outside the church before two people got out of a vehicle and started shooting,” Tamer Halasa, an eyewitness told Al-Mamlaka television.

Dozens were believed to be inside the church, witnesses told state media.

“We were more than 150 people inside and outside the church,” Halasa added.

People and security forces gather outside a Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hmoud in Jordan’s Karak governorate following a shooting on October 23. AFP/Getty Images

The region reacts

Jordanian government ministers and regional officials quickly condemned the shooting. Sectarian attacks in Jordan are rare, with the Christian community making up just 2% of the total population of the country.

Hassan declared three days of mourning, during which flags will be flown at half-staff over all government and public buildings

Condemnation from elsewhere in the region also came pouring in following the attack.

“On behalf of the American people, we offer our most heartfelt condolences to the victims and survivors of the terror attack today at a church in Karak, Jordan,” the US embassy in Jordan said, expressing its solidarity with the Jordanian king.

The embassy said US citizens should expect to see higher police presence in many parts of Jordan including malls and foreign embassies in Amman.

“We remind U.S. citizens of the continued need for caution and encourage them to monitor Jordanian authorities for breaking developments, such as Jordan’s Directorate of Public Security,” the embassy said in the travel advisory.

The Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem extended its condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims, Hammoud residents, all those affected by the shooting.

“The national cohesion of the Jordanian people serves as a vital safeguard against terrorism, extremism, and any attempts to sow division or discord,” said the patriarchate, which leads Catholics living in Israel, the Palestinian territories, Jordan and Cyprus.

Cairo’s Al-Azhar Institute, Sunni Islam top learning center, also condemned the attack.

“This crime contradicts the teachings of the Abrahamic religions and reveals that its perpetrators are devoid of all compassion, humanity and morality,” the institute’s Grand Imam Ahmed Al-Tayeb said in a post on social media.

The Iraqi government said the attack “demonstrates that terrorism is a root of evil that the Iraqi people have previously suffered from and confronted with determination and strength.”

“It calls on us to stand united against all voices that threaten the security of our societies and undermine civil peace,” the Iraqi statement added.

This story is breaking and will be updated.

World.title: Why Zelensky insists it’s not personal with Trump — even though it is
World.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky told CNN on Thursday that there’s “not something personal” driving his latest estrangement from President Donald Trump.

Unfortunately for Ukraine’s wartime president, nothing could be further from the truth.

Everything about Trump’s presidency is personal.

Trump has substituted his own values — the flexing of dominance, the courting of strongmen and the pursuit of cash-spinning deals — for those that guided previous modern presidents as they secured democracy and faced down tyrants.

The result is that Zelensky now confronts one of the most critical — and hard to believe — questions about the war: Does Ukraine’s fate now depend not only on its capacity to fend off Russian aggression but also on the possibility that the US has joined Moscow’s camp?

Trump makes no secret of his personal distaste for Zelensky, who blamelessly helped precipitate his first impeachment. So it is no surprise that he’s adopted Russia’s demand for Ukraine to get a new president.

Trump’s personal political interests also shape US foreign policy: His diesel deal that could send billions of dollars to Russian President Vladimir Putin’s war machine came as he faced pressure to show midterm voters he can ease high fuel prices. So did his demand that Ukraine sheath one of its most effective tactics: attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky attends a lunch meeting with US President Donald Trump at the White House on October 17, 2025. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images/File

And Trump’s idiosyncratic political personality has long undermined peace efforts. His undimmed desire to please Putin has seen the US pressure Ukraine for concessions rather than Russia. Far from from favoring the invaded party, he’s rewarded the invader.

This pattern has become more concrete in recent weeks.

After rhetorically favoring Russia’s position for nearly two years, Trump has begun taking active steps to reinforce it. He invited Putin to the G20 summit; is considering a great powers meeting with the Russian leader and China’s Xi Jinping to try to end the war in Ukraine’s absence; and declines to send Patriot missiles to repel Russia’s aerial onslaught.

Ukraine says its access to a military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink network is still disrupted — meaning its drones are limited to lower speeds and thus less effective. It’s unclear who in the administration is to blame, though Trump insists it wasn’t him.

The spectacle of Trump envoy Steve Witkoff praising Putin — an accused war criminal — as a “humanitarian” to his face in St. Petersburg this week epitomized the White House’s moral expediency. Trump justified the praise as necessary to extract a US prisoner, Stephen Hubbard, from Russia.

But this accelerating strategy of offering carrot after carrot to the Russian leader has already demonstrably failed to end the war. Putin keeps contradicting Trump’s assurances that he wants peace with murderous missile and drone strikes on Ukraine that recently hit civilian buses and killed a 1-year-old in her stroller. Trump did not condemn such attacks.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky during a meeting on October 14 in London, England. Henry Nicholls/WPA/Pool/Getty Images

‘We will survive’

His nation’s relentless pain was etched on Zelensky’s face during his interview with CNN’s Christiane Amanpour. While he went out of his way to avoid a new clash with Trump, he vowed never to compromise his principles or squander Ukraine’s sacrifice. Projecting dignity and resolve, he at times implicitly pleaded for a return to an American foreign policy built on traditional American values.

“We will survive and we will stay strong,” Zelensky said. “We will do everything to bring peace closer. But we will not give (a) chance (to) Putin to win this war.”

Zelensky told Amanpour he had no desire for personal rifts with Trump.

“It’s not about personalities,” he said. “It’s not something personal between me and President Trump.”

The Ukrainian leader has no option but to try to repair relations with the US president, since he’s the only world leader who could, if he wished, create pressure for a genuine peace process.

But he made clear his dismay at some of Trump’s recent moves, including the diesel deal and waiving of a new US sanctions law targeting Russia. “It will only give much more money for Putin for this war. And that’s why I’m against it,” Zelensky said. He signaled that even if he is rebuked for his rhetoric, with Ukraine’s freedom at stake, “I have to speak about it.”

A rescue worker puts out a fire of a building destroyed after a Russian missile attack in Kyiv, Ukraine, on September 8. Alex Babenko/AP

‘Break us, destroy us, kill us’

The deepening quagmire poses two grave questions.

How will this war — which is only becoming more savage — ever end?

And what happens if it doesn’t? The conflict is growing even more dangerous as the Kremlin opens a new front of hybrid warfare against Ukraine’s European allies.

The dire possibilities leave no option but for Ukraine and its European allies to stay engaged, even if they mistrust Trump’s lopsided peace efforts.

Two minor developments this week that offered a scintilla of hope.

Russia agreed after Witkoff’s visit that Russia will join trilateral peace talks with Washington and Kyiv. And Zelensky reiterated a proposal to freeze current frontlines in a bid to spur a ceasefire and diplomacy.

These are hardly breakthroughs. The technical talks Russia has agreed to attend won’t take place until mid-November — so weeks of killing lie ahead. At best they will lead to an extended diplomatic process: Russia traditionally fights while it talks.

And Zelensky has in the past offered multiple formulations for ceasefires and diplomatic openings and initiatives to end the war, all of which Putin has ignored. There is no indication that Ukraine’s latest inducements will tempt him.

Still, hopes that current tensions between Ukraine and the US will not thwart some diplomacy are bolstered by the way previous blowups between Zelensky and Trump have ebbed over time, amid feverish European diplomacy to close the gaps. And US officials said talks in Norway with Zelensky and European partners this week had made progress and created momentum for the trilateral talks.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finland’s President Alexander Stubb deliver a joint news conference on October 20, in Oslo, Norway. Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP/Getty Images

The general formula for any peace deal has been clear for years. It would entail a truce that would likely see Russia keep the spoils of its land grabs; US and/or European security guarantees for Kyiv; plans for a vast post-war reconstruction program for Ukraine; and a framework regarding NATO-Russian relations in Europe.

But Putin has shown no sign he’ll accept anything less than his maximal demands. And why would he, when Trump keeps offering him concessions?

Russia is seeking to negotiate the ceding of strategic territory in Ukraine’s eastern Donbas region that its troops failed to claim on the battlefield, despite horrendous casualties. Zelensky told CNN he could never accept such terms because “a lot of people died defending this land, defending our independence, our country.”

While Trump keeps insisting Putin wants a deal, Zelensky arguably has a more realistic view of his adversary’s aspirations. “Putin is playing, you know, he’s a player,” he said. “It’s a pity because he plays with the lives of other people.” He said Putin’s goal is to “break us, destroy us, kill us.”

But Ukraine’s living hell, and the growing possibility that the war could burst its borders mean there’s no option but to once again test Putin’s intent.

That means dealing with Trump’s temperament, grievances and personal goals.

Zelensky cannot let personalities get in the way.

World.title: The biggest-ever internet security threat has been known for 22 years. AI made it a crisis in 2 days
World.content:
In July 2004, security researcher Stefan Esser sent a warning.

A critical flaw in PHP, the programming language that powers 70% of the world’s websites, could allow an attacker to do some seriously nefarious stuff: read passwords, steal databases or even take over entire websites.

But Esser’s warning went mostly ignored for decades. In 2020, another researcher discovered a related problem, and the PHP overseers issued a partial fix. A similar PHP vulnerability was uncovered in 2024 – but was left unfixed.

Why was one of the most severe threats to the foundation of the internet left unresolved for 22 years?

Because it would have taken mind-numbing work for a human to figure out how to take advantage of it: tedious, time-consuming, monotonous coding. That rendered the PHP vulnerability impractical to exploit.

AI just figured out how to do it in two days.

On Wednesday, OpenAI’s public revelation of the exploit was announced in conjunction with a security update to fix the problem.

Phew, you might think. The good guys got to it first. But the AI-assisted discovery deeply concerned cybersecurity researchers, because the next one might come from someone who wants to weaponize it.

And AI doesn’t care who’s pulling the trigger.

Security by exhaustion

The internet is held together with shoestring and bubblegum.

An apt xkcd cartoon visualizes “all modern digital infrastructure” as a giant Jenga tower supported by one, thin, vertical block with the label: “a project some random person in Nebraska has been thanklessly maintaining since 2003.”

On July 30, researchers at AI security company Calif, in conjunction with OpenAI’s new Patch the Planet security initiative, decided to point a large-language AI model at one of those Jenga blocks – PHP – and see what came of it. It didn’t expect to find anything critical.

On August 1, it found a method to attack PHP’s vulnerabilities. Days later, it found another. Then another. Later that month, Google-backed security company Wiz – another Patch the Planet participant – discovered new exploits for PHP vulnerabilities, too.

The patch went out Wednesday, and the companies publicly disclosed their findings. Wiz called it one of the most severe vulnerabilities in software history.

The security community lit up social media with I-told-you-sos.

“The security industry has long been warning about the coming security apocalypse, because AI can do these things very, very quickly – better than humans,” said Vyas Sekar, professor of computer engineering at Carnegie Mellon University. “This may be the first of many. This is a wakeup call.”

Sekar says there are more PHP-like vulnerabilities out there to discover and exploit. A lot more. Some are known, and many are unknown.

Master/Moment RF/Getty Images

The wide availability of AI tools has significantly lowered the barrier to entry for hackers to take advantage of potential security vulnerabilities. That fact freaked out Anthropic enough that the AI company paused deployment of its Mythos model in June, as it was so good at exposing security vulnerabilities and finding vectors for attack that the US government labeled it a national security threat.

But Calif researcher Ryan Austin noted in a blog post that the company didn’t use any special AI models that weren’t generally available to the public.

That democratization of AI tools made clear that “security by exhaustion” is no longer a viable safeguard against bad guys, said Nick Rogers, CEO of Fieldwork AI.

For 22 years, PHP was like a bank with no security guards. Anyone could walk down to the vault and make off with the cash – if they had the time to try every code. It was such arduous work, it wasn’t worth anyone’s time.

But AI doesn’t get tired. And it can crack safes way faster than humans.

“Taking a theoretical (vulnerability) and proving you can exploit it is quite tedious and mechanical work,” said Rogers. “AI can keep churning until it figures it out. You don’t even need to try. You can drink coffee while it does it.”

The vulnerability

Effectively, PHP is an engine that powers most of the internet. Until it was patched Wednesday, it had a fatal flaw.

A vulnerability left open a patch for an attacker to mess around with the way PHP processes requests to run websites. If a server crashed because it ran out of memory, it would leave stale data behind that could be exploited to leak the data or execute bad code.

Think of the exploit like taking advantage of a busy restaurant kitchen. Customers could overwhelm the chef with too many complex orders – so much that she quits midway through dinner, leaving dirty pans, raw ingredients and recipes strewn about the counter. Then, when a new chef is hired, he serves the contaminated food on filthy dishes – and even sends some recipes to customers along with their dinner orders.

Although the vulnerability was long known to be theoretically exploitable, figuring out how to do it proved exceedingly difficult. Hackers had to force the server into an out-of-memory crash at a specific instant to bypass PHP’s safety limits.

When researchers pointed AI at the problem, it quickly found a couple ways around that. One solution exploits a mismatch between the way PHP measures compressed files and decoded files. Effectively, it allowed compressed files through its gates, letting the file unpack itself and take over from the inside.

Another attacks PHP with deeply nested file structures that overwhelmed PHP’s directory structure, triggering the memory failure.

The vulnerability was patched, but the threat may not be over, noted Adam Meyers, vice president of counter adversary at security company CrowdStrike. Many outdated versions of PHP are still in use, and the patch almost certainly didn’t fix all of PHP’s problems.

Also, an apparent leak about the vulnerability before the patch was released resulted in thousands of exploits in the hours ahead of the announcement, according to security company Cloudflare.

“Bad guys don’t need to find the vulnerability first – they can weaponize it after the fact,” Meyers said. “We are still waiting to see how much of this shows up in the wild.”

What’s next?

OpenAI offered several suggestions in its disclosure about the PHP patch, all of which basically boil down to: Write better, more secure code from the start.

That’s not super helpful if your web application has been written using PHP.

“Migrating away from PHP is a pretty expensive process,” noted Meyers. “It’s not like switching from Microsoft mail to Google mail; you need to rebuild the whole application.”

If the solution isn’t to migrate 70% of the web to a new programming language, then fixing its underlying problems – and all the other software problems in the world – would hardly be an easy fix, either.

What’s needed, then, may be a paradigm shift in the way the security community operates. Effectively, assume everything poses a security risk.

Companies need to treat every single business operation like air traffic controllers treat their surroundings, said Madhu Shashanka, cofounder of security company Concentric AI.

“Everything is a potential vulnerability,” Shashanka said. “Every business operation is a high-stakes operation.”

For example, companies that leave certain software unpatched – even for a few days – are exposing themselves to vulnerabilities that are no longer too difficult or expensive for bad actors to exploit.

“Lots of vulnerabilities are out there that are never exploited because it takes effort,” said Shashanka. “AI has rendered that effort meaningless.”

World.title: Border demarcation between Egypt-Turkey requires consultation: Foreign Ministry
World.content:
The Egyptian Foreign Ministry said that the topic of border demarcation between Egypt and Turkey requires consultation.

This comes amid a series of diplomatic activities in Istanbul, including regional and international meetings focused on addressing regional issues and strengthening efforts toward peace and stability.

A spokesperson for the Foreign Ministry emphasized that the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait are vital to Egypt’s national security, and that the unity and independence of Sudan constitute a “red line” for Egypt.

The spokesperson also highlighted the significance of the meetings held in Istanbul, describing them as highly important.

Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty reiterated, during a meeting with his Turkish counterpart, Hakan Fidan, in Istanbul on Friday, Egypt’s categorical rejection of the Libyan parliament’s ratification of the 2019 memorandum of understanding between Libya and Turkey concerning the delimitation of maritime jurisdictions.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Quadripartite Group—comprising the foreign ministers of Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey—as well as a joint ministerial meeting that included the foreign ministers of Italy, France, Germany, and the United Kingdom.

The discussion addressed developments in Libya, with Abdelatty reaffirming Egypt’s support for Libya’s unity, sovereignty, territorial integrity, and stability.

FM stresses adhering to international maritime law

He underscored Egypt’s commitment to bolstering Libyan state institutions in a manner that safeguards the interests of the Libyan people.

The minister further emphasized the importance of upholding the principles of international maritime law and the provisions of the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea regarding the delimitation of the Exclusive Economic Zone and the continental shelf, in accordance with the principles of justice and equity among states.

Fidan on his end affirmed his understanding of Egypt’s concerns regarding developments in Libya, stressing the importance of continued consultation, coordination, and joint action to address them, as well as supporting efforts aimed at achieving security and stability in the country.

Egypt rejects memorandum between Libya/Turkey

During an interview with the Turkish channel TRT on the sidelines of his visit to Istanbul, Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s rejection of the maritime memorandum of understanding signed between Libya and Turkey, emphasizing the necessity of adhering to international maritime law and the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.

Egypt on Wednesday announced its rejection of the Libyan House of Representatives’ ratification of the memorandum, asserting that this step carries no legal implications for Egypt.

The Libyan House of Representatives earlier on Tuesday voted unanimously to approve the memorandum of understanding regarding the delimitation of maritime jurisdiction zones in the Mediterranean Sea, thereby ending a parliamentary stance—held since 2020—that had rejected the agreement.

The House spokesperson, Abdullah Bleihaq, announced on the X platform that the assembly had rescinded Resolution #1 of 2020, which had rejected the ratification of the two memoranda of understanding concluded between the Government of National Accord and Turkey.

Furthermore, the House repealed Resolution #6 of 2020, which had called for the severance of political relations with Ankara.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Industry Minister: Egypt Forum 2026 to address manufacturing challenges, boost investment
World.content:
Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said Egypt Forum 2026 would help strengthen the industrial sector by addressing challenges facing manufacturers and fostering dialogue between the government and industry stakeholders to promote growth, attract investment and support domestic production.

In an interview with Extra News on Friday, October 23, 2026, Hashem said holding the forum at this time reflects the government’s commitment to listening to manufacturers, removing obstacles to their operations and developing practical solutions to the challenges they face.

These efforts, he added, would help create more opportunities for young people and support Egypt’s broader economic development.

The minister noted that the government is working to simplify industrial licensing procedures and accelerate the approval process through clear, streamlined mechanisms.

He also highlighted the role of universities in contributing ideas and proposals at the forum, saying their participation could help address challenges facing the industrial sector in the coming period.

Hashem further announced the implementation of new measures to simplify the procedures factories must follow to obtain insurance documents through the Ten-Year Insurance Pool (Al-Mogamaa Al-Ashariya).

The measures are intended to reduce the financial and administrative burdens on industrial investors, speed up project implementation and facilitate the start of production.

He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to reviewing and streamlining administrative procedures and expanding their digitization to improve the business environment and encourage industrial investment.

World.title: PM’s remarks on electricity load shedding taken out of context
World.content:
The Cabinet’s Media Center denied reports attributed to Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly suggesting that electricity load-shedding cuts could last between six and eight hours daily.

In a statement issued Thursday, October 22, 2026, the Media Center said the remarks were taken out of context and did not reflect any actual decision to implement load shedding.

Madbouly made the comments during a session titled “Egypt’s Energy Journey: National Achievements and Future Prospects,” while discussing possible scenarios for addressing rising energy prices.

The Prime Minister outlined three options: passing the full increase in energy costs on to citizens, having the state absorb the entire increase, or keeping the budget allocations and purchasing petroleum products at the new prices within available resources.

He explained that the third option could cover only 50–60% of citizens’ needs, potentially forcing the government to consider more difficult measures, including electricity load-shedding cuts for six to eight hours a day.

World.title: Liberia: Judge Cites Evidence in Finding NSA Staff Peter Bon Jallah Guilty of Statutory Rape, Kidnapping
World.content:
Criminal Court E Acquits Him of Gang Rape; Orders Pre-Sentence Report Before Sentencing

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

Monrovia — Assigned Circuit Judge Wesseh Alphonsus Wesseh Sr. has found 63-year-old Peter Bon Jallah, a staff member of the National Security Agency (NSA), guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping, but not guilty of gang rape in a case involving a 16-year-old boy.



In a verdict delivered Friday, October 23, Judge Wesseh said he had reviewed the evidence presented by both parties and considered the arguments advanced during the trial before determining that the prosecution had established sufficient grounds to convict Jallah on two of the three charges.

The judge framed his decision around three central questions: whether the prosecution’s evidence justified a conviction for gang rape, statutory rape and kidnapping.

He answered the first question in the negative, acquitting Jallah of gang rape, but answered the other two in the affirmative, finding him guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping.

Following the verdict, Judge Wesseh ordered Jallah remanded at Monrovia Central Prison pending the submission of a pre-sentence and behavioral report by the Bureau of Probation Services at the Ministry of Justice.

The judge directed the clerk of court to communicate with the probation authorities to ensure that the report is made available as soon as possible to assist the court in determining the appropriate sentence.

Judge Identifies Three Decisive Questions

In his ruling, Judge Wesseh said the court had examined the facts and circumstances contained in the evidence presented at trial before identifying three issues that were decisive to the case.

On the gang rape charge, the judge concluded that the prosecution’s evidence did not provide sufficient and reasonable grounds to convict Jallah. He consequently declared the defendant not guilty and acquitted him of that charge.

However, on statutory rape, the judge found that the evidence presented by the prosecution provided sufficient grounds for conviction.

He reached a similar conclusion on the kidnapping charge, finding Jallah guilty on that count as well.

The ruling represents a split decision in a case that involved allegations of repeated sexual abuse of a minor and the alleged confinement of the complainant for several days.

Indictment Details Alleged Repeated Abuse

According to the indictment summarized in the court’s verdict, Jallah and two unidentified men were indicted by the Montserrado County Grand Jury during the February 2026 Term of Court for gang rape, statutory rape and kidnapping.

The indictment alleged that Jallah and the two other men acted individually and jointly in sexually abusing the complainant on multiple occasions.

It further stated that the complainant, who was 16 at the time of the alleged incidents, lived in the Airfield Shark Community in Monrovia and regularly visited Jallah’s residence to perform domestic work for which he received compensation.

The indictment alleged that on November 29 and December 24, 2025, Jallah lured the boy to his residence in the Sharks Community of Airfield Sinkor, where he allegedly sexually assaulted him.

The most serious allegations concerned an incident said to have occurred on January 1, 2026, after the boy participated in a community football league at the Kpelle Town football field.

According to the indictment, the boy encountered Jallah near his residence after the game. Jallah allegedly offered to purchase football boots for him and instructed him to return home to bathe before accompanying him.

The indictment alleged that the two subsequently travelled by car to a building in the Camp Johnson Road area of downtown Monrovia, where the boy was allegedly held for three days and sexually abused by Jallah and the two unidentified men.

It further alleged that on January 3, 2026, at about 10 p.m., the boy was concealed at the back of Jallah’s vehicle and abandoned along 15th Street in Sinkor.

The complainant was reportedly rescued by private security guards, who alerted his parents. His mother and other relatives subsequently took him to the John F. Kennedy Medical Center for medical examinations.

These details formed part of the allegations contained in the indictment and should not be interpreted as separate findings by the court unless expressly established in the judge’s ruling.

Case Faced Procedural Delays

The court’s verdict also outlined the procedural history of the case, which experienced several delays before proceeding to a full trial.

The case was initially before Criminal Assizes Court “A” for Montserrado County before being transferred to Criminal Court “E” for evidentiary proceedings and a full trial.

Jallah was arraigned on June 18, 2026, and pleaded not guilty to the indictment. He subsequently elected to be tried by a judge without a jury.

The trial was delayed after the prosecution filed a motion seeking a change of venue. Following the denial of that motion, the prosecution petitioned the Chamber Justice for a writ of certiorari, but the petition was denied and the case was ordered to proceed.

The proceedings encountered another setback when the judge previously presiding over the matter could not continue taking evidence after the regular sitting of the court expired.

On August 5, 2026, the case was reassigned for trial.

According to the written verdict, the prosecution presented 13 regular witnesses and six rebuttal witnesses, while the defense called eight regular witnesses and three subpoenaed witnesses from the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, Orange GSM and the John F. Kennedy Medical Center.

The prosecution’s witnesses included the complainant, police investigators, medical personnel and Rwandan forensic examiner Pascal Bavugirije.

The defense witnesses included Jallah himself and several other individuals who testified on his behalf.

The number of witnesses listed in the written verdict differs from earlier accounts that referred to 12 prosecution witnesses, making the court’s official record the appropriate reference for the final tally.

DNA and Medical Evidence Featured at Trial

The prosecution relied in part on forensic findings linking Jallah’s DNA profile to biological material recovered from four clothing exhibits.

However, testimony attributed to the forensic examiner indicated that the findings could not establish precisely when or how the biological material was deposited.

The defense challenged the prosecution’s interpretation of the evidence, pointing to alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

Medical evidence also featured prominently in the proceedings. Earlier accounts of the trial referenced a John F. Kennedy Medical Center report that reportedly found no visible signs of anal trauma, while the parties disputed the significance of the medical and forensic findings.

The precise weight the court assigned to each item of evidence should be established from the complete written ruling and trial record. The verdict provided identifies the court’s conclusions on the three charges but does not detail its assessment of every witness or exhibit.

Prosecution and Defense Clash in Final Arguments

During final arguments on Thursday, October 22, prosecution lawyer Cllr. Calvin H. Momolu urged Judge Wesseh to convict Jallah, maintaining that the evidence presented during the trial supported the charges.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Wilfred Sayeh argued that the prosecution had failed to prove its case to the required legal standard. The defense questioned the police investigation and challenged the interpretation of the medical, forensic and testimonial evidence.

The judge adjourned the proceedings until Friday morning to review the evidence and arguments before delivering the verdict.

In reaching his decision, Judge Wesseh found the prosecution’s evidence sufficient to convict Jallah of statutory rape and kidnapping, while concluding that it did not warrant a conviction for gang rape.

The two other men named in the indictment were not brought under the court’s jurisdiction and were not tried alongside Jallah in these proceedings.

Defense Plans Appeal

Following the verdict, defense lawyer Cllr. Sayeh announced plans to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court of Liberia.

The planned appeal would give the defense an opportunity to challenge the lower court’s decision before the country’s highest court.

In the meantime, Jallah remains ordered remanded at Monrovia Central Prison while the Bureau of Probation Services prepares the report requested by Judge Wesseh.

The report is intended to assist the court in determining the sentence to be imposed following the guilty verdicts.

The case now enters the sentencing stage before the anticipated appeal, with the court having found Jallah guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping but acquitted him of gang rape.
