World.content:
BRAZIL · SPORT

Key Facts — What is happening Brazil’s Rebeca Andrade won the women’s vault final at the world championships in Rotterdam on Saturday, 24 October, her third world vault title.

— Why it matters Americans Claire Pease and Skye Blakely took silver and bronze, so US gymnasts made the podium behind an Olympic champion.

— The numbers Andrade scored 14.466, Pease 14.233 and Blakely 14.166 in the vault final, a margin of 0.233 points over silver.

— Who is who Andrade is a Brazilian Olympic medallist; Pease and Blakely are US gymnasts, and Blakely won the all-around gold on Friday, 23 October.

— What to watch Apparatus finals continue on Sunday, 25 October in Rotterdam, with US highlights on NBC at noon ET.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US fans saw two Americans on the vault podium, and the United States has six medals at these championships, two of them gold.

Brazil’s Rebeca Andrade won her third world vault title in Rotterdam. Two Americans stood on the podium behind her.

Brazilian gymnast Rebeca Andrade won the women’s vault final at the world championships in Rotterdam on Saturday, 24 October. It is her third world vault title, USA Gymnastics said, and the Rebeca Andrade vault result puts two Americans behind her.

Claire Pease took silver and Skye Blakely bronze, both for the United States, according to USA Gymnastics. Andrade’s win comes as Brazil prepares for a national vote on Sunday, 25 October, yet it is a sporting story first.

How the Vault Final Played Out

The final was held at Rotterdam Ahoy on Saturday, 24 October, the second-to-last day of the championships. USA Gymnastics lists Andrade first with 14.466, Pease second with 14.233 and Blakely third with 14.166.

Andrade’s title follows her world vault wins in Kitakyushu in 2021 and Antwerp in 2023, CNN Brasil reported. That outlet counts it as her tenth world championships medal.

She also led qualifying on vault with 14.533, the outlet said, ahead of South Korea’s Yeo Seojeong on 14.483. Andrade returned to competition after a break in 2025 that she spent on mental health and family, the outlet added.

Two Americans on the Podium

Pease, a US gymnast, won her first individual world medal with the vault silver, USA Gymnastics said. Blakely, who also competes for the University of Florida, added vault bronze to a busy week.

Blakely won the women’s all-around gold on Friday, 23 October, with 55.733 points. Liudmila Roschina took silver with 55.199 and Qinqin Ke of China bronze with 55.032.

Pease finished seventh in that all-around with 54.232 points. The result extends a 23-year run of US women medalling in the world all-around, dating to Anaheim in 2003.

On Saturday Blakely also took bronze on uneven bars with 14.600. Kaylia Nemour of Algeria won gold with 15.333, and Frederick Richard won men’s floor gold with 14.633, giving the Americans four medals.

How Brazil Fared in Rotterdam

Brazil finished fifth in the women’s team final on Wednesday, 21 October, with 159.730 points, Agência Brasil reported. China won with 165.764, the United States took silver with 165.531 and Japan bronze with 164.063.

Brazil had qualified eighth with 159.131 points and improved its total in the final. Andrade scored 14.400 on vault in the team final, the highest individual vault mark in the report.

The Brazilian team was led by Olympic medallists Andrade and Flávia Saraiva, the agency said. Earlier coverage of Andrade’s career is in a Rio Times report on her Paris Olympic victory.

What It Means for US Readers

For US fans, the result shows how close the vault field is, with two Americans within about 0.3 points of Andrade. USA Gymnastics counts six US medals so far at these championships, two of them gold.

NBC Sports lists the apparatus finals on Peacock and NBCSN, with highlights on NBC at noon ET on Sunday, 25 October. Brazil’s wider Olympic record is covered in a Rio Times review of Paris 2024 and a guide to key Brazilian figures.

What Is Not Known

The world federation’s official results sheet and Olympics.com could not be opened, so scores rest on USA Gymnastics and CNN Brasil. The two outlets give the same final totals.

The published vault scores for each jump do not average to the final totals, so only the totals are used here. Whether Andrade competes in a further final on Sunday, 25 October is not confirmed in the sources reviewed.

The Brazilian outlet said Simone Biles attended the final as a guest of honour and not as a competitor. No second source confirmed that detail.

What Comes Next

The championships end on Sunday, 25 October with more apparatus finals in Rotterdam. The sources reviewed do not say how these results count towards Olympic qualification.

The next Olympics are in Los Angeles in 2028. Neither the Brazilian nor the US federation has announced selection plans in the reports reviewed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who won the women’s vault final at the 2026 world championships?

Brazil’s Rebeca Andrade won with 14.466 points on Saturday, 24 October in Rotterdam. Americans Claire Pease and Skye Blakely took silver and bronze.

How many world vault titles does Rebeca Andrade have?

Andrade now has three, USA Gymnastics says. Brazilian reports date the wins to 2021 and 2023 and count ten world medals in all.

Did Americans win medals on the same day?

Yes, the United States won four medals in Saturday’s apparatus finals. They were vault silver and bronze, uneven bars bronze and men’s floor gold.

Who won the women’s all-around in Rotterdam?

American Skye Blakely won the all-around on Friday, 23 October, with 55.733 points. Liudmila Roschina took silver and China’s Qinqin Ke bronze.

Where was the competition held?

The 2026 Artistic Gymnastics World Championships run at Rotterdam Ahoy in the Netherlands from 17 to 25 October. The vault final was on Saturday, 24 October.

World.title: Guatemalan Gets Life for UNC Murder, 23 Oct
World.content:
GUATEMALA · US JUSTICE

Key Facts — What is happening A North Carolina jury convicted Guatemalan-born Miguel Salguero Olivares on Friday, 23 October, of the 2012 murder of student Faith Hedgepeth, and the judge sentenced him to life without parole.

— Why it matters The case went cold for more than nine years and was solved with DNA, including a sample from a 2021 drunk driving stop.

— The numbers Hedgepeth was 19 when she was found dead on 7 September 2012; the trial ran 19 days with 23 state witnesses, and the court added 64 to 89 months and two terms of 240 to 348 months.

— Who is who Salguero Olivares, 33, was born in Guatemala; Hedgepeth was a University of North Carolina student and a member of the Haliwa-Saponi Tribe.

— What to watch His lawyers have indicated an appeal, but no filing is known, and no Guatemalan government comment is known.

— What it means for you The verdict shows how DNA ancestry tools can solve old cases. It is one man’s crime; no source links it to Guatemalans in general.

A jury in Durham County, North Carolina, found Guatemalan Miguel Salguero Olivares guilty of murdering student Faith Hedgepeth in 2012. He received life without parole on Friday, 23 October.

A North Carolina jury has convicted Guatemalan Miguel Salguero Olivares of the Faith Hedgepeth murder, unsolved for more than nine years. Judge Keith Gregory sentenced him to life without parole on Friday, 23 October 2026.

Hedgepeth, 19, a University of North Carolina student, was found dead in her off-campus apartment on Friday, 7 September 2012. The verdict came in a Durham County courtroom, and Prensa Libre, a Guatemalan daily, reported it on Saturday, 24 October.

For US readers, this is a cold case solved with DNA. Prensa Libre in Guatemala reports it and calls him Guatemalan, and the Rio Times Guatemala hub tracks the country.

What the Jury Decided on Friday

WRAL, a Raleigh television station, reports guilty verdicts for first degree murder, burglary, rape and a sexual offense. ABC11, another Raleigh-Durham station, says the verdict came shortly before 4:30 p.m. after deliberations that began on Thursday.

The judge gave him life without parole for the murder, plus 64 to 89 months for burglary. He also gave 240 to 348 months each for rape and the sexual offense, all to run one after another.

The 240 to 348 month terms equal 20 to 29 years each. WRAL reports that the defendant said “It’s not fair” as the verdict was read, and that he shook his head at times.

How a Drunk Driving Stop Solved a 2012 Case

Authorities say DNA from a 2021 drunk driving stop matched evidence from the crime scene. WRAL reports he was arrested on Thursday, 16 September 2021, nine years after the killing.

ABC11 reported in January 2022, citing court documents, that investigators used DNA ancestry technology to find his distant relatives. Those relatives gave interviews and DNA samples, which investigators said helped identify him.

At trial, prosecutors presented DNA and fingerprint evidence they argued tied him to the scene. A forensic scientist said the DNA was 170 septillion times likelier from him and Hedgepeth than from an unknown person.

The State Bureau of Investigation (SBI), North Carolina’s state detective agency, says more than 25 agents worked the case. It collected more than 400 DNA samples, and prosecutors said the defendant was a stranger who acted in a fit of rage.

The Trial and the Defence Case

The trial opened on Wednesday, 7 October, and Friday was its 19th day including jury selection. The state called 23 witnesses over nine days and rested on Monday, 19 October.

The defence rested on Wednesday, 21 October, without calling a witness, and the defendant told the judge he would not testify. WRAL reports the defence argued that prosecutors had failed to prove their case and questioned the reliability of the investigation.

Defence attorney James Rainsford said in his opening that police lost evidence tied to apparent blood, WUNC reports. The jury returned guilty verdicts on every count after deliberating from Thursday to Friday afternoon.

Who Faith Hedgepeth Was

Hedgepeth grew up in Hollister, North Carolina, and was a member of the Haliwa-Saponi Tribe in Warren County. Native News Online reports she wanted to become a pediatrician and serve her community.

Her father, Roland Hedgepeth, counted the wait at 14 years, six weeks and four days. Her mother, Connie Hedgepeth, said in a victim impact statement that the family had closure and peace.

Haliwa-Saponi Tribal Chairman Earl Evans told Native News Online he hoped for closure for her family and the tribal nation. Judge Gregory told her mother his own son was at the same university at the time.

The Guatemalan Angle

Prensa Libre, a Guatemalan daily, calls him a Guatemalan and says US media report he is from Guatemala. ABC11 reported after his 2021 arrest that a neighbor said he had moved to the United States from Guatemala.

For background on the country, see the Rio Times guide to who holds power in Guatemala. No reviewed report links the verdict to Guatemala’s government, and none says Guatemala’s embassy has commented.

The sources reviewed do not state his immigration status, so this article does not either. One person’s crime does not define a country or the Guatemalans who live in the United States.

What It Means for US Readers

Court documents reported by ABC11 show investigators used DNA ancestry technology, which links crime scene DNA to distant relatives, to identify him. At trial, the jury heard separate DNA and fingerprint evidence, and the defence questioned the investigation.

For North Carolina, the conviction ends a case that was unsolved for more than nine years. Native News Online describes it as a high-profile missing and murdered Indigenous person case.

What Is Not Known

His immigration status, and whether he faces any federal immigration action, is not stated in the reports reviewed. WRAL reports he is appealing, but no filing or date has been reported.

Reports differ on whether Hedgepeth was a sophomore or a junior, so this article does not state her year. No statement from the Guatemalan government has been reported.

What Comes Next

WRAL reports he is appealing his convictions and sentences. The sources reviewed do not say when a filing was made or which court will hear it.

The life sentence carries no possibility of parole. The judge ordered the other sentences to run one after another rather than at the same time, WRAL reports.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was convicted in the Faith Hedgepeth murder?

Miguel Salguero Olivares, a 33 year old Guatemalan-born man, was convicted on Friday, 23 October 2026. A North Carolina jury found him guilty on all four counts.

What sentence did he receive?

He received life in prison without parole for first degree murder. The judge added 64 to 89 months for burglary and 240 to 348 months each for rape and a sexual offense.

How was the case solved?

ABC11 reported that investigators used DNA ancestry technology to find his distant relatives. DNA from a 2021 drunk driving stop then matched evidence from the 2012 scene, authorities said.

Why is a Guatemalan outlet covering it?

Prensa Libre reports it because it describes the defendant as a Guatemalan. ABC11 reported in 2021 that a neighbor said he moved from Guatemala.

Is an appeal expected?

WRAL reports he is appealing his convictions and sentences. No filing details had been reported by 24 October 2026.

Sources: WRAL, verdict and sentence; ABC11 live updates; ABC11, court documents (2022); ABC11, after arrest (2021); WUNC, AP trial opening; Native News Online; Prensa Libre (all accessed 24 October 2026).

World.content:

GUINEA · INFRASTRUCTURE

Key Facts — The country Guinea is a West African country on the Atlantic coast, run by President Mamadi Doumbouya, a former army colonel who took power in a 2021 coup.

— What happened Guinea ratifies road loan of 300 million euros (about US$336 million) by decree, reported on Saturday 24 October 2026.

— The lender A group of banks led by Bank of Africa United Kingdom, the London arm of Morocco’s Bank of Africa group, signed the loan with the government on 22 July 2026.

— The road The project paves 148.86 km of national roads 27 and 28, adds an 11.44 km spur at Banti-Koubia and builds a 200-metre bridge.

— The timeline Guinéenews reported in July that works are planned for 36 months, with the Compagnie sahélienne d’entreprises as the builder.

— The exchange rate The conversion uses 0.89 euros to the US dollar, the market rate of 24 October 2026.

— Still open The interest rate, the repayment period and the start date of works were not stated in the decree report.

Guinea ratifies road loan of 300 million euros (about US$336 million) to pave a highland road from Labé to Tougué in the north. The decree was read on national television, and Guinéenews reported it on Saturday 24 October 2026.

For US readers, the deal shows Guinea turning to Moroccan, Gulf and Chinese banks to finance roads. It also adds to Guinea’s debt as the country waits for revenue from the Simandou iron ore mine.

What the Decree Ratified

With the decree, Guinea ratifies road loan terms agreed between the government and several international banks for the Labé-Tougué national road. The decree was read out on national television, according to Guinéenews, a pioneer of online news in Guinea.

Finance minister Mariama Ciré Sylla and infrastructure minister Facinet Sylla signed the financing agreement on 22 July 2026 in Conakry, the capital. At that signing, Facinet Sylla said the agreement would take effect only after ratification.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Africa Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Is Lending the Money

Bank of Africa United Kingdom PLC acts as the lead arranger of the 300 million euro (about US$336 million) syndicated loan. A syndicated loan is a single loan shared among several banks, and this one brings together lenders from Africa, the Gulf and China.

Guinéenews lists Africa Finance Corporation, ABC Islamic Bank, Bank of Africa and Bank of China among the lenders, alongside banks from Kuwait and Abu Dhabi. Africa Finance Corporation is a Lagos-based investor in African infrastructure that is owned by African governments and institutions.

The Road From Labé to Tougué

The project covers 148.86 km on national roads 27 and 28, plus a spur of 11.44 km from Banti to Koubia on national road 34. Together that makes about 160 km of new asphalt in the Fouta Djallon highlands.

The plan includes a 200-metre bridge over the Bafing river, surfaced with bituminous concrete. The infrastructure minister said the prefectures of Tougué, Koubia and Bafing have never had a paved road since independence in 1958.

Islamic Finance and a First for Guinea

Bank of Africa said the operation is Guinea’s first appearance in the international syndicated loan market. It also includes an Islamic tranche of the Murabaha type, a cost-plus sale structure used in Islamic finance.

The Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit, known as ICIEC, partly insures the loan. The finance minister said both Bank of Africa United Kingdom and ICIEC are working in Guinea for the first time.

Why the Road Matters for Simandou 2040

The government presents the road as part of Simandou 2040, the president’s long-term development programme built around the giant Simandou iron ore mine. Finance minister Sylla said the road will bring farmers closer to markets and cut transport costs in a region of farming, herding and mining potential.

The central bank governor expects Simandou to pay the state about US$2.5 billion by 2040, the Rio Times reported on Wednesday 21 October. The government says it will borrow only for productive investment and keep debt sustainable.

What It Means for US Readers

American contractors should note that this road is financed by banks from Morocco, the Gulf, pan-African institutions and China, not Western lenders. Guinea is also drawing British interest, as the UK investment goal of about US$3.6 billion announced on 21 October showed.

For investors in Guinean debt, the loan is a new claim on state finances that arrives before the mining revenue. The road may also lower costs for any foreign firm that wants to reach farms and mines in the north.

What Is Not Known

The interest rate, the repayment period and the grace period of the 300 million euro (about US$336 million) loan have not been made public. Bank of Africa’s own statement, carried by Morocco’s Challenge magazine, gave the size as US$300 million, while Guinéenews and the decree report speak of euros.

The decree report does not say whether Parliament voted, although Facinet Sylla mentioned parliamentary ratification in July. The date when construction starts has not been announced, and the decree report does not say when repayments begin.

More: Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who ratified the Guinea road loan?

Guinea ratifies road loan agreements by decree, and this one was read on national television, according to Guinéenews on 24 October 2026. The loan agreement itself was signed on 22 July 2026.

How much is the Labé-Tougué loan worth?

Guinea ratifies road loan funding worth 300 million euros (about US$336 million) in the Guinéenews reports. Bank of Africa’s own statement, carried by Morocco’s Challenge magazine, gave the figure as US$300 million.

Who is lending the money to Guinea?

A syndicate led by Bank of Africa United Kingdom PLC, the London unit of Morocco’s Bank of Africa group. Other lenders named include Africa Finance Corporation, ABC Islamic Bank and Bank of China.

How long is the road being built?

The paved section is 148.86 km long, plus an 11.44 km spur at Banti-Koubia, about 160 km in all. It also includes a 200-metre bridge over the Bafing river.

What does ratification change?

Ratification is the step that brings the agreement into force, according to the infrastructure minister in July. The decree report gives no drawdown dates.

When will construction finish?

Guinéenews reported in July that works are planned for 36 months. A start date has not been announced.

World.content:

BRAZIL · EXPLAINER

Key Facts The country Brazil is South America’s largest country, with more than 210 million people, and it holds a presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October 2026.

What the TSE is The TSE is the Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, which runs elections and judges candidacy disputes.

The legal roads A candidate can be barred under the Ficha Limpa (Clean Record) law after a conviction, or under the Constitution’s ban on paramilitary groups.

The challenge Under Complementary Law 64 of 1990, a candidate, party, coalition or electoral prosecutor has 5 days from publication of a registration request to challenge it.

What happened On Friday 23 October 2026 the electoral prosecution asked the TSE to bar Rio state deputy-elect Márcio Canella, who has not been convicted.

TSE candidate vetting can end in rejection over alleged organized crime ties even without a conviction, as Rio deputy-elect Márcio Canella’s case shows. This explainer sets out the law and deadlines, while our Brazil election 2026 coverage follows the vote.

The case leaves the presidential race alone, so the Brazil election polls, the Brazil election odds and the Brazil runoff date stay unchanged. Our news report on the electoral prosecutor’s request against Canella covers the filing itself.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.0 %, Lula 49.0 % 43 national polls from 20 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

TSE Candidate Vetting in Plain Terms

TSE candidate vetting is run by Brazil’s electoral justice, led by the Superior Electoral Court, which registers candidates and settles who may run. Before anyone appears on a ballot, a court must approve the registration, and approval can be challenged.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

A challenge to a registration is called an impugnação in Portuguese. It is the main tool of the electoral prosecution when it believes a candidate is barred from office, including over alleged ties to criminal groups.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Brazil Elections 2026 Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Decides: The TSE, Regional Courts and the Prosecutor

Complementary Law 64 of 1990, published on the Planalto presidency’s legal database, says the TSE judges challenges to presidential candidates. Regional electoral courts, the TREs, judge senators, governors and federal and state deputies, so a Rio state deputy starts at the TRE-RJ.

In TSE candidate vetting, the Ministério Público Eleitoral, the electoral prosecution, is the part of Brazil’s federal prosecution service that acts. The same law lets any candidate, party or coalition file a challenge, and that does not stop the prosecutor from acting.

Two Legal Roads: Ficha Limpa and the Paramilitary Ban

The first road is the Ficha Limpa, or Clean Record, law, Complementary Law 135 of 2010, signed on 4 June 2010. It makes a person ineligible after a conviction by a panel of judges, even while appeals continue, until eight years after the sentence is served.

The crimes listed include money laundering, drug trafficking, terrorism and crimes committed by a criminal organization, a gang or a band. Ficha Limpa therefore needs a conviction, and an inquiry or an arrest alone does not trigger it.

The second road is Article 17, paragraph 4, of the Constitution, which says political parties may not use a paramilitary organization. In May 2025 the TSE unanimously upheld a ban on a Belford Roxo council candidate, and prosecutors say the Constitution was the ground.

That candidate had been convicted of forming a private militia and sentenced to eight years, the same release says. The electoral prosecution argues that TSE rulings let it bar politicians tied to such groups without a final conviction, if the evidence is solid.

Steps and Deadlines of TSE Candidate Vetting

TSE candidate vetting begins when parties file registrations, by 7 p.m. on 15 August of an election year, under the electoral law of 1997. For 2026 the TSE calendar sets 14 September as the date by which lower courts must decide every registration, challenged ones and their appeals included.

Under Complementary Law 64, a challenge must come within 5 days of the publication of the registration request. The candidate then has 7 days to answer, and the law gives 4 days to hear witnesses when needed and 5 days for final arguments.

The judge or rapporteur then decides, and an appeal to the TRE or the TSE normally has to be filed within 3 days of publication. These deadlines are continuous and do not pause for weekends or holidays after the registration deadline, the law says.

A candidate whose registration is still disputed on election day may campaign and appear on the ballot, under Article 16-A of the electoral law. Votes for that candidate count only if a higher court finally approves the registration.

The Canella Case as a Live Example

Márcio Canella, of the União Brasil party, is a former mayor of Belford Roxo, a city in Rio’s Baixada Fluminense area. He won 197,178 votes for the Rio state assembly, the second-highest total among state deputies in Rio, Metrópoles and O Antagonista report.

On Friday 23 October 2026, deputy electoral prosecutor-general Alexandre Espinosa asked the TSE to bar Canella’s registration, Metrópoles, Gazeta do Povo and O Antagonista report. It also asks the TSE to overturn the TRE-RJ decision that cleared him.

The filing says Canella acted as a political organizer of a criminal scheme and cites alleged militia and Comando Vermelho gang ties, Metrópoles reports. Gazeta do Povo adds that it alleges he appointed militia leaders to city posts and received money from the scheme.

Metrópoles says the prosecutor argues that the Rio court ruled before seeing evidence from a Supreme Court inquiry, whose secrecy was lifted this month. Tribuna do Sertão reported that the TRE-RJ approved his registration by 6 votes to 1 on Tuesday 29 September.

That inquiry is Operation Unha e Carne, in which Canella was arrested on Thursday 15 October, Gazeta do Povo reports. Police say a fuel-station network moved R$7.6 billion (about US$1.5 billion) in six years, and no conviction against Canella has been reported.

Our earlier reports cover the arrest in the fuel-laundering probe and the three elected candidates flagged for crime links. The outlets carry no reply to the new filing, though his lawyer earlier called the militia claim an extravagant story, Tribuna do Sertão reported.

What Happens After the Vote

Winning does not end TSE candidate vetting, since a mandate can be challenged within 15 days of the ceremony where winners receive their certificate. That ceremony is called the diplomação, and the challenge needs proof of abuse of economic power, corruption or fraud.

If a court finally rejects a registration, the electoral law says votes cast for that candidate do not count. The TSE must now decide whether to keep or reverse the Rio ruling, and none had been reported by Saturday 24 October.

What It Means for US Readers

TSE candidate vetting shows how Brazil’s courts handle alleged criminal infiltration of politics, which matters to anyone following the country’s institutions. This case concerns one Rio state seat and does not affect the presidential runoff, trade or travel.

Observers should watch whether the TSE accepts the prosecution’s reading that credible evidence can bar a candidate without a conviction. A ruling for the prosecution would set a precedent for TSE candidate vetting of other elected figures questioned over crime links.

What Is Not Known

It is not known when the TSE will finish its candidate vetting of Canella or whether it will accept the opinion. Nor is it known how his 197,178 votes will be treated if the TSE reverses the Rio ruling.

No court has ruled on the new allegations, and Canella has not been convicted of any crime in the cases cited. His defense has not been reported responding to the filing, and the facts are for the courts to decide.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can TSE candidate vetting reject someone without a conviction?

In TSE candidate vetting, the electoral prosecution argues that rulings allow it, under the Constitution’s ban on paramilitary groups, if the evidence is strong. The Ficha Limpa law, by contrast, requires a conviction.

What is the Ficha Limpa law?

Ficha Limpa, meaning Clean Record, is Complementary Law 135 of 2010, which bars people convicted by a panel of judges from running. The bar lasts until eight years after the sentence is served.

Who can challenge a candidate’s registration in Brazil?

Any candidate, party, coalition or the electoral prosecution can file within 5 days of publication of the registration request. The candidate then has 7 days to answer.

What did the prosecutor ask the TSE about Márcio Canella?

The deputy electoral prosecutor-general asked the TSE on Friday 23 October 2026 to bar his registration and reverse the Rio court’s approval. The filing’s allegations are unproven, and no TSE ruling has been reported.

Does the Canella case affect the 25 October runoff?

No outlet cited reports any effect on the presidential vote, which stays on Sunday 25 October 2026. The case concerns one seat in Rio de Janeiro’s state assembly.

World.title: Mexico F1 Organizers Reject Alternating Race
World.content:
Corona Capital returns to the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez from November 20 to 22 (Photo: ProtoplasmaKid, CC BY-SA 4.0)

Key Facts Stance: Mexico City’s Grand Prix organisers say they do not want to alternate years with another venue.

Contract: The race is contracted through 2028; no renewal has been signed.

Talks: Organisers expect talks with Formula 1 at the end of 2026 or early 2027.

Race: Sunday, November 1, 3:00 p.m. ET (2:00 p.m. Mexico City).

Impact: A business chamber forecasts US$1.2 billion (22.228 billion pesos) in economic activity.

The organisers of Formula 1’s race in Mexico City say they want it every year, not every other year, as our Mexico City Grand Prix updates page tracks. Director general Federico González Compeán said on October 21 that alternating seasons would complicate the logistics of an operation that works all year.

The current contract guarantees the race through 2028, and talks on a longer deal are expected at the end of 2026 or in early 2027. The next race is on Sunday, November 1, at 3:00 p.m. ET (2:00 p.m. Mexico City).

In plain English Formula 1 sells each race slot to a host city under a contract. Some European circuits now share a slot and race in alternate years, and Mexico City wants to avoid that.

Why Mexico Rejects a Shared Slot

González Compeán told Mexican media that racing only every second year would complicate the logistics of the event. He described an organisation that works throughout the year.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

He said organisers expect to open talks with Stefano Domenicali, Formula 1’s chief executive, around the end of this year or in early 2027. He said he is confident about renewal but stressed that the decision will come later.

Formula 1 already uses rotation elsewhere. Barcelona and Spa-Francorchamps are due to share a slot from 2028 to 2032, with Barcelona hosting in even years and Spa in odd years.

New Rivals for Calendar Space

Pressure on the calendar is growing. Rwanda has signed a deal to bring Formula 1 back to Africa from the early 2030s, which adds to competition for a limited number of dates.

Mexico is also adding to its own programme. Formula 2, the main support series, is due to race in Mexico City for the first time in October 2027.

File photo: a car at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City.

Race Weekend and Money

The 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix is round 19 of the season and runs from Friday, October 30, to Sunday, November 1. Qualifying is on Saturday, October 31, at 5:00 p.m. ET (3:00 p.m. Mexico City), and the race starts a day later at 3:00 p.m. ET (2:00 p.m.).

The gap between the two cities shrinks from two hours to one on race day because US clocks go back on November 1. Mexico does not change its clocks.

Canaco-CDMX, the capital’s chamber of commerce, estimates the race will generate 22.228 billion pesos (about US$1.2 billion at 18.65 pesos per dollar, RT market data, October 24) in economic activity. That is about 6.5% more than in 2025, and it is a forecast, not an audited result.

The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4.304-kilometre circuit more than 2 kilometres above sea level. Formula 1 lists its first Grand Prix there as 1963, and the race returned to the calendar in 2015.

What It Means for You

For fans in the United States, a guaranteed annual slot means a predictable date for planning a trip to Mexico City. Nothing beyond 2028 is secure yet.

The race follows the United States Grand Prix in Austin, held October 23 to 25, and precedes the Brazilian round on November 6 to 8.

What Is Not Known

No renewal has been signed, and no date for a meeting with Domenicali has been announced. The length of any new deal, the fee and any public support from Mexico City have not been disclosed.

Formula 1 has not said whether it would ask Mexico City to share its slot. The economic figure is the chamber’s own projection.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Mexico City want to alternate years with another race?

No. Director general Federico González Compeán said the logistics would be complicated for an event that works all year. Organisers want a full-time extension.

How long is the current contract?

The race is contracted through 2028. Talks on a longer deal are expected at the end of 2026 or in early 2027.

When is the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix?

The weekend runs from Friday, October 30, to Sunday, November 1, 2026. The race starts at 3:00 p.m. ET, which is 2:00 p.m. Mexico City time.

Which circuits already alternate years?

Barcelona and Spa-Francorchamps are due to share one slot from 2028 to 2032. Barcelona hosts in even years and Spa in odd years.

World.title: Argentina Detains Priest and 2 at Protest
World.content:
ARGENTINA · PROTEST

Key Facts — What is happening Argentine federal police detained priest Paco Olveira and activists Cristian Valderrama and Lucas García at a pension protest in Buenos Aires on Friday, 23 October 2026; the priest was freed that evening.

— Why it matters Protesters call it repression of a peaceful march, while officials describe an attempt to force entry into the presidential palace, so the two accounts clash.

— The numbers Three people were held and one official was hurt in the scuffle; the minimum October pension is ARS 435,748.51 (about US$285), plus a bonus of up to ARS 70,000 (about US$46).

— Who is who Olveira belongs to a group of priests who back the poor; Valderrama and García became known through a viral flag photo at a university funding march.

— What to watch Whether any court brings charges against the three, whether the government publishes its own account, and how police handle the next pension protest in central Buenos Aires.

— Power Index Argentina ranks 4th of 14 in Argentina ranks 4th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 61.2 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you Visitors to central Buenos Aires can expect heavy police presence around Plaza de Mayo, and investors watch social tension because it tests the government’s austerity drive.

Federal police held a priest and two activists near the presidential palace on Friday. Protesters and officials give very different accounts of why.

Federal police detained priest Francisco “Paco” Olveira and two activists at a pension protest in Buenos Aires on Friday, 23 October 2026. The priest was freed shortly before 9 p.m. local time, according to TeleSol Diario and Del Sur Diario.

Protest accounts say the three were held only for carrying the Argentine flag. Official accounts describe an attempt to force entry into the Casa Rosada, the presidential palace.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 61.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The case matters to US readers because it tests how President Javier Milei’s government handles protest at its own palace. Investors in Argentine bonds and shares watch such social tension closely.

What Happened at Plaza de Mayo

Plaza de Mayo is the square in front of the Casa Rosada, in central Buenos Aires. On Friday afternoon, federal police detained Olveira and two other protesters there during a retirees’ protest.

The two others are Cristian Valderrama and Lucas García, according to Página/12, Minuto Uno and TeleSol Diario. Olveira belongs to Curas en Opción por los Pobres, a group whose name means “Priests in Option for the Poor”.

TeleSol Diario and Del Sur Diario report that Olveira was accused of resisting authority. They say the other two remained held after he left custody.

Olveira had been detained at earlier protests, in November 2025 and February 2026, those outlets add. By that count, this is his third detention in under a year.

Who Are the Two Activists

Valderrama and García became known at the latest Marcha Federal Universitaria, a march to defend public university funding. A photo showed them holding an Argentine flag in front of an advancing water-cannon truck.

Since then they have joined pension marches and other protests, TeleSol Diario reports. Tiempo Argentino, a left-leaning outlet, calls them symbols of resistance.

Only Tiempo Argentino reports that both were released in the early hours of Saturday, 24 October. It says they were held at a police facility at Suipacha 150 while human rights groups waited outside overnight.

Two Accounts of What Happened

Olveira told reporters the two young people were detained “only for carrying the Argentine flag”. He said he went inside the police line to stand beside them and not leave them alone.

Página/12, a newspaper critical of the government, headlined the arrests as violence and repression during a peaceful retirees’ protest. Its report says federal police made the arrests.

The official version came through the news agency Noticias Argentinas, as relayed by Minuto Uno. It says authorities reported that three people tried to force their way into the Casa de Gobierno.

A scuffle followed with presidential guards and security forces, and the three were restrained and arrested, Minuto Uno and Diario Crónica report. The official running the building’s operations was hurt and taken to the Churruca-Visca medical complex as a precaution, official versions say.

One detainee wore clothing with inscriptions referring to Olveira and a group called “Los 12 apóstoles”, the same reports say. LCR Diario Digital adds that officials stressed the security protocol worked and that the president and other officials were not at risk.

Federal forces then reinforced patrols and checks around the perimeter and main entrances of the Casa Rosada. Neither account has been tested in court.

Why Retirees Keep Marching

Retirees hold weekly protests in central Buenos Aires over their income. The October minimum pension is ARS 435,748.51 (about US$285, at ARS 1,528 per US$ on 24 October 2026), up 1.66%.

ANSES, the national social security agency, also pays a bonus of up to ARS 70,000 (about US$46), iProfesional reports. With it, the lowest pensioners receive ARS 505,748 (about US$331).

What It Means for US Readers

Scenes at the Casa Rosada draw attention abroad, including in the United States. Investors in Argentine bonds and shares watch whether social tension complicates the government’s austerity drive.

Visitors to central Buenos Aires can expect a heavy police presence around Plaza de Mayo on protest days. Reports say federal forces tightened checks around the palace after Friday’s incident.

Related reports cover the Falklands bill, the LIBRA ruling for Milei and the Kirchner trial. The Argentina news hub and the guide to Argentina give more context.

What Is Not Known

No Ministry of Security statement was found, and the official account rests on agency reports citing unnamed sources. The Página/12 page could not be read in full, so its text was checked in republished copies.

No report says whether a court opened a case against anyone. Every report opened names one injured official, with no medical details.

The release of the two activists rests on Tiempo Argentino alone. No Infobae, La Nación, Clarín or Perfil report was found, no video is verified, and no court has ruled.

What Comes Next

The next step is whether a federal prosecutor or judge brings charges over the Casa Rosada incident. The next weekly retirees’ protest at Plaza de Mayo will show how police handle the crowd.

Release from custody does not mean the cases are closed, and it does not settle which account is right. Any charges would be allegations until a court decides.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Paco Olveira?

Francisco “Paco” Olveira is a Catholic priest in the group Curas en Opción por los Pobres. Argentine outlets say police also detained him at protests in November 2025 and February 2026.

Why were the three detained in Buenos Aires?

Police have not given a public reason in the reports found. Protesters say they were held for carrying a flag, while officials describe an attempt to force entry into the Casa Rosada.

Are the three still in custody?

Olveira was freed shortly before 9 p.m. on Friday, 23 October. Only Tiempo Argentino reports that the other two went free early on Saturday.

What is the Casa Rosada?

The Casa Rosada, or Pink House, is the seat of Argentina’s presidency on Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires. It is the country’s equivalent of the White House.

What is the minimum pension in Argentina in October?

The minimum pension is ARS 435,748.51 (about US$285). A bonus of up to ARS 70,000 (about US$46) lifts it to ARS 505,748 (about US$331).

Sources: Página/12, 23 October; Minuto Uno, 23 October; Diario Crónica, 23 October; LCR Diario Digital, 24 October; TeleSol Diario, 23 October; Del Sur Diario, 23 October; Pura Ciudad, 23 October; Tiempo Argentino, 24 October; iProfesional on ANSES pensions, October; exchange rate from open.er-api.com, 24 October 2026 (all accessed 24 October 2026).

World.title: Brazil Judge Toffoli Urges Ad Curbs 24 Oct
World.content:
BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Key Facts — What is happening Justice Dias Toffoli of Brazil’s electoral court said on Saturday, 24 October, that courts should stop campaign airtime and social posts from becoming a “ring” of attacks.

— Why it matters He spoke to international observers on the eve of the runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, and the report mentions no new rule or vote.

— The numbers Brazil’s electoral courts have taken in more than 100,000 cases this year, mostly about campaign accounts and irregular election ads.

— Who is who Toffoli sits on both the Supreme Court and the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), which is led by president Kassio Nunes Marques.

— What to watch Voting on Sunday, 25 October, and whether the court turns Toffoli’s call into a formal proposal or resolution for future elections.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro an 82.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 17.5% (24 October, 12:52 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 83% and Kalshi at 84% (Lula: 18% and 17% ), as of 24 October, 1:00 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

— What it means for you US investors in Brazilian assets face a runoff that the ad debate does not change.

Justice Dias Toffoli says Brazil’s electoral courts should stop free airtime from turning into personal attacks. The report mentions no draft text and no vote.

Justice Dias Toffoli of Brazil’s electoral court said on Saturday, 24 October, that courts should stop campaign airtime becoming a ring. He spoke a day before the Brazil election 2026 runoff between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

CNN Brasil reports that he told international observers that voters now see personal clashes instead of government plans. Bettors still see a Flávio win, as the latest Brazil election odds show.

WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Toffoli Said About Election Ads

Toffoli spoke at a morning meeting with international observers and representatives, the broadcaster reported. He said the electoral courts should find ways to stop candidates’ airtime becoming a ring.

Politics must go back to discussing politics, he said. He called it a challenge for Brazil and for much of the democratic world.

Toffoli criticised using free election airtime for attacks between candidates. He argued that citizens effectively pay for it, because broadcasters receive tax relief for the time they provide.

He said citizens should not have to pay for offences between candidates. Voters, he said, have stopped following government proposals and now watch personal clashes in official ads and on social networks.

A Call, Not Yet a Rule

The report does not say Toffoli filed a draft, asked for a vote or gave a date. Valor Econômico also covered the remarks, but its article could not be opened and is not relied on.

The remarks came at a meeting with observers, not in a ruling. A call by one justice does not by itself change what campaigns may broadcast.

What He Said Two Days Earlier

Toffoli raised the issue on Thursday, 22 October, during a TSE plenary session, the broadcaster reported. He called campaigns built on accusations against rivals and their allies shameful, saying that is not real campaigning.

Justice Estela Aranha backed him, saying ads built on organised crime accusations would leave no real campaign. She added that the court had tried to talk to the campaigns.

The ruling came in a case brought by a Flávio Bolsonaro colleague, who wanted an ad from Lula’s coalition removed. The ad carried an accusatory line about Flávio and showed a photo of a group she belonged to.

By majority, the court allowed the ad to air provided her face was blurred. It did not order the ad removed.

The Court Under Pressure Before Sunday

The broadcaster says the electoral courts have taken in more than 100,000 cases this year. Most concern campaign accounts and reports of irregular propaganda.

Brazil’s campaign has also turned on a challenge over secrecy. Justice André Mendonça, the TSE vice-president, let both candidates publish their own bank, tax and phone data on Thursday.

The TSE barred allies Nikolas Ferreira and Pablo Marçal from false posts on Friday, 23 October, in Brazil court bars false posts. On Tuesday the court upheld a takedown order over posts linking Flávio Bolsonaro to crime.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a crypto-based exchange, bettors gave Flávio Bolsonaro an 82.8% chance of winning at 12:52 p.m. ET on Saturday, 24 October. Lula stood at 17.5%.

The Flávio contract has traded about US$26.7 million, and the whole Brazil presidential event about US$194.9 million. These are bets on the Sunday vote, not polls, and nothing in them measures the ad debate.

Prices move fast and are bets, not polls. Live prices follow.

Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. What It Means for US Readers

US investors with Brazilian stocks, bonds or the real face a runoff that the ad debate does not change. Toffoli’s remarks matter because they show the court’s concern about the tone of the final campaign days.

The latest Brazil election polls show how close the race is, according to the Rio Times tracker. More coverage is on the Brazil news hub.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether Toffoli will file a formal proposal, or whether the TSE plenary would take it up. No source gives a date, a draft text or a vote count.

It is also unclear whether any limit could apply before Sunday’s vote. Nothing in the report suggests that it could.

The TSE website and Valor could not be opened, so the remarks rest on one news report. Details found only in Valor are not used here.

What Comes Next

Voting takes place on Sunday, 25 October, and the Brazil runoff date page explains when results come in. The TSE counts the votes and announces the winner.

Any change to ad rules would follow later, if the court takes it up. A call by one justice does not by itself change what campaigns may broadcast.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Dias Toffoli say about election ads?

He said electoral courts should find ways to stop campaign airtime becoming a ring of attacks. He said politics must return to discussing politics.

Has Brazil changed its election ad rules?

Not so far as reported. The report mentions no draft, vote or resolution, only Toffoli’s remarks on Saturday, 24 October.

Who is Dias Toffoli?

He is a justice of Brazil’s Supreme Court who also sits on the Superior Electoral Court. He spoke to international observers on Saturday.

Why did he mention taxes?

Toffoli said broadcasters get tax relief for campaign airtime. He argued that citizens effectively pay for it.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Voters choose between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro on Sunday, 25 October. The TSE counts the votes and announces the winner.

World.title: Santa Cruz Inspector’s New Truck and Mayor’s Son’s Bank Deposits Under Scrutiny in Guanacaste Probe
World.content:
A municipal inspector in Santa Cruz, Guanacaste, bought a new Toyota Hilux for 21.2 million colones (about $46,500) that his income cannot account for, according to a police report in the corruption investigation that has reached the area’s mayor. The inspector, Carlos Cedeño Leiva, is one of nine people under investigation for alleged influence peddling, bribery and illicit enrichment. The group includes Santa Cruz Mayor Jorge Arturo Alfaro Orias and his son, Jorge Alfaro Molina. None of them has been charged, and all are presumed innocent.

The police report lists other vehicles registered to the inspector, including a Yamaha motorcycle, a Hyundai Accent and a Hino Dutro truck, as well as a Hyundai Tucson bought in his wife’s name in August 2024. Investigators say the Hilux purchase does not match the asset declaration the inspector filed with the tax administration. He did not respond to requests for comment from local media.

The case is led by the Deputy Prosecutor’s Office for Probity, Transparency and Anticorruption and prosecutors suspect that municipal officials, including the mayor, the head of urban planning and inspectors, fast-tracked construction permits, land-use approvals, favorable inspections and coastal concessions in exchange for money or gifts.

According to the case file, the mayor’s son acted as a link between business owners and municipal staff. He is listed as president of Tamarindo Los Sueños Tres Marettimo S.A., a company that also involves two representatives of Constructora Masorati, both surnamed Canales.

Investigators found transfers from Constructora Masorati and the Tamarindo company into the son’s accounts, with no matching outflows to justify them. Prosecutors are treating those deposits as possible unlawful gains and are seeking banking and tax records. No total amount has been disclosed.

Prosecutors also point to the construction company’s rapid growth. It handled 21 projects in 2023 and another 20 through September 2024, an increase they link to the start of contacts between the businessmen and municipal officials. The case file attributes 145 construction permit applications to the company and one of its representatives, although not all of them were necessarily approved.

Phone records cited by prosecutors show calls between the private parties and officials responsible for permits, land use and inspections, which they view as possible signs of coordination. The investigation also covers an alleged scheme to obtain concessions in the Maritime Terrestrial Zone at Junquillal, Playa Blanca and Avellanas. According to prosecutors, those involved would then sell shares or transfer the concession rights to third parties for large sums through corporations.

Judicial investigators searched the Santa Cruz municipal offices, a construction company’s headquarters and two homes earlier this week, in the first public step of the Guanacaste permit investigation. Francisco Mairena, the municipality’s press officer, said the mayor would not comment because the case is already before the courts. He said the other officials involved would not comment either and that all of them continue to work normally.

Santa Cruz covers a large stretch of Guanacaste’s Pacific coast, including Tamarindo, Flamingo and Playa Grande, where tourism and real estate growth has driven demand for permits and coastal concessions. The allegations reflect the prosecution’s hypothesis at the investigative stage and do not constitute a judicial finding of responsibility.

World.title: International News: Vance becomes 11th Pacific hurricane this season
World.content:
International News: Vance becomes 11th Pacific hurricane this season

By Zoila Palma: Hurricane Vance became the 11th major hurricane of the 2026 central and eastern Pacific hurricane season on Friday, as meteorologists monitored its movement toward Mexico’s west-central coast.

According to AccuWeather, the storm briefly reached Category 3 status on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, with maximum sustained winds of at least 111 miles per hour. Forecasters are tracking multiple possible scenarios, including one in which the hurricane remains offshore and another in which it turns toward the Mexican coast.

Vance developed after an area of disturbed weather strengthened into a tropical depression on Wednesday before becoming a tropical storm four hours later. It intensified into a hurricane early Friday, with sustained winds reaching 90 miles per hour by 9 a.m. Friday.

AccuWeather Hurricane Expert Alex DaSilva said the storm could remain over open waters but warned that a northeast turn toward Mexico’s west-central coast could result in more dangerous conditions.

World.title: Belize Coast Guard cadet Elvis Solis completes major milestone in Mexico
World.content:
Belize Coast Guard cadet Elvis Solis completes major milestone in Mexico

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Coast Guard (BCG) is congratulating Cadet Elvis Solis on successfully completing four years of academic and military training in Naval Nursing at the Centro de Estudios Navales en Ciencias de la Salud (CENCIS), under Mexico’s Naval University. The achievement marks a significant milestone in his journey toward becoming a qualified naval nurse.

Solis’s accomplishment reflects the Belize Coast Guard’s continued investment in developing its future leaders and specialized personnel. The training equips cadets with the academic knowledge and military skills necessary to support healthcare services within the naval force.

Following the successful completion of this phase of training, Solis will be commissioned into the Belize Coast Guard at the rank of Lieutenant Junior Grade before proceeding to his fifth and final year of professional training.

Upon successfully completing the final year, he will qualify for a Bachelor’s Degree in Naval Nursing.

The Belize Coast Guard commended Solis for his dedication, perseverance and commitment to excellence.

The Belize Coast Guard also expressed appreciation to the Government of Mexico and the Mexican Navy for their continued partnership and support in advancing the professional development of Belizean personnel.

World.title: BDF officer cadets participate in selection process for U.S. Army Officer candidate school
World.content:
BDF officer cadets participate in selection process for U.S. Army Officer candidate school

By Zoila Palma: Belize Defence Force (BDF) officer cadets have participated in a selection process for the opportunity to attend the United States Army Officer Candidate School (OCS), marking an important step in their military careers and professional development.

The process provides aspiring officers with an opportunity to demonstrate their readiness for the responsibilities of commissioned service.

The selection process is intended to identify candidates prepared to meet the demands of military leadership and serve with dedication. For the participating cadets, the opportunity represents more than selection, as it also involves preparing to lead with integrity, accept responsibility and uphold the professional standards expected of a BDF officer.

The Commander of the Belize Defence Force commended all participating officer cadets for their dedication and willingness to undertake the challenge of pursuing professional development through OCS. The Commander noted that their ambition reflects the importance of developing capable leaders who can contribute meaningfully to the Force and the country.

The BDF Force Headquarters and Training and Doctrine Battalion extended their best wishes to the candidates as they continue their journey toward commissioned service.

World.title: Belize Defence Force Air Wing commander receives Brazilian Order of Aeronautical Merit
World.content:
Belize Defence Force Air Wing commander receives Brazilian Order of Aeronautical Merit

By Zoila Palma: Lieutenant Colonel Kenroy Smith, Commanding Officer of the Belize Defence Force (BDF) Air Wing, has been awarded the Order of Aeronautical Merit in the grade of Grand Officer (Grande Oficial) by the Government of Brazil.

The award was presented by Brazil’s Ambassador to Belize, Olyntho Vieira, during a ceremony at the Brazilian Embassy in Belmopan on October 23, 2026, as part of the observance of Brazilian Aviation Day.

The Order of Aeronautical Merit is a distinguished Brazilian Air Force decoration that recognizes outstanding service and exceptional contributions to military aviation and aeronautical development.

Smith’s recognition highlights his contributions to advancing military aviation, strengthening regional cooperation and building professional ties between the Belize Defence Force and Brazil’s armed forces.

The BDF congratulated Smith on the achievement, commending his dedication, professionalism and commitment to excellence.

The BDF also expressed appreciation to the Government and people of Brazil for their longstanding support in defence, security, training and military professional development.

World.title: Belize marks United Nations Day, celebrates work of 22 UN agencies
World.content:
Belize marks United Nations Day, celebrates work of 22 UN agencies

By Zoila Palma: Belize joins the international community today in commemorating United Nations Day, marking the 81st anniversary of the global organization.

The occasion highlights the work of 22 United Nations agencies operating in Belize, 12 of which are based in the country, supporting development initiatives in partnership with the Government, civil society and local communities.

United Nations Day commemorates the entry into force of the UN Charter on October 24, 1945, which officially established the organization.

The annual observance provides an opportunity to reaffirm the principles of peace, international cooperation, equality and sustainable development that guide the United Nations in its efforts to address global challenges and promote a better future for all.

In Belize, the work of UN agencies and their partners focuses on creating opportunities for people and building a more inclusive, resilient and sustainable country.

This year’s observance also highlights the importance of collaboration in advancing human dignity and ensuring that no one is left behind.

Special Envoy Rossana Briceno said the day celebrates the power of unity, peace and international cooperation, encouraging renewed commitment to equality and sustainable development.

World.title: International News: France deploys 70,000 police as demonstrations continue over cost of living
World.content:
International News: France deploys 70,000 police as demonstrations continue over cost of living

By Zoila Palma: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Paris and other French cities today as authorities deployed 70,000 police officers to prevent a repeat of the riots and looting that swept across the country the previous weekend, Reuters report.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 135 people had been arrested nationwide by early afternoon, with some arrests following searches that uncovered fireworks, ball bearings and other items that could be used as weapons.

The heightened security measures included the deployment of 10,000 additional police officers and gendarmes compared with October 17, when protests over the cost of living and deteriorating public services escalated into some of France’s worst unrest in years.

While the main demonstration in Paris began peacefully, police fired tear gas at crowds in Lyon, the country’s third-largest city. Nunez warned that authorities faced significant calls for disruption from political groups and criminals.

Much of central Paris took on the appearance of a city under lockdown, with businesses boarding up storefronts, major cultural institutions closing and more than 20 metro stations shutting down.

World.title: International News: El Salvador’s President on rescue mission in Haiti: “God will grant us victory”
World.content:
International News: El Salvador’s President on rescue mission in Haiti: “God will grant us victory”

By Zoila Palma: President of El Salvador Nayib Bukele says that the Salvadoran army has launched a rescue mission to rescue four Salvadoran members of an international, United Nations-backed security force who are reportedly being held hostage by armed gangs in Haiti.

The four Salvadorans went missing on Sunday after jumping from a burning armored vehicle that was ambushed by armed gangs on the outskirts of Haiti’s capital while they were returning from a market to their base, according to security officials.

Bukele says that there are many messages and analysis claiming that the gangs in Haiti are not like those in El Salvador—”that they are bloodthirsty, heavily armed, and unconquerable; that all previous missions have failed; that we are walking into a trap; that we do not know what we are facing; that this will be our ruin; and that we are heading toward our own Waterloo.”

Bukele says that God will grant victory to the Salvadoran army.

“But when God grants us victory, those same people who are saying all this today will change their tune. They will claim that it was always easy, that anyone could have done it, and that the gangs in Haiti were never as dangerous as people thought.

In any case, we have never listened to them, and we are not going to start now.

Everyone who has enlisted is a believer, and we have entrusted this mission to God—whereas the gangs in Haiti are satanic, and it is common knowledge that they perform human sacrifices,” Bukele asserted.

“The Creator of the Universe is with us,” he said.
