World.title: Iraqi PM adviser accuses Iran of severe border violations and smuggling
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A senior adviser to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has openly accused Iran of orchestrating deliberate security breaches, widespread drug smuggling, and illicit financial flows across the border, marking a rare and pointed public rebuke from within Baghdad’s executive circle as Iraq shuttered key commercial crossing points.

Speaking to domestic media, prime ministerial adviser Abdelamir Taiban stated that Tehran has actively undermined Iraqi internal stability by allowing unauthorized, affiliated networks to bypass border protocols, inciting borderland disorder.

Taiban noted that Iraqi nationals have faced abductions after entering Iranian territory, identifying the areas surrounding the Shalamcheh terminal in Basra and the Al-Sheeb terminal in Maysan as high-risk corridors. He urged the federal government to aggressively scale electronic monitoring and comprehensive automation across every operational terminal along the shared 1,599-kilometer frontier.

The adviser characterized the inbound traffic of narcotics and counterfeit currency as the most damaging economic threat facing the nation, asserting that the resulting market sabotage has inflicted financial disruption outpacing the economic fallout previously caused by ISIS.

The remarks follow the indefinite closure of the Al-Sheeb port of entry in Maysan governorate to both travelers and commercial cargo—a measure following the precautionary shutdown of Shalamcheh in September amid regional drone incidents—which prompted demonstrations by local transport operators and cross-border truckers concerned over disrupted trade in fresh produce and construction materials.

In response, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi convened the Ministerial Council for National Security, ordering security units to safeguard peaceful assemblies while maintaining stringent checks to intercept illicit trafficking channels.

World.title: US dollar dips to 168,500 IQD following Zaidi’s remarks on cash inflows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar retreated by approximately 1,000 dinars per $100 across parallel market trading desks on Saturday, October 24, 2026.

The softening followed public statements delivered on Friday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, in which he disclosed that Washington will dispatch $1 billion in physical cash shipments to Iraq and assured the public that parallel rates will soon decline toward 155,000 dinars per $100.

The remarks stemmed upward momentum that had pushed dollar transactions across domestic exchange bureaus to 169,500 dinars on Thursday and Friday, driving the prevailing market benchmark down to 168,500 dinars.

Across major trading hubs in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra, foreign exchange desks and licensed counters posted identical rates on Saturday morning, listing cash selling quotes at 169,000 dinars against buying bids of 168,500 dinars per $100.

Despite the temporary retreat, parallel figures continue to maintain a notable spread over the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory cash peg, which remains set at 152,000 dinars per $100.

The divergence highlights persistent liquidity dynamics and demand pressures outside central electronic settlement channels, even as executive assurances of incoming dollar consignments aim to stabilize market sentiment and curb speculative price premiums.

World.title: US State Department reissues Level 4 ‘Do Not Travel’ advisory for Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. Department of State issued a renewed travel advisory on Saturday, October 24, 2026, maintaining its highest “Level 4: Do Not Travel” warning for Iraq and urging American citizens to avoid travel to the country under any circumstances.

According to the advisory, Washington cited the inability of Iraqi authorities to guarantee the safety of foreign nationals in the event of sudden armed conflict or localized violence, while emphasizing the U.S. government’s severely constrained capacity to execute emergency evacuations or consular relief operations inside Iraqi territory.

The State Department warned of acute security and public health vulnerabilities, citing risks from terrorism, kidnappings, civil unrest, and frequent asymmetric strikes. It specified recurring hazards from improvised explosive devices (IEDs), unmanned aerial systems, and indirect rocket fire conducted by Iran-aligned armed groups and remnants of ISIS against U.S. personnel, diplomatic compounds, commercial companies, energy installations, and commercial airports.

The advisory also drew attention to regional escalation vectors—including cross-border hostilities conducted by the Houthi movement—as well as widespread unmarked minefields and UXO hazards, aviation restrictions implemented under Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) notices, and severe structural shortages across Iraq’s trauma and emergency medical infrastructure.

In response to sustained security threats, strict operating restrictions remain enforced on U.S. diplomatic personnel, requiring special authorization for in-country travel and residency within heavily fortified protocols.

For private American citizens currently residing in Iraq, the State Department urged immediate contingency planning independent of U.S. governmental assistance, including enrolling in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP), drafting emergency wills and power-of-attorney designations, leaving DNA reference samples with family medical providers, securing private medical and emergency evacuation insurance, and developing comprehensive personal departure protocols.

World.title: Iraqi FM Fuad Hussein condemns deadly church attack in Jordan’s Karak
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein held a telephone conversation on Friday, October 23, 2026, with Jordan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Ayman Safadi, strongly condemning the deadly armed attack that targeted mourners at a church in Jordan’s southern Karak Governorate.

During the call, Hussein conveyed Iraq’s full solidarity with the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in confronting terrorism and violent extremism.

The Iraqi foreign minister extended the government and people of Iraq’s heartfelt condolences to the leadership, government, and citizens of Jordan, as well as to the families of the victims, while wishing a swift recovery to those injured.

The diplomatic outreach followed a shooting incident earlier on Friday, in which unidentified gunmen opened fire during a funeral service at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hmoud, located in Karak Governorate approximately 180 kilometers south of Amman.

The attack left at least seven people dead and dozens wounded, prompting heightened security deployments and an active manhunt by Jordanian security agencies.

World.title: Ukraine says two soldiers died after arrested girl sent Russian poison
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian police said Friday they had detained a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia’s security services to poison Ukrainian soldiers and that two had died.

Ukraine and Russia have throughout their war since 2022 accused each other of recruiting minors for sabotage acts including poisoning.

The girl, who was not named, is suspected of having packaged deadly drugs and sending them to Ukrainian soldiers she contacted by Telegram, said a police statement.

She was arrested by police in Zhytomyr, west of Kyiv, after allegedly following instructions from a Russian handler in exchange for at least 5,000 hryvnias ($111), they said.

After receiving packages with “free drugs”, the soldiers were “instructed to take them on camera”, the statement said.

“The recipients did not know that the capsules contained a lethal dose of methadone,” it said, adding that “two soldiers died from poisoning in the Zhytomyr region.”

Police said they had identified other recipients of the packages, which “prevented four more murders” across the country.

“The young woman was notified that she is suspected of aiding and abetting the premeditated murder of two people as part of a prior conspiracy,” the police statement said.

She was also suspected of “shipping drugs and psychotropic substances for the purpose of distribution”, it said, adding that she faced up to 15 years in jail if found guilty.

Police cautioned that Russia aims “to kill our people and destabilise the situation within the country”.

“Do not accept medication or other substances, as well as food or drinks of dubious origin, from people you do not know well,” police cautioned.

Since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Ukrainian authorities say they have opened thousands of investigations into collaboration with the enemy, and frequently arrest individuals accused of working for Moscow.

In 2023, Ukraine accused Russia of poisoning the wife of Kyrylo Budanov, who was then head of Ukraine’s military intelligence and is now a presidential advisor.

World.title: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts
World.content:
Stockholm – Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.

The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide.

Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year.

It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.

Shortly after 0800 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down almost 30 percent.

“We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change,” chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, “through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees”.

The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.

In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

“We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges,” Samuelsson said.

“However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient.”

Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.

The company said in September that Samuelsson would resign when his contract ends, with Skoda Auto CEO Klaus Zellmer set to replace him “no later” than October next year.

World.title: France braces for new protests as Macron seeks to restore order
World.content:
Paris – France was on Friday bracing for a weekend of new protests after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, as President Emmanuel Macron sought to reclaim the initiative and restore order.

Macron, who on Thursday announced that only union demonstrations would be authorised this weekend, was to hold a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and also meet security forces.

He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked a movement that has broadened nationwide into a show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city.

Macron is due to announce “additional decisions” after hosting the meeting of his defence council, on top of the limited curfews already announced, his office said.

At the meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP.

Pierre Sourzat, who heads the organisation Les Lyceens (The High School Students), was sceptical: “He’ll listen to us, pretend he’s understood us, and then nothing will come of it.”

Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday.

In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.

On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend.

– ‘Police have a responsibility’ –

Demonstrations in Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast have been banned at the weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares.

Marseille authorities however reversed a decision to halt all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short.

Some 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week.

“In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons.

The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors.

A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections.

It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 percent of the vote.

World.title: Kering shares tumble as Gucci fails to reassure investors
World.content:
Paris – Kering shares were down more than 10 percent in Paris Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand.

At 0730 GMT, Kering shares were down 10.8 percent at 190.40 euros, their lowest since June 2025. The market’s CAC40 index was down 0.3 percent.

Kering reported late Thursday that third-quarter sales were flat at 3.34 billion euros ($3.75 billion).

Sales at Gucci, by far the group’s largest single brand, fell by four percent to 1.29 billion euros, worse than the three-percent decline registered in the second quarter.

“Gucci has not shown convincing signs of stabilisation,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note.

Italy-based Gucci is key to Kering’s fortunes, but has been in freefall since 2023 as the brand lost its luxury cachet.

World.title: Congress high command steps in, asks Karnataka govt to probe alleged sting attempts on CMs
World.content:

and his Keralam counterpart V D Satheesan, party sources told PTI on Saturday.

The direction follows Shivakumar's recent claim that a businessman wearing Meta AI smart glasses met him under suspicious circumstances, prompting him to suspect that an attempt was being made to record or spy on him. The businessman had also met Satheesan, he said.

Speaking to a Kannada television channel, Shivakumar said the businessman had sought an appointment to discuss business but instead began talking about politics and electoral psephology.

âAn officer had fixed an appointment for a businessman to meet me. He took me to the ante-chamber and opened his laptop,â Shivakumar said.

World.title: RG Kar victim's parents question ex-principal Sandip Ghosh's bail; citizens' groups plan CBI office march
World.content:
The parents of the RG Kar rape-and-murder victim on Saturday questioned the bail granted to former hospital principal Sandip Ghosh in a corruption case, while announcing renewed calls for accountability in the investigation into their daughter's death.

Meanwhile, two citizens' groups, 'Voice of Abhaya' and 'Voice of Women', have announced a protest march to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) office on November 12, starting from RG Kar Medical College and Hospital. The organisers have appealed to citizens, particularly women, to join the demonstration and press for action in the case.

"We appeal to citizens from all sections of society, especially women, to come out on the streets on November 12 and show that they do not have to depend on any government to get their demands fulfilled.

Let the CBI know that despite attempts to destroy, withhold or suppress evidence, people are still protesting and are on the streets. There is no room for despair," one of the organisers said, as quoted by PTI.

The groups urged people not to lose hope and called on the investigating agency to act on the evidence.

The proposed demonstration comes amid mounting criticism from the victim's family and sections of the medical community over the pace of the investigation.





The Joint Platform of Doctors had also criticised the CBI last week following the Supreme Court's decision to grant bail to Ghosh, warning of a larger agitation over the slow progress of the probe.

The victim's mother, Ratna Debnath, who is now a BJP MLA, expressed anger over Ghosh's bail and questioned why those who were with her daughter in the hours before her death had not been arrested.

"If everyone had been arrested at the time instead of allowing evidence to be destroyed, the situation might have been different.

In every case, the last-seen theory is examined. Those present with my daughter must be questioned. The doctors have said that she died between midnight and 6 am. Who was with her during that period? Why have they not been arrested? Is it because they are doctors? My daughter was also a doctor," she said.

Debnath also demanded action against those she alleged had ordered the destruction of evidence following the crime.

"Who were the people who directed that everything be destroyed so quickly? The then health minister, the health secretary NS Nigam and Sandip Ghosh... those responsible must be identified. The main conspirators must be brought to justice," she said.

The victim's father also criticised the investigation and said Ghosh should have been sentenced to life imprisonment in the case, while expressing faith that justice would eventually be delivered.

"He should have been sentenced to life imprisonment in this case," he said.

Last week, the father had questioned the CBI's handling of the investigation and demanded that Ghosh be chargesheeted in the rape-and-murder case. He also said the agency's investigating officer, Monish Upadhyay, had told him that there was little the CBI could do at present and that the process would take time.

The father had expressed concern over the agency's accountability, saying, "If 1.47 billion people place their trust in an agency, how can they continue to have faith in it if such negligence persists? The government is not responsible; the investigating agency is."

Debnath had similarly said at the time that the government could not be held directly responsible for the CBI's actions, describing it as an independent investigating agency that would have to answer for its work.

The victim's father also questioned the continued tenure of West Bengal health secretary NS Nigam. "He will not remain in the post. The chief minister has said that if evidence is found, he can be removed," he said.

BJP leader Rahul Sinha also expressed surprise over Ghosh's bail but said the decision rested with the judiciary.

"We were also surprised that Sandip Ghosh got bail. I would clearly say that it would have been better if he had not been granted bail. But can any of us interfere with a judge? The decision to grant or deny bail rests entirely with the judiciary, and obtaining bail is also an individual's legal right. I can say clearly that nobody in Bengal is happy with this bail order," Sinha told reporters.

The Supreme Court granted bail to Ghosh on October 17 in the case concerning alleged financial irregularities at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital and the manipulation of merit scores to accommodate undeserving candidates.

A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale allowed his plea challenging the Calcutta High Court's February 23 order denying bail. The apex court took note of the period Ghosh had spent in custody and the pace of the trial, observing that he had been incarcerated for more than two years while only seven of the 147 witnesses had been examined.

Ghosh had resigned as the hospital's principal after the rape and murder of the postgraduate trainee doctor in August 2024. He was subsequently arrested in connection with alleged financial irregularities at the institution. The CBI had also arrested Ghosh and Abhijit Mondal, the then officer-in-charge of Tala police station, over allegations linked to evidence tampering and lapses in the investigation.

Junior doctor Aniket Mahata, a prominent figure in the RG Kar movement, had also criticised the bail decision last week, saying it had renewed anger among doctors and calling for a united fight for justice.

World.title: 'Opposes BJP by lineage': BJP MLA's swipe at Naseeruddin Shah over SRFTI row
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

MLA Ritesh Tiwari on Saturday hit out at veteran actor

over his support for protesting students at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Kolkata.

"Naseeruddin Shah is, by lineage, an opponent of the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Sangh.

I also know his elder brother. His daughter is married in Kolkata; she is the daughter-in-law of a CPI(M) leader and has even contested elections.

When ministers from West Bengal and the Mayor of Kolkata were raising the slogan of Dawat-e-Islam, why was Naseeruddin silent?... These are people who dance to the tune of foreign money, and the people of this country are watching," Tiwari said.

His remarks came after the veteran actor had criticised the BJP-led government in West Bengal over the reported action against students protesting at the institute.

In a video posted on Instagram, the actor alleged that the students were facing reprisals for demanding accountability from the administration and accused the government of targeting those who did not subscribe to its views.

"The BJPâ¦ after its manipulative victory in the Bengal elections now seems all out for revenge on anyone who does not subscribe to their beliefs and their policies," Shah said, adding that students had been served show-cause notices, placed under surveillance, threatened and asked to vacate their hostels.

World.title: EC declares UP MLC poll at three Agra stations 'void', orders repoll on October 26
World.content:
EC declares UP MLC poll at three Agra stations 'void'

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Saturday declared the poll taken on Friday at three polling stations of Agra division's teachers constituency for UP legislative council election, as "void" and ordered a fresh repoll there on Oct 26. This follows allegations of poll irregularities and harassment by the Samajwadi Party candidate and supporters.A communication sent by EC to the Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer on Saturday asked the Agra divisional commissioner to fix responsibility of the persons involved, including police and polling officers, that led to the incidents resulting in re-poll at the aforesaid polling stations. "This enquiry shall be done immediately and the report...sent to the Commission latest by 25.10.2026," stated the poll panel.The Commission declared as null and void the poll taken, in exercise of powers conferred on it under Section 58A (2)(a) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. "It must be ensured that the persons involved in any unlawful activities which may have caused the irregularities/lapses leading to vitiation of poll are not deputed during the said re-poll," the EC conveyed to the UP CEO.The commission further directed that indelible ink shall be applied on the right hand forefinger of the electors.A fresh permission for commencement of counting of votes in respect of Agra division Teachers' constituency shall be obtained after the successful completion of repoll in the aforementioned polling stations in the proforma prescribed by the Commission, the EC ordered.Dramatic scenes had unfolded after the poll in Agra as Samajwadi Party MLC candidate Akash Agarwal broke down before the media, alleging booth capturing, electoral irregularities and harassment of his supporters during polling.Agarwal accused the BJP and local administration of interfering with the polling process in Kheragarh, Fatehabad and other areas. He alleged that his supporters and school management associates across 12 districts were being harassed, with repeated complaints failing to bring any relief.

World.title: ‘Sri Lanka, Bangladesh happen when protests are not allowed’: Sonam Wangchuk on anti-SIR stir crackdown
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Activist

on Saturday described protests as a âgreat mechanismâ for governments to improve their performance, citing the unrest in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh as examples of what could happen when demonstrations are not allowed.

âNations all around the world happily permit protests, and that too right in front of Parliament. In countries like the UK, Norway and Sweden, protests are allowed right in front of Parliament,â the educationist said at an event in Mumbai.

âIn India, it was far from Parliament. Even when it was just Jantar Mantar, it was too far,â he added.

Wangchuk was referring to demonstrations held at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar, the capitalâs now-denotified designated protest site, in June and July following the NEET-UG paper leak in May.

The protests, in which Wangchuk played a key role by undertaking an indefinite fast for over 20 days before being removed and taken to a hospital, ended with the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25.

His remarks came amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.





The Centre deployed extensive security measures, drawing criticism from opposition parties.

âLook what happens when protests are not allowed. That is the example of Sri Lanka, Bangladesh,â Wangchuk remarked, referring to the youth- and student-led demonstrations in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh that culminated in the ouster of the incumbent governments.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âIf you (the Centre) do things that need not be done, people will turn against you.

This will only hurt the government. Do what is right,â he stated.

The movements in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh were also cited by several opposition leaders, civil society members and student leaders, some of whom called for âregime changeâ in India along the lines of the two neighbouring countries. After the ruling BJP seized on these remarks, alleging that the anti-CEC protestersâ real intention was to topple the democratically-elected Modi government, the leaders clarified that they were advocating "regime change through elections.

"

Delhi Police has also made several protesters sign peace bonds, undertaking to maintain "peace and good behaviour."

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Congress to launch door-to-door campaign, hold marches over voter list 'discrepancies'
World.content:
Congress alleged that crores of voters across the country had been unfairly deprived of their voting rights due to large-scale deletions and discrepancies in electoral rolls.

Congress to appoint booth-level agents

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Solanki flags discrepancies in Latur

NEW DELHI: The Congress will hold marches, conduct door-to-door visits and organise awareness meetings to address alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. The party will also ensure all eligible citizens are registered by the end of December, senior party leader and former Union minister Bharatsinh Solanki said on Saturday.Congress plans to appoint booth-level agents to verify voter lists and flag discrepancies to election authorities.Addressing a press conference, Solanki, an All India Congress Committee (AICC) observer, said the campaign would cover rural and remote areas as well as urban centres. It aims to put a special focus on disadvantaged communities and young voters. The party will distribute pamphlets and hold meetings to raise awareness about the issue, he added.Solanki alleged that crores of voters across the country had been unfairly deprived of their voting rights due to large-scale deletions and discrepancies in electoral rolls. He accused the Centre and the Election Commission of allowing electoral procedures to be misused."The country's democracy and Constitution are under threat amid rising inflation, unemployment and corruption. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi have launched a nationwide campaign to raise awareness about electoral malpractices," he said.As part of the campaign, the Congress will appoint a booth level agent-2 (BLA-2) at every polling booth to work alongside booth level officers (BLOs) and verify electoral rolls through door-to-door visits, Solanki said.The party will submit complaints to the relevant authorities over discrepancies and, if necessary, approach district election officials, the state election machinery and the Supreme Court, he added.Referring to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Solanki said the exercise had previously been undertaken in 12 states and was currently underway in 17 states. He alleged that the ECI, despite being an independent constitutional body, was facing pressure from those in power.Citing Latur city constituency, he said around 45,000 voter entries had been identified as suspicious or potentially affected by discrepancies. These included more than 12,000 entries relating to deceased voters, over 6,000 suspected duplicate entries, and names of people who were absent, had migrated or were listed at incorrect addresses, he said.

World.title: CBI books IL&FS Energy Development Co. and top directors in Rs 212 crore Canara Bank fraud case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered an FIR against Mumbai-based firm and its top executives for allegedly cheating Canara Bank of Rs 212 crores, officials said on Saturday.

Searches were conducted in Delhi, Mumbai and Noida Saturday and incriminating documents seized.

The agency has named as accused M/s IL & FS Energy Development Company Limited along with its Managing Directors and Directors - Sunil Wadhwa, Anoop Seth, Hari Sankaran, Ramesh Chandra Bawa, and Arun Kumar Saha âin addition to unknown public servants and private individuals.

The case was registered on October 21 following a formal complaint lodged by Canara Bankâs Circle Office in Bandra (East), Mumbai.

According to the CBI, the accused entered into a criminal conspiracy to secure a term loan of Rs 100 crore from the erstwhile Syndicate Bank (now merged with Canara Bank) at its Large Corporate Branch in Mumbai, along with a foreign currency loan of USD 50 million from its London branch.

Rather than utilizing the credit facilities for their sanctioned purposes, the firm allegedly defrauded the lender by diverting and siphoning off the funds through associate entities, causing an estimated wrongful loss of Rs 212.3 crore.





Following the registration of the First Information Report (FIR) under charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating, and provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act, the agency carried out extensive search operations across multiple premises linked to the accused directors.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

During these raids, CBI officials recovered and seized a range of incriminating material, including bank account and property details of the directors, deposit slips, mutual fund portfolio documents, and company ledgers.

Probe agency officials confirmed that further investigation is ongoing to uncover the full extent of the conspiracy, trace the ultimate end-use of the diverted loan proceeds, and establish the specific roles of all involved individuals, including public servants.

World.title: NMC weighs five-year rotation of HoDs after stakeholder feedback
World.content:
(Representative image): The original draft amendment to the Postgraduate Medical Education Regulations, 2023, proposed rotating the HoD post every three years among eligible professors and associate professors, based on seniority. Nearly a year and a half after the draft was published, the proposal remains unresolved.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) is considering a revised proposal to rotate heads of departments (HoDs) in medical colleges every five years, instead of the three-year tenure proposed earlier, following feedback from stakeholders.Under the revised proposal, rotation would be restricted to professors, rather than including both professors and eligible associate professors as envisaged in the draft amendment published in May 2025, M K Ramesh, president of the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB), told TOI.Ramesh said the commission had received substantial feedback on the earlier proposal and that valid points raised by stakeholders would be considered. Suggestions included rotation periods of five or 10 years, as well as doing away with mandatory rotation altogether.The original draft amendment to the Postgraduate Medical Education Regulations, 2023, proposed rotating the HoD post every three years among eligible professors and associate professors, based on seniority. Nearly a year and a half after the draft was published, the proposal remains unresolved.Ramesh said the proposal would need to be taken up afresh and that the revised draft would be moved shortly. Once initiated, the process would be completed within six weeks, he said.He did not confirm whether the NMC would invite stakeholders to comment again on the revised proposal or take a decision based on the feedback already received.The delay had also prompted an RTI application by Dr A N Dattatri, professor and head of the department of pharmacology at Karnataka Medical College and Research Institute, Hubballi, seeking the PGMEBâs detailed note on stakeholder feedback and its views on the proposal. In a reply dated September 16, 2026, the board said the matter was under consideration and declined to disclose the information, citing Section 8(1)(i) of the RTI Act.The proposed change could affect how leadership positions are assigned in medical college departments. The five-year rotation plan remains a proposal and has not yet been formally notified.

World.title: Women entrepreneurs urged to focus on attractive, quality packaging at SARAS Mela
World.content:
Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya visited the National SARAS Mela–2026 in Vijayawada on Saturday.

Interacting with women entrepreneurs from various Self Help Groups (SHGs), the Minister of State learnt about their handicraft products, business activities and experiences in producing and marketing their goods. Emphasising the importance of product presentation, she urged the women entrepreneurs to focus on attractive and quality packaging, noting that improved packaging can enhance product appeal, attract customers and help increase sales.

Addressing the gathering after the interaction, Ms. Bambhaniya highlighted the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi in empowering Lakhpati Didis and enabling rural women to become financially independent and self-reliant. She appreciated the transformation of SHG women from wage earners into entrepreneurs creating livelihood opportunities and generating employment for others.

The Minister expressed confidence that organising the event in Vijayawada would encourage wider participation by States in future editions and create greater opportunities for women-led enterprises across the country. Later, the Minister toured the exhibition stalls, viewed the products showcased by SHG women from different States and encouraged the participating women entrepreneurs.

According to information from the A.P. State Rural Livelihoods Mission, the mela recorded cumulative sales of ₹7.17 crore from October 15 to 23, with 2.77 lakh products sold.

World.title: Only a matter of time before everyone involved in sting operation is exposed, says Priyank Kharge
World.content:
Home Minister Priyank Kharge on Saturday said that everyone involved in the alleged criminal conspiracy behind a sting operation targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah would be exposed, asserting that the investigation was under way and would be completed soon.

Speaking to reporters here, Mr. Kharge said it was a matter of time before everybody is exposed — who did the criminal conspiracy, where it happened, how it happened, who did the sting, why they did it, how it got into someone’s hands after so many years, how it was suddenly uploaded, how it was publicised, and so on. “We will trace it from the source and expose it in a few days,” he added.

He pointed out while some claimed that it dated to 2011, others claim it was recorded in 2023 before emerging on social media in 2026.

Mr. Kharge maintained that the investigation would be conducted transparently, adding that those whose names had emerged during the investigation had been called in, and their statements recorded. “There is no escaping it. The charge sheet must be filed. We have to submit it to the court,” he said, adding that the findings would be made available at the appropriate time

Asked about the alleged involvement of Congress leaders, the Minister alleged that the video pointed to a case of extortion and blackmail, as it was “very evident in the video itself.” “When you know there are faces visible who belong to the party, they cannot deny it. But it is a very clear case of extortion. It’s a very clear case of blackmail. And we are investigating; sooner or later everything will be on record,” he said..

World.title: Schools in Andhra Pradesh to conduct e-waste collection drive on October 28
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh School Education Department will conduct the concluding activities of ‘Special Campaign 6 – E-Waste Collection’ in all government and private schools and junior colleges across the State on October 28 under the Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE programme.

Director of School Education and In-charge State Project Director of Samagra Shiksha A. Thameem Ansariya said on Saturday that the initiative was being implemented in accordance with the Union Ministry of Education’s guidelines to promote environmental awareness and responsible waste management among students.

Schools have been instructed to conduct a special quiz on e-waste management, reuse and safe disposal during the morning assembly on October 28. Headmasters and headmistresses must also submit answers to the questions available on the designated web portal through the prescribed link.

Students will be encouraged to bring unused or damaged electronic items from home, including old devices, cables, chargers and mobile phones, and deposit them in designated black boxes at e-waste collection corners in schools.

The collected material must be sent through the prescribed channel to the Mandal Education Office for collection by authorised recyclers. The department has directed schools to hand over e-waste only to recyclers or refurbishers authorised by the Central Pollution Control Board or the State Pollution Control Board. Handing it over to unauthorised scrap dealers is strictly prohibited.

Officials said authorised recyclers had been identified at the field level and their contact details communicated to the authorities concerned. Schools have also been instructed to follow safety precautions and ensure that students and staff do not dismantle hazardous electronic items such as batteries, CRT monitors, LED bulbs and CFL bulbs.

All government and private schools must upload details of the e-waste collected to the Eco Clubs portal through their respective Eco Club Coordinators by October 27.

Ms. Ansariya urged headmasters, teachers, parents, students and Eco Club Coordinators to participate actively in the campaign. The initiative aims to instil environmental responsibility among students and promote the safe collection, handling and disposal of electronic waste.

World.title: BJP seeks probe into death of mother, baby in Kashmir’s Gurez, flags healthcare gaps
World.content:
The BJP on Saturday (October 24, 2026) targeted the ruling National Conference (NC) over the death of an expecting mother and its failure to post a permanent gynaecologist at the Gurez Valley, a popular tourist destination that remains cut off in winters due to snowfall, in north Kashmir.

“An expecting mother should not have to depend on uncertainty when she needs emergency medical care. No family should have to endure such a devastating loss while questioning whether timely treatment and adequate facilities were available. The allegations surrounding this tragic incident must be investigated impartially, and responsibility must be fixed wherever lapses are established,” said BJP J&K spokesperson Danish Bhat.

On October 14, a 30-year-old Haseena Begum and her unborn baby died due to a lack of maternity care in the Gurez valley. “The tragedy has brought the region’s long-standing healthcare deficiencies into sharp focus. NC MLA Nazir Ahmad Khan Gurezi, who has represented the constituency across four Assembly elections since 2002,” said Mr. Bhat.

Referring to the hunger strike observed by the locals over healthcare, Mr. Bhat said, “Nearly two decades of political representation should have translated into reliable healthcare, functioning emergency services and dignity for the people of Gurez. Instead, residents are now forced to sit on a hunger strike to demand a gynaecologist, a radiologist, a functional operation theatre, a blood bank and even appropriately equipped ambulances. This is not merely a healthcare failure; it raises serious questions about political accountability.”

He said the NC needs to meet the demands of a permanent specialist, a functioning operating theatre, and emergency transport. “Gurez is a remote and strategically important region where difficult terrain and winter conditions make dependable medical infrastructure indispensable. These challenges are well known; they cannot be invoked indefinitely as an excuse for inadequate preparedness,” said Mr. Bhat.

Meanwhile, the BJP demanded a time-bound investigation into the deaths of Begum and her baby, “with the findings made public and appropriate action taken in accordance with the law”.

“People of Gurez are not asking for favours. They are demanding basic healthcare, accountability and the assurance that their lives matter. Their hunger strike must not be reduced to another headline that disappears after a few days,” said the BJP spokesman.

World.title: Siddaramaiah ‘sting operation’: Delhi-based man arrested and released on bail
World.content:
Investigation into the alleged sting operation targeting former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has intensified with the first arrest made on Saturday. The Central Crime Branch (CCB) arrested Delhi-based Ritesh Pandey in connection with uploading the video on social media.

Pandey was instructed to upload the footage by a person associated with the social media team of a regional political party, according to the police. He was brought to Bengaluru on Saturday for questioning, and the phone used to upload the video was seized.

The probe has reportedly revealed that Pandey used a second-hand SIM card and an e-SIM-enabled device to download the video from a pendrive and upload it on social media.

The CCB is examining the seized phone, SIM-related details, and the digital trail to establish how the footage was transferred and circulated.

Who handed over pendrive?

Investigators are now trying to identify the person who handed over the pendrive to Pandey and also establish the role of others. Officials have also summoned several people for questioning based on information reportedly provided by Pandey.

Pandey was produced before a Metropolitan Magistrate Court and granted bail, subject to the condition that he cooperates with the investigation. The offence is punishable with imprisonment of less than seven years, according to the information available in connection with the case.

Earlier, the CCB questioned Rakesh Shetty, head of a private Kannada news channel.

The CCB is continuing its investigation to establish the source of the video, the circumstances under which it was recorded and circulated, and whether other individuals were involved in the alleged sting operation.

Investigators are also examining whether the video was prepared and disseminated as part of a coordinated effort and are seeking to establish the identities and roles of those involved, officials said.

World.title: 14-year-old killed in road accident at Kommadi in Visakhapatnam
World.content:
A 14-year-old boy died after a container lorry rammed into an auto-rickshaw at the Kommadi junction on NH-16 in the early hours of Saturday (October 24, 2026). The deceased has been identified as B. Dhanush.

According to the police, the accident occurred around 12:50 a.m. Dhanush was travelling with his friends toward Kommadi when the incident took place. The collision occurred as the auto-rickshaw was negotiating a right turn toward the service road at the junction. A container lorry, allegedly driven in a rash and negligent manner, crashed into the three-wheeler. The lorry driver allegedly fled the scene.

Dhanush, who sustained serious injuries, was initially shifted to a private hospital and later moved to King George Hospital (KGH) for further treatment. However, he succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment. The autorickshaw driver was also seriously injured in the accident.

According to the India Meteorological Department’s (IMD) Bhubaneswar Met Centre, a low-pressure area over east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal persisted over the same region at 8.30 a.m. on Friday (October 23, 2026).
